G2264.outline_usage: Herod = " heroic" , the name of a royal family that flourished among the Jews in the times of Christ and the Apostles. Herod the Great was the son of Antipater of Idumaea. Appointed king of Judaea B.C. 40 by the Roman Senate at the suggestion of Antony and with the consent of Octavian, he at length overcame the great opposition which the country made to him and took possession of the kingdom B.C. 37  and after the battle of Actium, he was confirmed by Octavian, whose favour he ever enjoyed. He was brave and skilled in war, learned and sagacious  but also extremely suspicious and cruel. Hence he destroyed the entire royal family of Hasmonaeans, put to death many of the Jews that opposed his government, and proceeded to kill even his dearly beloved wife Mariamne of the Hasmonaean line and his two sons she had borne him. By these acts of bloodshed, and especially by his love and imitation of Roman customs and institutions and by the burdensome taxes imposed upon his subjects, he so alienated the Jews that he was unable to regain their favour by his splendid restoration of the temple and other acts of munificence. He died in the 70th year of his age, the 37th year of his reign, the 4th before the Dionysian era. In his closing years John the Baptist and Christ were born  Matthew narrates that he commanded all the male children under two years old in Bethlehem to be slain., Herod surnamed " Antipas" , was the son of Herod the Great and Malthace, a Samaritan woman. After the death of his father he was appointed by the Romans tetrarch of Galilee and Peraea. His first wife was the daughter of Aretas, king of Arabia  but he subsequently repudiated her and took to himself Herodias, the wife of his brother Herod Philip  and in consequence Aretas, his father-in-law, made war against him and conquered him. He cast John the Baptist into prison because John had rebuked him for this unlawful connection  and afterwards, at the instigation of Herodias, he ordered him to be beheaded. Induced by her, too, he went to Rome to obtain from the emperor the title of king. But in consequence of the accusations brought against him by Herod Agrippa I, Caligula banished him (A.D. 39) to Lugdunum in Gaul, where he seems to have died. He was light minded, sensual and vicious., Herod Agrippa I was the son of Aristobulus and Berenice, and grandson of Herod the Great. After various changes in fortune, he gained the favour of Caligula and Claudius to such a degree that he gradually obtained the government of all of Palestine, with the title of king. He died at Caesarea, A.D. 44, at the age of 54, in the seventh [or the 4th, reckoning from the extension of his dominions by Claudius] year of his reign, just after having ordered James the apostle, son of Zebedee, to be slain, and Peter to be cast into prison Acts 12 21, (Herod) Agrippa II, son of Herod Agrippa I. When his father died he was a youth of seventeen. In A.D. 48 he received from Claudius Caesar the government of Chalcis, with the right of appointing the Jewish high priests, together with the care and oversight of the temple at Jerusalem. Four years later Claudius took from him Chalcis and gave him instead a larger domain, of Batanaea, Trachonitis, and Gaulanitis, with the title of king. To those reigns Nero, in A.D. 53, added Tiberias and Taricheae and Peraean Julias, with fourteen neighbouring villages. He is mentioned in Acts 25 and 26. In the Jewish war, although he strove in vain to restrain the fury of the seditious and bellicose populace, he did not desert to the Roman side. After the fall of Jerusalem, he was vested with praetorian rank and kept the kingdom entire until his death, which took place in the third year of the emperor Trajan, [the 73rd year of his life, and the 52nd of his reign] He was the last representative of the Herodian dynasty.

G5076.outline_usage: a tetrarch, a governor of the fourth part of a region. Thus Strabo states that Galactia was formerly divided into three parts, each one of which was distributed into four smaller subdivisions each of which was governed by a tetrarch. Strabo relates that Thessaly, before the time of Philip of Macedon, had been divided into four tetrarchies, each having its own tetrarch., the governor of a third part or half a country, or even a ruler of an entire country or district provided it were of comparatively narrow limits  a petty prince. Thus Antony made Herod (afterwards king) and Phasael, sons of Antipater, tetrarchs of Palestine. After the death of Herod the Great, his sons, Achelaus styled an ethnarch but Antipas and Philip with the title of tetrarchs, divided and governed the kingdom left by their father.

G5330.root_word: H6567 | פָּרַשׁ |  shew, scatter, declare, distinctly, sting
G5330.outline_usage: A sect that seems to have started after the Jewish exile. In addition to OT books the Pharisees recognised in oral tradition a standard of belief and life. They sought for distinction and praise by outward observance of external rites and by outward forms of piety, and such as ceremonial washings, fastings, prayers, and alms giving  and, comparatively negligent of genuine piety, they prided themselves on their fancied good works. They held strenuously to a belief in the existence of good and evil angels, and to the expectation of a Messiah  and they cherished the hope that the dead, after a preliminary experience either of reward or of penalty in Hades, would be recalled to life by him, and be requited each according to his individual deeds. In opposition to the usurped dominion of the Herods and the rule of the Romans, they stoutly upheld the theocracy and their country's cause, and possessed great influence with the common people. According to Josephus they numbered more than 6000. They were bitter enemies of Jesus and his cause  and were in turn severely rebuked by him for their avarice, ambition, hollow reliance on outward works, and affection of piety in order to gain popularity.

G405.derivation: from a derivative of a compound of 435 and 4228

G407.strongs_def: ἀνδρίζω [in LXX for חָזַק אָמַץ (Jos.1:6 ff., 1Ch.22:19, al.; in 2Ki.10:12, Psa.27:14 31:24 combined with κρατιοῦσθαι, as in 1Co, l.with) ;] to make a man of. Mid., to play the man (cf. MM, VGT, see word): 1Co.16:13.† (AS)

G409.strongs_def: ἀνδρο-φόνος, -ου, ὁ [in LXX: 2Ma.9:28 * ;] a man-slayer: 1Ti.1:9 (cf. φονεύς, and see MM, VGT, see word).† (AS)

G411.strongs_def: ἀν-εκδιήγητος, -ον (ἀ-, ἐκδιηγέομαι) inexpressible: 2Co.9:15 (MM, VGT, see word).† (AS)
G411.derivation: from 1 (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of 1555

G412.derivation: from 1 (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of 1583

G415.strongs_def: ἀν-ελεήμων, -ον (-ἀ, ἐλεήμων), [in LXX for אַכְזָר ;] without mercy: Rom.1:13.† (AS)

G420.strongs_def: ἀνεξί-κακος, -ον (fut., ἀνέξομαι, κακός) patiently forbearing (cf. ἀνεξικακία, Wis.2:19; and see MM, VGT, see word): 2Ti.2:24.† (AS)

G422.strongs_def: ἀν-επ-αίσχυντος, -ον (ἐπαισχύνομαι) not to be put to shame: 2Ti.2:15.† (AS)
G422.derivation: from 1 (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of a compound of 1909 and 153

G423.strongs_def: ἀν-επί-λημπτος (Rec. -λμπτος; Bl., § 6, 8), -ον (ἀ- ἐπιλαμβάνω) without reproach: 1Ti.3:2 5:7 6:14.† SYN.: ἀμεμπτος, ἀνέγκλητος. It is stronger than these, for it implies not only that the man is of good report, but that he is deservedly so (cf. MM, VGT, see word). (AS)
G423.derivation: from 1 (as a negative particle) and a derivative of 1949

G434.strongs_def: ἀν-ήμερος, -ον (ἀ-, ἥμερο ), not tame, savage (MM, VGT, see word): 2Ti.3:3.† (AS)
G434.derivation: from 1 (as a negative particle) and hemeros (lame)

G462.strongs_def: ἀν-όσιος, -ον (ἀ- neg., ὅσιος), [in LXX: Eze.22:9 (זִמָּה, Wis.12:4, 2Ma.7:34 2Mac 8:32, 3Ma.2:2 3Mac 5:7, 4Ma.12:11 * ;] unholy, profane (Cremer, 464): 1Ti.1:9, 2Ti.3:2 (MM, VGT, see word).† (AS)

G475.strongs_def: ἀντι-δια-τίθημι in mid, to place oneself in opposition, oppose: 2Ti.2:25 (EV; but see Field, Notes, 215 f.; cf. MM, VGT, see word) (AS)

G484.strongs_def: ἀντί-λημψις (Rec. -ληψις; see MM, VGT see word; M, Pr., 56), -εως, ἡ (ἀντιλαμβάνομαι) [in LXX for עֹז, זְרוֹעַ, etc., frequently in Psa.2:1-12,3Mac.; frequently also in π. in petitions to the Ptolemies in sense of βοήθεια (see Deiss., LAE, 107; BS, 92, 223) ;] __1. cl. a laying hold of, an exchange. __2. Hellenistic (LXX, π.) help: pl. of ministrations of deacons; 1Co.12:28 (DB, ii, 347 f.; Cremer, 386).† (AS)

G486.strongs_def: to rail at or abuse in turn , (New Testament); Mid., with accusative rei, (Lucian) (ML)

G487.strongs_def: ἀντί-λυτρον, -ου, τό [in Al.: Psa.49:9 * ;] a ransom: 1Ti.2:6 (see CGT, in l; and cf. λύτρον).† (AS)

G491.strongs_def: Ἀντιοχεύς, -έως, ὁ a citizen of Antioch, an Antiochian: Act.6:5.† (AS)

G492.strongs_def: ἀντι-παρ-έρχομαι [in LXX: Wis.16:10 * ;] to pass by opposite to: Luk.10:31-32 (MM, VGT, see word).† (AS)

G494.strongs_def: Ἀντιπατρίς, -ίδος, ἡ Antipatris, bet. Joppa and Caesarea: Act.23:31.† (AS)

G500.strongs_def: άντι-χριατος, -ον, ό Antichrist, "one who assuming the guise of Christ opposes Christ" (Westc., Epp. Jo., 70): 1Jn.2:18 Jn 2:22 Jn 4:3, 1Jn.1:7 pl. 1Jn.2:18 (cf. ψευδόχριστος, and see MM, VGT, see word).† (AS)

G519.strongs_def: ἀπ-άγχω (ἄγχω, to press, strangle), [in LXX: 2Ki.17:23 (חָנַק), Tob.3:10 * ;] to strangle; mid., to hang oneself (or, to choke; see M, Pr., 155): Mat.27:5.† (AS)
G519.derivation: from 575 and agcho (to choke akin to the base of 43)

G521.strongs_def: ἀ-παίδευτος, -ον (παιδεύω), [in LXX for כְּסִיל, etc., chiefly in Wis. lit. ;] uninstructed, ignorant: 2Ti.2:23.† (AS)
G521.derivation: from 1 (as a negative particle) and a derivative of 3811

G532.derivation: from 1 (as a negative particle) and a derivative of 3903

G535.strongs_def: ἀπαρτισμός, -οῦ, ὁ (ἀπαρτίζω, to finish), completion: Luk.14:28 (cf. MM, VGT, see word).† (AS)

G550.strongs_def: ἀπ-εῖπον, 2 aor. without present in use [in LXX for מָאַס, אָמַר, etc. ;] __1. to tell out. __2. to forbid (3Ki.11:2). __3. to renounce: 1 aor. mid. (WH, App., 164; MM, VGT, see word), 2Co.4:2.† (AS)
G550.derivation: reflexive past of a compound of 575 and 2036

G558.strongs_def: ἀπ-ελεύθερος, -ου, ὁ, ἡ a freedman: τ. κυρίου (MM, see word), 1Co.7:22.† (AS)

G562.strongs_def: ἀπέραντος, -ον (περαίνω, to complete, finish) [in LXX: Job.36:26 (חֵקֶר אַיִן) 3Mac.20 * ;] endless, interminable: 1Ti.1:4.† (AS)
G562.derivation: from 1 (as a negative particle) and a secondary derivative of 4008

G563.strongs_def: ἀπεριστπάστως adv. (περισπάω the adj. occurs in Wis.16:11 Sir.41:1); without distraction: 1Co.7:35.† (AS)
G563.derivation: from a compound of 1 (as a negative participle) and a presumed derivative of 4049

G579.strongs_def: ἀπό-βλητος, -ον (ἀποβάλλω), [in Aq.: Lev.7:18, al.; Sm.: Hos.9:3 (טָמֵא) ;] to be thrown away, rejected: 1Ti.4:4 (Hom., Plut.).† (AS)

G581.strongs_def: ἀπο-γίνομαι (cl. -γίγν-) [in LXX: Da TH Dan.2:1 * ;] __1. to be away, removed from. __2. to depart life, to die (MM, see word): τ. ἀμαρτίαις, i.e. with ref. to sins, 1Pe.2:24 (Cremer, 149, 668).† (AS)
G581.derivation: past participle of a compound of 575 and 1096

G585.strongs_def: ἀπό-δειξις, -εως, ἡ (ἀποδείκνυμι) [in LXX: 3Ma.4:20, 4Ma.3:19 4Mac 13:10 * ;] __1. a showing off. __2. As used by Gk. philosophers, demonstration, certain proof: 1Co.2:4 (see ICC, in l; MM, see word; Lft., Notes, 173).† (AS)

G594.strongs_def: ἀπο-δοχή, -ῆς, ἡ (ἀποδέχομαι), acceptance, approbation (Field, Notes, 203): 1Ti.1:15 4:9 (Cremer, 686; MM, see word).† (AS)

G597.strongs_def: ἀπο-θησαυρίζω [in LXX: Sir.3:4 * ;] to treasure up, store away: 1Ti.6:19.† (AS)

G610.strongs_def: ἀπό-κριμα, -τος, τό (ἀποκρίνω); __1. prop., a judicial sentence: 2Co.1:9, R, mg. __2. an answer (see Thayer, see word): 2Co.1:9, R, txt. (In FlJ, Ant., xiv, 10, 6, of a rescript of the Senate; in Inscr. of an official decision, Deiss., BS, 257; a reply to a deputation, MM, see word: cf. also Cremer, 3'75).† (AS)
G610.derivation: from 611 (in its original sense of judging)

G623.strongs_def: Ἀπολλύων, -οντος, ὁ (present ptcp. of ἀπολλύω), Apollyon, i.e. the Destroyer: Rev.9:11 (cf. Ἀβάδδων). (Cremer, 453; DB, i, 125, 172.) † (AS)

G632.strongs_def: ἀπο-νέμω (νέμω, to distribute), [in LXX: Deu.4:19 (חָלַק), 3Ma.1:7 3Mac 3:16 * ;] to assign, apportion: 1Pe.3:7. (In π. of a Prefect who renders to all their dues; see MM, see word)† (AS)

G642.strongs_def: ἀπ-ορφανίζω (ἀπό, ὀρφανός), to be bereaved (prop., of a parent, Lft., Notes, 36); metaphorically, 1Th.2:17 (where Field thinks it = χωρισθέντες, Notes, 199).† (AS)

G665.strongs_def: ἀπο-τρέπω [in LXX: Sir.20:29 48:18, 3Ma.1:23, 4Ma.1:33 4Mac 16:12 * ;] to turn away; mid., to turn oneself away from: with accusative, 2Ti.3:5.† (AS)

G668.strongs_def: ἀπο-φεύγω [in LXX: Sir.22:22 * ;] to flee from, escape: with accusative, 2Pe.2:18 2:20; with genitive, 2Pe.1:4.† (AS)

G676.strongs_def: ἀ-πρόσ-ιτος, -ον (πρόσειμι, to go to), unapproachable: φῶς, 1Ti.6:16.† (AS)
G676.derivation: from 1 (as a negative particle) and a derivative of a comparative of 4314 and eimi (to go)

G678.strongs_def: ἀπροσωπολήμπτως (Rec. -λήπτως, cl.), adv. (α- neg., προσωπολήμπτης), without respect of persons, impartially: 1Pe.1:17.† (AS)
G678.derivation: from a compound of 1 (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of a presumed compound of 4383 and 2983 [cf 4381]

G691.strongs_def: ἀργέω, -ῶ (ἀργός), [in LXX: Est.4:24, Ecc.12:3 (בָּטֵל), I Est.2:30, Sir.33:27), 2Ma.5:25 * ;] to be idle; τὸ κρίμα . . . ἀ., lingers (cf. MGr. ἀργά, late: MM, see word): 2Pe.2:3.† (AS)

G702.strongs_def: Ἀρέτας (WH, Ἀρ.; Intr., 313), -α, ὁ, Aretas, an Arabian king: 2Co.11:32 (Deiss., BS, 183 f., thinks the proper spelling Ἀρέθας was changed, as Schürer suggests, "by desire to Hellenise a barbaric name by assimilation to ἀρετή").† (AS)

G711.strongs_def: Ἀριστόβουλος, -ου, ὁ (ἄριστος, βουλή, i.e. best-counselling) Aristobulus, a Christian: Rom.16:10.† (AS)

G717.strongs_def: Ἁρμαγεδών (WH, Ἃρ Μαγεδών; Rec. Ἀρμαγεδδών, prop. = הַר מְגִדּוֹן), cf. LXX, Μαγεδών, 2Ch.35:22, Μαγεδώ, Jdg.1:27; Har-Magedon (AV, Armageddon): Rev.16:16 (see Swete, in l, but also Thayer, see word).† Ἅρ, indecl., Rev.16:16, see, Ἁρμαγεδών Μαγεδών, Magedon: Rev.16:16 (WH, Ἅρ M. for Ἁρμαγεδών, which see).† (AS)

G718.strongs_def: ἁρμόζω (ἁρμός), [in LXX for אמן, etc. ;] __1. to fit, join. __2. of marriage, to betroth. Mid., __(a) to join to oneself, marry, take to wife; (b) to give in marriage: 2Co.11:2 (for this there is no direct parallel. But see M, Pr., 160; MM, see word).† (AS)

G731.strongs_def: ἄρρητος, -ον (ἀ- neg., ῥητός, ῥέω), [in Sm.: Lev.18:23 * ;] __1. unspoken (Hom., al.). __2. unspeakable (Hat., al.; frequently in Inscr.; MM, see word): 2Co.12:4.† (AS)
G731.derivation: from 1 (as a negative particle) and the same as 4490

G750.strongs_def: ἀρχι-ποίμην, -ενος, ὁ [in Sm.: 4Ki.3:4 * ;] found on an Egyptian mummy label (Deiss., LAE, 97 ff.; cf. MM, see word); used by modem Greeks of tribal chiefs; chief shepherd. of Christ, 1Pe.5:4.† (AS)

G753.strongs_def: ἀρχι-τέκτων, -ονος, ὁ (τέκτων), [in LXX: Isa.3:3 (חָרָשׁ) Sir.38:27. 2Ma.2:29 * ;] a master-builder, architect: 1Co.3:10 (in π. of building contractors, MM, see word).† (AS)

G790.strongs_def: ἀστατέω, -ῶ (ἄστατος, unstable), [in Aq.: Isa.58:7 (LXX, ἄστεγος)* ;] to be unsettled, be homeless, lead a vagabond life (Cremer, 738 MM, see word): 1Co.4:11 † (AS)
G790.derivation: from 1 (as a negative particle) and a derivative of 2476

G793.derivation: from 1 (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of 4741

G795.strongs_def: ἀστοχέω, -ῶ (στόχος, a mark), [in LXX: Sir.7:19 8:9 * ;] to miss the mark, fail: with genitive, 1Ti.1:6 (so in π., MM, see word); before περί, 1Ti.6:21, 2Ti.2:18.† (AS)
G795.derivation: from a compound of 1 (as a negative particle) and stoichos (an aim)

G807.strongs_def: ἀσχημονέω, -ῶ (ἀσχήμαων), [in LXX: Eze.16:7, 22 16:39 23:29 (עֶרְיָה); Deu.25:3 (קָלָה ni.)* ;] to act unbecomingly, behave dishonourably: 1Co.13:5; before ἐπί, ib. 1Co.7:36 (MM, see word).† (AS)

G809.strongs_def: ἀσχήμων, -ον (ἀ- neg., σχῆμα) [in LXX: Gen.34:7 (נְבָלָה), Deu.24:1 (עֶרְוָה), Wis.2:20, Da TH Sus 1:63, 2Ma.9:2 * ;] __1. shapeless. __2. uncomely, unseemly: 1Co.12:23.† (AS)
G809.derivation: from 1 (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of 2192 (in the sense of its congener 4976)

G812.strongs_def: ἀτακτέω -ῶ (ἄτακτος), primarily, of soldiers marching, to be out of order, to quit the ranks; hence, metaphorically, to be remiss, fail in the performance of duty (in π., of truancy on the part of an apprentice): 2Th.3:7 (on ἀ. and its cognates, see M, Th., 152 ff.; MM, s.vv.).† (AS)

G813.strongs_def: ἀ-τακτος, -ον (τάσσω), [in LXX: 3Ma.1:19 * ;] out of order, out of place (Lat. inordinatus), frequently of soldiers not keeping the ranks, or an army in disarray (cf. 3Ma.1:19); hence, metaphorically, irregular, disorderly (see previous word): 1Th.5:14.† (AS)
G813.derivation: from 1 (as a negative particle) and a derivative of 5021

G821.strongs_def: ἀτιμόω, -ῶ (ἄτιμος), [in LXX chiefly for בָּזָה ;] = ἀτιμάζω, to dishonour, treat with indignity: Mrk.12:4, Rec.† (AS)

G823.strongs_def: ἄ-τομος, -ον (τέμνω), [in Sm.: Isa.54:8 (MM, see word) * ;] indivisible; of time, ἄτομον, a moment: ἐν ἄ., 1Co.15:52.† (AS)
G823.derivation: from 1 (as a negative particle) and the base of 5114

G825.strongs_def: Ἀτταλία (Rec. -άλεια), -υς, ἡ Attalia, a city of Pamphylia: Act.14:25.† (AS)

G826.strongs_def: αὐγάζω (αὐγή), [in LXX: Lev.13:24-28, 38 14:56 (בֹּהֶרֶת) Lev.13:39 (כֵּהֶה)* ;] __1. Trans. (cl.), to irradiate. __2. Intrans. __(a) (poët.), to see clearly (so perh. 2 Co, l.with; MM, see word) __(b) as in LXX, to shine forth: 2Co.4:4 (cf. δι-, κατ-αυγάζω).† (AS)

G830.strongs_def: αὐθαίρετος, -ον (αὐτός, αἱρέομαι), [in Sm.: Exo.35:5, 22 * ;] __1. self-chosen. __2. of one's own accord: 2Co.8:3 8:17.† (AS)

G831.strongs_def: αὐθεντέω, -ῶ (αὐθέντης, i.e. αὐτο- ἕντης, one who acts on his own authority, in π., an autocrat; cf. Wis.12:6; cf. -ία, 3Ma.2:29; -ικος is frequently in vernacular, MM, see word) to govern, exercise authority over: 1Ti.2:12.† (AS)
G831.derivation: from a compound of 846 and an obsolete hentes (a worker)

G836.strongs_def: αὐλός, -οῦ, ὁ (ἄω, to blow), [in LXX chiefly for חָלִיל ;] a pipe: 1Co.14:7.† (AS)

G841.strongs_def: αὐτάρκεια, -ας, ἡ (αὐτάρκης, which see), __(a) sufficiency (MM, see word): in subjective sense (see Milligan, NTD, 57), 2Co.9:8; __(b) contentment: 1Ti.6:6.† (AS)

G842.strongs_def: αὐτάρκης, -ες (αὐτός, ἀρκέω), [in LXX: Pro.30:8 (חֹק), Sir.5:1 11:24 31:28 40:18, 4Ma.9:9 * ;] as in cl., in philosophical sense, self-­sufficient, independent; subjectively, contented: Php.4:11 (in non-lit. π., the word means simply enough, sufficient; MM, see word).† (AS)

G843.strongs_def: αὐτο-κατά-κριτος, -ον (αὐτός, κατακρίνω), self-condemned: Tit.3:11 (Eccl., Cremer, 377; MM, see word).† (AS)

G850.strongs_def: αὐχμηρός, -ά, -όν (αὐχμός, drought); __1. dry __2. squalid, dismal: 2Pe.1:19 (MM, see word).† (AS)
G850.derivation: from auchmos [probably from a base akin to that of 109] (dust, as dried by wind)

G854.strongs_def: ἀφανισμός, -οῦ, ὁ (ἀφανίζω), [in LXX chiefly for שַׁמָּה, שְׁמָמָה ;] vanishing: Heb.8:13.† (AS)

G865.strongs_def: ἀ-φιλ-άγαθος, -ον without love of good: 2Ti.3:3 (not elsewhere in Gk. lit., but see MM, see word).† (AS)

G877.strongs_def: ἀφροσύνη, -ης, ἡ (ἄφρων), [in LXX for אִוֶּלֶת, נְבָלָה, etc. ;] foolishness: Mrk.7:22, 2Co.11:1 11:17 11:21.† (AS)

G896.strongs_def: Βάαλ (Rec. βαάλ), ὁ, ἡ, indecl. (Heb. בַּעַל, lord), Baal: Rom.11:4 (LXX). The fem. art. here agrees with the usage of LXX, where, following a similar Hebrew practice (בֹּשֶׁת for בַּעַל), αἰσχύνη appears to have been substituted in reading for the written Βάαλ (cf. 3Ki.18:19), and to account for the frequently use of the fem. art. bef. Β. The usage, however, is not general, and in the passage cited in Ro (3Ki.19:18), LXX reads τῷ Β. † (AS)

G898.strongs_def: βαθμός, -οῦ, ὁ, Ion. form of βασμός (βαίνω, to step), [in LXX 1Ki.5:5 (מִפְתָּן), 4Ki.20:9, 10 11 (מַעֲלָה), Sir.6:36 * ;] a step (4Ki, l.with, of degrees of a dial); metaphorically, a degree, standing: 1Ti.3:13.† (AS)

G919.strongs_def: Βαρι-ησοῦς, -οῦ, ὁ (Aram. בַּר־יֵשׁוּעַ, son of Joshua), Bar-Jesus: Act.13:6 (see: Ἐλύμας).† (AS)

G933.strongs_def: βασίλειον, -ου, τό (βασίλειος, which see), [in LXX for הֵיכָל ( Nam.2:6, Dan.6:18*), מַמְלָכָה ( 3Ki.3:1 14:8, 4Ki.15:19*), etc. ;] __1. a capital city. __2. Freq. in pl., τὰ β., a palace: Luk.7:25. † (AS)

G934.strongs_def: βασίλειος, -ον (also -α, -ον; βασιλεύς), [in LXX; Exo.19:6, Deu.3:10 (מַמְלָכָה), Exo.23:22, Wis.18:15, 3Ma.3:28, 4Ma.3:8 * ;] royal: 1Pe.2:9 (LXX) (see Hort, in l.).† royal, regal, kingly;, metaphorically possessed of high prerogatives and distinction, 1Pet. 2:9; (AS)

G955.strongs_def: Βελίαλ, ὁ, indecl. (Heb. בְּלִיַּעַל, worthlessness, but see DB, i, 268), Belial, a name of Satan: 2Co.6:15, Rec. See next word.† Βελιάρ, ὁ, indecl. (another form of previous word, "due to harsh Syriac pronunciation," or else Heb. בֵּל יַעַר, lord of the forest), Beliar, a name of Satan: 2Co.6:15 (see DB, i, 269).† (AS)

G957.strongs_def: βελτίων, -ον (genitive -ονος), comp. of ἀγαθός, [in LXX chiefly for טוֹב ;] neut. as adv., better, very well: 2Ti.1:18 (also Act.10:28 D). On elative use in these passages, see M, Pr., 78, 236.† (AS)
G957.derivation: a compound of a derivative of 906 (used for the comparative of 18)

G977.strongs_def: βιβρώσκω, poët, and late prose, [in LXX for אכל ;] to eat: Jhn.6:13.† (AS)
G977.derivation: a reduplicated and prolonged form of an obsolete primary word [perhaps causative of 1006]

G980.strongs_def: βιόω, -ῶ (βίος), [in LXX: Pro.7:2 9:6 (חיה), Job.29:18, Wis.4:4 א 1, 12:23, Sir.40:28, 4Ma.5:22 17:18 * ;] to spend life, to live: τ. χρόνον βιῶσαι (cl., more frequently 2 aor., -ναι), 1Pe.4:2 (cf. Jb, l.with).† SYN.: ζάω (which see). (AS)

G990.strongs_def: βλέμμα, -τος, τό (βλέπω), a look, a glance: βλέμματι καὶ ἀκοῇ, 2Pe.2:8, sight and hearing, a sense not found for β. in Gk. lit., but perh. recognized in the vernacular (ICC, in l.)† (AS)

G1002.strongs_def: βολίς, -ίδος, ἡ (βάλλω), [in LXX for חֵץ, יָרָה, etc. ;] a dart, javelin: Heb.12:20, Rec. (LXX).† (AS)

G1004.strongs_def: βόρβορος, -ου, ὁ, [in LXX: Je 45(38):6 (טִיט)* ;] mud, filth: 2Pe.2:22.† (AS)

G1007.strongs_def: Βοσόρ see Βεώρ - ὁ, indecl. (Heb. בְּעוֹר), Beor, father of Balaam: 2Pe.2:15 (Rec. Βοσόρ).† (AS)

G1019.strongs_def: βραδύνω (βραδύς), [in LXX: Gen.43:10 (מההּ hith.), Deu.7:10, Isa.46:13 (אחר pi.), Si 32 (35):18 * ;] __1. trans., to retard (Soph., Is, l.with). __2. More frequently intrans., to be slow, to tarry: 1Ti.3:15, 2Pe.3:9.† (AS)

G1022.strongs_def: 1. slowness , (Iliad by Homer), attic 2. of the mind, (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G1029.strongs_def: βρόχος, -ου, ὁ, [in LXX: Pro.6:5 (יָד) 7:21 (חֵלֶק) 22:25 (מוֹקֵשׁ), 3Ma.4:8 * ;] a noose, a slip-knot, a halter: metaphorically, a restraint (not, as AV, R, txt., a snare): 1Co.7:35.† (AS)

G1034.strongs_def: βρώσιμος, -ον (βρῶσις), [in LXX: Lev.19:23, Neh.9:25, Eze.47:12 (מַאֲכָל)* ;] eatable: Luk.24:41.† (AS)

G1036.strongs_def: βυθίζω (βυθός), [in LXX: 2Ma.12:4 * ;] trans., to cause to sink, to sink: metaphorically, εἰς ὄλεθρον, 1Ti.6:9; pass., to sink, intrans.: Luk.5:7.† (AS)

G1037.strongs_def: βυθός, -οῦ, ὁ, [in LXX: Exo.15:5, Neh.9:11 (מְצוֹלָה), Psa.67 (68):22 68 (69):2, 15 106 (107):24 (מְצוּלָה)* ;] __1. the bottom. __2. the depth of the sea, the deep sea: 2Co.11:25.† (AS)

G1042.strongs_def: Γαββαθα (Rec. -θᾶ), ἡ, indecl., Gabbatha, the Greek transliteration of an uncertain Aramaic word (DB, see word; Dalman, Words, 7), used as the equivalent of λιθόστρωτον, stone pavement: Jhn.19:13.† (AS)

G1044.strongs_def: γάγγραινα, -ης, ἡ, a gangrene, an eating sore, which leads to mortification: 2Ti.2:17.† (AS)

G1053.strongs_def: Γαλατία, -ας, ἡ, Galatia; __1. a gentilic region in Asia Minor, settled by Gauls (iii/B.C). __2. A Roman Province which included this region (DB, ii, 85ff.): 1Co.16:1, Gal.1:2, 2Ti.4:10 (T, Tr., mg., Γαλλίαν), 1Pe.1:1.† (AS)

G1055.strongs_def: γαλήνη, -ης, ἡ, a calm: Mat.8:26, Mrk.4:39, Luk.8:24.† (AS)

G1079.strongs_def: γενετή, -ῆς, ἡ = γενεή, Ion. for γενεά, [in LXX: Lev.25:47 (עֵקֶר מִשְׁפָּחָו), Est.4:17 * ;] birth: ἐκ γ., Jhn.9:1.† (AS)
G1079.derivation: from a presumed derivative of the base of 1074

G1091.strongs_def: γεώργιον, -ου, τό (γεωργός), [in LXX, frequently in Pr., for שָׂדֶה, etc. ;] __1. a field (Pro.24:5, 30, Strabo). __2. cultivation, husbandry, tillage (Pro.6:7 9:12, Jer.28:23, Sir.27:6): 1Co.3:9.† (AS)

G1098.strongs_def: γλεῦκος (-εος), -ους, τό, [in LXX for יַיִן, Job.32:19 * ;] must, sweet new wine (Arist.): Act.2:13.† (AS)

G1114.strongs_def: γόης, -ητος, ὁ (γοάω, to wail), __1. a wailer. __2. a wizard. __3. an impostor (cf. γοητεία, trickery, 2Ma.12:24): 2Ti.3:13.† (AS)

G1126.strongs_def: γραώδης, -ες (γραῦς, an old woman, εἶδος), anile, old-womanish: 1Ti.4:7.† (AS)

G1130.strongs_def: γυμνιτεύω (Rec. γυμνητ-, V. Tdf ., Pr., 81), to be naked or scantily clad: 1Co.4:11 (cf. ἐν ψύχει κ. γυμνότητι), 2Co.11:27; γυμνοί, Jas.2:15. In κοινή writers, γ. also means to go light-armed.† (AS)

G1133.strongs_def: γυναικάριον, -ου, τό (diminutive of γυνή), a little woman; contemptuously, a silly woman (EV): 2Ti.3:6.† (AS)

G1134.strongs_def: γυναικεῖος, -α, -ον (γυνή), [in LXX chiefly for אִשָּׁה ;] female: 1Pe.3:7.† (AS)

G1141.strongs_def: δαιμονιώδης, -ες (δαιμόνιον, εἶδος), [in Sm.: Ps 90(91):6 * ;] demon-like: Jas.3:15 (Cremer, 171).† (AS)

G1145.strongs_def: δακρύω [in LXX for בָּכָה, etc. ;] to weep, shed tears: Jhn.11:35.† SYN.: κλαίω, of audible weeping, to cry; ὀδύρομαι, of grief expressed verbally, to lament; θρηνέω, of formal lamentation, to sing a dirge; ἀλαλάζω, to wail in Oriental fashion; στενάζω, of grief expressed by inarticulate sounds, to groan. (AS)

G1148.strongs_def: Δαλμανουθά, ἡ indecl., Dalmanutha, an unidentified place near the Sea of Galilee: Mrk.8:10 (cf. Μαγαδάν).† (AS)

G1149.strongs_def: Δαλματία (L, Δελ-), -ας, ἡ Dalmatia, a part of Illyria on E. coast of the Adriatic: 2Ti.4:10.† (AS)

G1156.strongs_def: δάνιον, -ου, τό (late form of δάνειον, Rec.; see: δανίζω), [in LXX: Deu.24:11 (נָשָׁה) 15:8, 10 (עָבַט hi.), 4Ma.2:8 * ;] a loan: Mat.18:27.† (AS)

G1167.strongs_def: δειλία, -ας, ἡ (δειλός), [in LXX for אֵימָה, מְחִתָּה, etc. ;] cowardice, timidity (never in good sense): 2Ti.1:7.† SYN.: φόβος, fear, in general, good or bad; εὐλάβεια (which see), apprehension generally, but chiefly pious fear, "that careful and watchful reverence which pays regard to every circumstance in that with which it has to deal" (cf. Tr., Syn., § x).† (AS)

G1168.strongs_def: δειλιάω, -ῶ (δειλία), [in LXX for חתת ni., פּחד, etc. ;] = the more frequently ἀποδ-, to be cowardly, timid, fearful: Jhn.14:27.† (AS)

G1174.strongs_def: δεισι-δαίμων, -ον (δείδω, to fear; δαίμων, deity) reverent to the deity, religious; compar. -μονεστέρους (AV, too superstitious, R, txt., somewhat superstitious, a sense in wh. the word is sometimes used; cf. Field, Notes, 125), more religious, God fearing, than others, quite religious (Abbott, Essays, 105 ff.; Deiss., LAE, 285): Act.17:22.† SYN.: εὐσεβής (which see), θεοσεβής, θρῆσκος (Cremer, 681; DB, ext., 142 a). (AS)
G1174.derivation: the compound of a derivative of the base of 1169 and 1142

G1185.strongs_def: δελεάζω (δέλεαρ, a bait), to allure by a bait: metaphorically, to allure, entice: with accusative, 2Pe.2:14, 18; pass., Jas.1:14.† (AS)

G1243.strongs_def: δι-αίρεσις, -εως, ἡ (διαιρέω), [in LXX chiefly for מַחֲלֹקֶת ;] __1. a distinction, diference. __2. a division, distribution: 1Co.12:4-6 (cf. διαιρέω; Cremer, 616).† (AS)

G1267.strongs_def: δια-μερισμός, -οῦ, ὁ (διαμερίζω), [in LXX: Eze.48:29 (מַחֲלֹקֶת), Mic.7:12 * ;] a division: opposite to εἰρήνη, Luk.12:51.† (AS)

G1281.strongs_def: δια-πραγματεύομαι , "perfective compound" (see M, Pr., 118); __1. to examine thoroughly (Plat.). __2. In late writers (Dion. Hal.), to gain by trading: Luk.19:15.† (AS)

G1297.strongs_def: διά-ταγμα, -τος, τό (διατάσσω), [in LXX: Est.7:11 (נִשְׁתְּוָן), Est.3:13, Wis.11:7 * ;] an edict, mandate: Heb.11:23.† (AS)

G1305.strongs_def: δια-τροφή, ῆς, ἡ (διατρέφω, to support, sustain), [in LXX: 1Ma.6:49 * ;] food, nourishment: 1Ti.6:8.† (AS)

G1306.strongs_def: δι-αυγάζω [in Aq.: Job.25:5 * ;] to shine through, to dawn: 2Pe.1:19 (cf. ἕως οὗ διαπνεύσῃ ἡ ἡμέρα, Gal.2:17).† (AS)

G1309.strongs_def: δια-φεύγω [in LXX: Jos.8:22 (פָּלִיט), Jos.10:28 (שָׂרִיד), etc. ;] to flee through, escape: Act.27:42.† (AS)

G1317.strongs_def: διδακτικός, -ή, -όν (= cl. διδασκαλικός) apt at teaching: 1Ti.3:2, 2Ti.2:24.† (AS)

G1351.strongs_def: διλογος, -ον (δίς, λέγω), __1. in sense of διλογεῖν, -ία (Xen.), given to repetition. __2. In NT, prob. (cf. δίγλωσσος, Pro.11:13, Sir.5:9) double-tongued: 1Ti.3:8.† (AS)

G1355.strongs_def: διό-περ conjunct. (διό, which see, strengthened by πέρ), [in LXX: Jdth.8:17; Jdt.8.1-36; 2Ma.5:1-27 * ;] for which very reason: 1Co.8:13 10:14.† (AS)

G1356.strongs_def: διοπετής (written also διϊπ-), -ές (δῖος, πίπτω, see Page on Ac, l.with; DB, i, 605, n., ext., 112a; Field, Notes, 130 f.), fallen from heaven (R, mg.): τὸ δ. (sc. ἄγαλμα, statue, image), Act.19:35.† (AS)
G1356.derivation: from the alternate of 2203 and the alternate of 4098

G1357.strongs_def: διόρθωσις, -εως, ἡ (see supr.), __1. a making straight. __2. a reforming, reformation (used in late writers of laws, etc.): Heb.9:10 (Cremer, 807).† διόρθωμα, -τος, τό (διορθόω, to make straight, set right), a correction, reform: Act.24:3.† διόρθωσις, -εως, ἡ (see supr.), __1. a making straight. __2. a reforming, reformation (used in late writers of laws, etc.): Heb.9:10 (Cremer, 807).† (AS)
G1357.derivation: from a compound of 1223 and a derivative of 3717, meaning to straighten thoroughly

G1359.strongs_def: Διόσ-κουροι, -ων, οἱ (Ion. and κοινή form of Att..., Διόσκοροι; Διός, genitive of Ζεύς + κόρος, a son), the Dioscuri (Castor and Pollux), twin sons of Zeus and Leda (RV, The Twin Brothers): Act.28:11.† (AS)
G1359.derivation: from the alternate of 2203 and a form of the base of 2877

G1361.strongs_def: Διοτρέφης (Rec. -τρεψής), -ες (Διός, genitive of Ζεύς + τρέφω: cherished by Zeus), as proper name, Diotrephes: III Jn 9.† (AS)

G1365.strongs_def: διστάζω (δίς), to doubt, hesitate: Mat.14:31 28:17.† SYN.: ἀπορέω, διαπορέω, διακρίνομαι, μετεωρίζομαι (see DCG, i, 491) (AS)

G1373.strongs_def: δίψος, -εος (-ους), τό (late form of δίψα), [in LXX chiefly for and cognates ;] thirst: 2Co.11:27.† (AS)

G1379.strongs_def: δογματίζω [in LXX: Est.3:9 (כָּתַב ni.), Dan LXX 2:13, 15 (דָּת), I Est.6:34, 2Ma.10:3 2Mac 15:36, 3Ma.4:11 * ;] to decree. Mid., to subject oneself to an ordinance: Col.2:20.† (AS)

G1386.strongs_def: δόλιος, -α, -ον (δόλος), [in LXX—chiefly in Pss, Pr, Sir—for etc. ;] deceitful: 2Co.11:13.† (AS)

G1389.strongs_def: δολόω, -ῶ (δόλος) [in LXX: Psa.15:3 (רָגַל), Psa.36:2 (חָלַק hi.) * ;] __1. to ensnare. __2. As of wine, to adulterate, corrupt: τ. λόγον τ. θεοῦ, 2Co.4:2.† SYN.: καπηλεύω which see (AS)

G1395.strongs_def: δότης, -ου, ὁ (δίδωμι), [in LXX: Pro.22:8 * ;] = δοτήρ, a giver: 2Co.9:7 (LXX) (not elsewhere).† (AS)

G1396.strongs_def: δουλαγωγέω, -ῶ (δοῦλος, ἄγω), to make a slave, bring into bondage: 1Co.9:27 (Cremer, 703).† (AS)
G1396.derivation: from a presumed compound of 1401 and 71

G1400.strongs_def: servant, slave; in the NT a person owned as a possession for various lengths of times (Hebrew slaves no more than seven years, Gentile slaves without time limit), of lower social status than free persons or masters; slaves could earn or purchase their freedom a male slave, or servant, of various degrees, Mt. 8:9, and frequently ; a servitor, person of mean condition, Phil. 2:7; feminine δούλη, a female slave; a handmaiden, Lk. 1:38, 48; Acts 2:18; δοῦλος, used figuratively, in a bad sense, one involved in moral or spiritual thraldom, Jn. 8:34; Rom. 6:17, 20; 1Cor. 7:23; 2Pet. 2:19; in a good sense, a devoted servant or minister, Acts 16:17; Rom. 1:1; one pledged or bound to serve, 1Cor. 7:22; 2Cor. 4:5

G1405.strongs_def: δράσσομαι [in LXX for נָשַׁק pi., Psa.2:12; elsewhere קָמַץ, as Lev.2:2 ;] to grasp with the hand, to lay hold of: metaphorically, with accusative (M, Pr., 65), 1Co.3:19 (LXX).† (AS)
G1405.derivation: perhaps akin to the base of 1404 (through the idea of capturing)

G1414.strongs_def: δυνατέω, -ῶ (δυνατός), to be able, be powerful, mighty: with inf., Rom.14:4, 2Co.9:8; absol., opposite to ἀσθενῶ 2Co.13:3.† (AS)

G1418.strongs_def: δυσ- inseparable prefix, opposite to εὖ, like un-, mis- (in unrest, mischance), giving the idea of difficulty, opposition, injuriousness, etc. (AS)
G1418.derivation: a primary inseparable particle of uncertain derivation

G1426.strongs_def: δυσφημία, -ας, ἡ (δύσφημος, slanderous), [in LXX: 1Ma.7:38, 3Ma.2:20 * ;] evil-speaking, defamation: opposite to εὐφημία, 2Co.6:8.† (AS)

G1449.strongs_def: 1. to mark in or on, to paint on , (Herdotus Historicus) 2. to inscribe, write in or on , (Herdotus Historicus):—;Pass., ἐγγεγραμμένος τι having something written on it, (Sophocles Tragicus); so Virgil flores inscripti nomina. 3. to enter in the public register , ἐγγρ. τὸν υἱὸν εἰς ἄνδρας (Demosthenes Orator):—;Pass., εἰς τοὺς δημότας ἐγγραφῆναι (Demosthenes Orator) 4. to enter on the judge's list, to indict , (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G1460.strongs_def: ἐγκατοικέω, see: ἐνκ-. ἐν-κατοικέω, -ῶ (Rec. ἐγκ-, see: ἐν), to dwell among: before ἐν, 2Pe.2:8.† (AS)

G1463.strongs_def: ἐγκομβόομαι, -οῦμαι (κόμβος, a knot, whence ἐγκόμβωμα, a garment tied on over others, used especially of a frock or apron worn by slaves), to put on oneself, as a garment, gird on: ἀλλήλοις τ. ταπεινοφροσύνην (as for service, RV, cf. Thayer, see word, but cf. also ICC, in l.), 1Pe.5:5.† (AS)
G1463.derivation: middle voice from 1722 and komboo (to gird)

G1464.strongs_def: ἐγκοπή, see: ἐνκ-. ἐν-κοπή (Rec. ἐγκ-, see: ἐν; T, ἐκκ-), -ῆς, ἡ (ἐγκόπτω) ; 1. an incision, a cutting, break. 2. Metaphorical, an interruption, a hindrance: 1Co.9:12.† (AS)

G1467.strongs_def: ἐγκρατεύομαι, depon., [in LXX for אפק, Gen.43:31, 1Ki.13:12, Est.5:10 א 3 * ;] to exercise self-control: 1Co.7:9; with accusative, πάντα (see Bl., 91), 1Co.9:25.† (AS)

G1468.strongs_def: ἐγκρατής, -ές (κράτος), [in LXX: Wis.8:20, Sir.6:27 15:1 26:15 27:30, al. ;] __1. strong, powerful. __2. C. genitive of thing(s), master of, hence, __3. (sc. ἑαυτοῦ), self -controlled, exercising self-control: Tit.1:8.† SYN.: σώφρων (see reff. s. ἐγκράτεια). (AS)

G1469.strongs_def: ἐγ-κρίνω, see: ἐνκ-. ἐν-κρίνω (Rec. ἐγκ-, see: ἐν), to reckon among : ἑαυτούς, 2Co.10:12.† (AS)

G1471.strongs_def: ἔγκυος, see: ἐνκ-. ἔνκυoς (Rec. ἐγκ-, see: ἐν), -ον (κύω, to conceive), [in LXX: Sir.42:10 * ;] pregnant, big with child : Luk.2:5.† (AS)

G1477.strongs_def: ἑδραίωμα, -τος, τό (ἑδραῖος), a support, bulwark, stay (Vg. fermamentum): 1Ti.3:15 (eccl.).† (AS)

G1481.strongs_def: ἐθνάρχης, -ου, ὁ (ἔθνος, ἄρχω), [in LXX: 1Ma.14:47 15:1, 2 * ;] an ethnarch, a provincial governor (cf. I Mac, ll. with; FlJ, Ant., xiii, 6, 6; Dalman, 332): 2Co.11:32.† (AS)

G1493.strongs_def: εἰδώλον (Rec. -εῖον), -ου, τό (εἴδωλον), [in LXX: Dan LXX 1:2 (בֵּית אוֹצַר אֱלֹהִים), Bel 9, I Est.2:10, 1Ma.1:47 10:83 * ;] an idol's temple: 1Co.8:10 (cf. Ἀσταρτεῖον, 1Ki.31:10; see ICC, in I Co, l.with).† (AS)

G1505.strongs_def: εἰλικρινία (Rec., cl., -κρινεία), -ας, ἡ (εἰλικρινής), [in LXX: Wis.7:25 A * ;] sincerity, purity: 1Co.5:8, 2Co.1:12 2:17.† (AS)

G1523.strongs_def: εἰσ-δέχομαι [in LXX for קָבַץ ;] to admit, receive: 2Co.6:17 (LXX) (Cremer, 687).† (AS)

G1548.strongs_def: ἐκ-γαμίσκω Rec. for γαμίσκω, which see: Luk.20:34-35. Not elsewhere.† γαμίζω (γάμος), to give in marriage, a daughter: 1Co.7:38. Pass., Mat.22:30 24:38, Mrk.12:25, Luk.17:27 20:35 (WH, mg., γαμίσκονται; cf. γαμίζω).† (AS)

G1549.strongs_def: ἔκ-γονος, -ον (ἐκγίγνομαι, to be born of), [in LXX for פְּרִי (neut.), בֵּן, etc. ;] __1. with genitive, born of. __2. As subst., ὁ, ἡ ἔ., a child, son or daughter; in pl., descendants: τέκνα ἢ ἔ., children or grand-children, 1Ti.5:4.† (AS)
G1549.derivation: neuter of a derivative of a compound of 1537 and 1096

G1550.strongs_def: εκ-δαπανάω, -ῶ strengthened form of δαπανάω, to spend wholly; pass., with reflexive force, to spend oneself wholly: before ὑπέρ, 2Co.12:15.† (AS)

G1552.strongs_def: ἔκ-δηλος, -ον (δῆλος), [in LXX: 3Ma.3:19 3Mac 6:5 * ;] strengthened form of δῆλος, which see, quite clear, evident: 2Ti.3:9.† (AS)

G1553.strongs_def: ἐκ-δημέω, -ῶ (ἔκδημος, from home; cf. -ία, 3Ma.4:11)*; to be from home, absent: 2Co.5:6; before ἀπό, 2Co.5:8; before ἐκ, 2Co.5:9 (cf. ἀπο-, ἐνδημέω).† (AS)

G1559.strongs_def: ἐκ-διώκω [in LXX for בָּרַח hi., צָמַת, הָדַף, etc. ;] to chase away, drive out: 1Th.2:15 (cf. Deu.6:19, Jol.2:20).† (AS)

G1569.strongs_def: ἔκ-θαμβος, -ον (θάμβος), [in LXX: Wis.10:19, Da TH Dan.7:7 (dreadful, terrible: אֵמְתָּנִי) * ;] amazed (cf. Polyb., xx, 10, 9): Act.3:11.† (AS)

G1571.strongs_def: ἐκ-καθαίρω [in LXX for בָּעַר, etc. ;] __1. to cleanse thoroughly, cleanse out: with accusative, ἑαυτόν, 2Ti.2:21; of the impurity removed, ζυμήν, 1Co.5:7.† (AS)

G1594.strongs_def: ἐκ-νήφω [in LXX: Gen.9:24, Hab.2:7 (יָקַץ), Jol.1:5, Hab.2:19 (יָקַץ hi.), 1Ki.25:37 (יָצָא), Sir.31:2 * ;] to become sober after drunkenness: metaphorically, of sobriety of mind, 1Co.15:34.† (AS)

G1597.strongs_def: ἔκ-παλαι adv. (of a class of compound adverbs common in late Gk.; see Mayor on 2 Pe, l.with), for a long time, from of old: 2Pe.2:3 3:5.† (AS)

G1619.strongs_def: ἐκτενῶς adv., [in LXX: Jon.3.8 (חׇזְקָה), Jol.1:14, Jdth.4:12, 3Ma.5:9 * ;] fervently, earnestly: Act.12:5, 1Pe.1:22; compar., Luk.22:44 (WH br., R, mg., omits).† (AS)

G1626.strongs_def: ἔκ-τρωμα, -τος, τό (ἐκτιτρώσκω, to miscarry), [in LXX: Job.3:16, Ecc.6:3 (; also in Aq., Psa.58:9, Num.12:12 (נָפַל) * ;] an abortion, an untimely birth (see Field, Notes, 179): 1Co.15:8.† (AS)
G1626.derivation: from a comparative of 1537 and titrosko (to wound)

G1629.strongs_def: ἐκ-φοβέω, -ῶ [in LXX chiefly for חָרֵד hi. ;] to frighten away, terrify: with accusative of person(s), 2Co.10:9.† (AS)

G1641.strongs_def: ἐλαττονέω, -ῶ (ἔλαττον), [in LXX (with -όω) chiefly for חָסֵר ;] to be less (RV, had no lack): 2Co.8:15 (LXX) (a rare word; cf. MM, Exp., xii).† (AS)

G1645.strongs_def: ἐλαφρός, -ά, -όν [in LXX chiefly for קַל, קָלָל ;] light in weight easy to bear: Mat.11:30; θλίψρις (EV, our light affliction), 2Co.4:17.† (AS)
G1645.derivation: probably akin to 1643 and the base of 1640

G1669.strongs_def: ἑλκόω, -ῶ __1. to wound. __2. to ulcerate; pass., to suffer from sores: pf. ptcp., εἱλκωμίνος (Rec. ἡλκ-), EV, full of sores, Luk.16:20.† (AS)

G1671.strongs_def: Ἑλλάς, -άδος, ἡ [in LXX: Isa.66:19, Eze.27:13 (יָוָן), 1Ma.1:1 1Mac 8:9 * ;] with varying usage as to geographical limits; in NT = 'Αχαία (cf. Act.18:12), Greece: Act.20:2.† (AS)

G1704.strongs_def: ἐν-περι-πατέω, -ῶ (Rec. ἐμπ-, see: ἐν) [in LXX: Lev.26:12 Job.1:7, al. (הָלַךְ hithp.), Wis.19:21 ;] to walk about in or among: before ἐν., dative of person(s), 2Co.6:16 (LXX),† (AS)

G1707.strongs_def: ἐμ-πλέκω [in LXX: Pro.28:18 (נָפַל), 2Ma.15:17 * ;] to weave in, entwine; pass., metaphorically, to be involved, entangled in: 2Ti.2:4, 2Pe.2:20.† (AS)

G1708.strongs_def: ἐμ-πλοκή, ῆς, ἡ (ἐμπλίκω), a braiding: τριχῶν, 1Pe.3:3.† (AS)

G2294.strongs_def: 1. courage, boldness , (Homer), attic; θ. τινός courage to do a thing, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 2. that which gives courage , θάρση grounds of confidence , (Euripides) 3. in bad sense, audacity , (Iliad by Homer): compare θράσος. (ML)

G2295.strongs_def: θαῦμα, -τος, τό [in LXX: Job.17:8 18:20 20:8 21:5 (שַׂעַר, etc.)* ;] __1. a wonder: 2Co.11:14. __2. wonder: Rev.17:6.† (AS)

G2302.strongs_def: θέατρον, -ον, τό (θεάομαι), __1. a theatre (used also as a place of assembly): Act.19:29, 31. __2. Collective for οἱ θεαταί, the spectators. __3. = θέα, θέαμα, a spectacle, show: metaphorically, 1Co.4:9.† (AS)

G2308.strongs_def: θέλησις, -εως, ἡ (θέλω) [in LXX: 2Ch.15:15, Pro.8:35 (רָצוֹן), Eze.18:23 (חֵפֶץ), LXX Dan.11:45 (צְבִי), Tob.12:18, Wis.16:25, 2Ma.12:16, 3Ma.2:26 * ;] in colloq. and MGr. = τὸ θέλειν, will: Heb.2:4.† (AS)

G2312.strongs_def: θεο-δίδακτος, -ον taught of God (cf. διδακτοὶ θεοῦ, Jhn.6:45): 1Th.4:9.† (AS)

G2314.strongs_def: θεομάχος, -ον [in Sm.: Job.26:5, Pro.9:18 21:16 * ;] fighting against God: Act.5:39.† (AS)

G2315.derivation: from 2316 and a presumed derivative of 4154

G2317.strongs_def: θεοσέβεια, -ας, ἡ (θεοσεβής), [in LXX Gen.20:11 (אֱלֹהִים יִרְאָה), Job.28:28 (אֲדֹנָי id.), Sir.1:24, Bar.5:4, 4Ma.7:6 4Mac 7:22, א 4Ma.15:28 א 4Ma.17:15 * ;] fear of God, godliness: 1Ti.2:10.† (AS)

G2341.strongs_def: θηριομαχέω, -ῶ (θηρίον, μάχομαι), to fight with wild beasts (Diod., al.): 1Co.15:32.† (AS)

G2352.strongs_def: θραύω [in LXX for 1,21 (Deu.28:33, Isa.42:4 58:6), etc. ;] to break in pieces, shatter; metaphorically, to break down: Luk.4:18 (LXX).† (AS)

G2353.strongs_def: θρέμμα, -τος, τό (τρέφω) __1. a nurseling, esp. of animals (Eur., Plat., al.). __2. cattle: Jhn.4:12.† (AS)

G2366.strongs_def: θύελλα, -ης, ἡ (θύω), [in LXX Deu.4:11 5:22 (עֲרָפֶל), Exo.10:22 * ;] (poët. in cl.), a hurricane, cyclone, whirlwind: Heb.12:18.† SYN.: λαίλαψ (which see) (AS)

G2386.strongs_def: ἴαμα, -τος, τό (ἰάομαι), [in LXX for מַרְפֵּא (2Ch.36:16, Ecc.10:4, Jer.33:6, etc. ;] __1. most frequently in cl., a means of healing, remedy (Thuc., al.; Wis.11:4 10:9). __2. = ἴασις (which see), a healing (Plat.; Jer, l.with): pl., 1Co.12:9 12:28 12:30.† (AS)

G2404.strongs_def: Ἱεράπολις (WH, Ἱερὰ Πόλις), -εως, ἡ Hierapolis: a city in the Lyons valley in the Province of Asia: Col.4:13.† (AS)

G2406.strongs_def: ἱεράτευμα, -τος, τό (ἱερατεύω), [in LXX: βασίλειον ἱ., Exo.19:1-25 6:1-30 (כֹּהֵן מַמְלָכָה) Exo.23:22, 2Ma.2:17 * ;] a priesthood, body of priests: ἱ ἅγιον, 1Pe.2:5; βασ. ἱ, 1Pe.2:9 (LXX, Ex, l.with).† (AS)

G2413.strongs_def: ἱερός, -ά, όν [in LXX: Eze.28:18 (מִקְדָּשׁ); τό ἱ, 1Ch.29:4 (בַּיִת), Eze.45:19 (עֲזָרָה); very frequently in I Est.1:1-58 -4 Mac ;] __1. in Hom., marvellous, mighty, divine. __2. (Also in Hom, and later cl.) consecrated to the deity, sacred: pl., ἱ. γράμματα, 2Ti.3:15. __3. As subst., __(a) (so in Hom.), τὰ ἱ., sacrifices, sacred rites, sacred things: 1Co.9:13; __(b) later, τὸ ἱ.,., a consecrated or sacred place, a temple: τ. Ἀρτέμιδος, Act.19:27; of the temple at Jerusalem, i.e. the entire precincts or some part thereof (as distinct from ὁ ναός, which see, the Sanctuary proper): 1Co.9:13, and frequently in Gosp. and esp. in Ac, Mat.12:6, Mrk.13:3, Act.4:1, al. (on the use of ἱ. in Imperial Iuser., see Deiss., LAE, 380 f.) (AS)

G2416.strongs_def: ἱερο-συλέω, -ῶ (ἱερόσυλος, which see), [in LXX: 2Ma.9:2 * ;] to rob a temple (commit sacrilege, R, mg.): Rom.2:22.† (AS)

G2429.strongs_def: ἰκμάς, -άδος, ἡ [in LXX. Jer.17:8 (יוּבַל), Job.26:14 (שֶׁמֶץ)* ;] moisture: Luk.8:6.† (AS)

G2431.strongs_def: ἱλαρός, -ά, -όν (ἵλαος = ἵλεως, which see), [in LXX: Pro.19:12 (רָצוֹן) Pro.22:8, Est.5:1, Job.33:26, Sir.13:26 26:4, 3Ma.6:35 * ;] cheerful, joyous: 2Co.9:7 (Pro.22:8" (LXX) )† (AS)

G2432.strongs_def: ἱλαρότης, -ητος, ἡ (ἱλαρός), [in LXX: Pro.18:22 (רָצוֹן)* ;] cheerfulness: Rom.12:8.† (AS)

G2434.strongs_def: ἱλασμός, -οῦ (ἱλάσκομαι), [in LXX: Lev.25:9, Num.5:8 (כִּפֻּר), Psa.130:4, Da TH Dan.9:9 (סְלִיחָה), Amo.8:14 (אַשְׁמָה), Eze.44:27 (חַטָּאָה), 1Ch.28:20, Sir.18:20 A, 2Ma.3:33 * ;] __1. an appeasing (Plut.). __2. a means of appeasing, propitiation (Philo; Nu, Ez, ll.with): 1Jn.2:2 Jn 4:10. __3. In LXX also forgiveness (Ps, Da TH, ll.with).† (AS)

G2442.strongs_def: ἱμείρω [in LXX: Job.3:21 B3R (ABא, ὁμ-) ;] 1Th.2:8 (Rec.), see: ὁμείρομαί. (AS)
G2442.derivation: middle voice from himeros (a yearning, of uncertain affinity)

G2450.strongs_def: Ἰουδαΐζω (Ἰουδαῖος), [in LXX: Est.8:17 (יָהַד hith.)* ;] to can-form to Jewish practice, to Judaize: Gal.2:14.† (AS)

G2472.strongs_def: ἰσότιμος, -ον (ἴσος, τιμή), equally privileged, held in equal honour: πίστις, 2Pe.1:1 (R, mg., equally precious, but v Field, Notes, 240; Mayor, in l).† (AS)

G2493.strongs_def: Ἰωήλ, ὁ indecl. (Heb. יוֹאֵל,), Joel: Act.2:16.† (AS)

G2506.strongs_def: καθ-αίρεσις, -εως, ἡ (καθαιρέω), [in LXX: Exo.23:24 (הָרַס), 1Ma.3:43 * ;] a pulling down, destruction: figuratively, κ. ὀχυρωμάτων, 2Co.10:4; opposite to οἰκοδομή, 2Co.10:8 13:10.† (AS)

G2562.strongs_def: καλάμη, -ης, ἡ (cf. κάλαμος), [in LXX chiefly for קַשׁ, Exo.5:12, Isa.5:24, al. ;] a stalk of corn, stubble: 1Co.3:12.† (AS)

G2567.strongs_def: καλο-διδάσκαλος, -ου, ὁ a teacher of that which is good: Tit.2:3.† (AS)

G2569.strongs_def: καλο-ποιέω, -ῶ [in LXX: Lev.5:4 F (καλῶς π., B) * ;] to do well, act honourably: 2Th.3:13 (cf. Gal.6:9 τὸ καλὸν π.).† (AS)

G2571.strongs_def: κάλυμμα, -τος, τό (καλύπτω), [in LXX: Num.3:25 4:8 ff. (מְכַסֶּה), Exo_34:33 ff. (מַסְוֶה), etc. ;] a covering, veil: 2Co.3:13-16 † (AS)

G2585.strongs_def: καπηλεύω (κάπηλος, a huckster, cf. Isa.1:22 (LXX), Sir.26:29) to make a trade of (RV, mg., make merchandise of), or perhaps (cf. Isa, l.with) to corrupt (RV, tit.): 2Co.2:17.† (AS)

G2599.strongs_def: κατα-βαρέω, -ῶ to weigh down: metaphorically, with accusative of person(s), 2Co.12:16.† (AS)

G2607.strongs_def: κατα-γινώσκω (see: γινώσκω), [in LXX: Deu.25:1 (רָשַׁע hi.), Pro.28:11 (חָקַר), Sir.14:2 19:5 * ;] to blame, condemn: with genitive of person(s), 1Jn.3:20-21; pass., κατεγνωσμένος ἦν (RV, he stood condemned, see Ellie., in l; but cf. Field, Notes, 188): Gal.2:11.† (AS)

G2619.strongs_def: κατα-καλύπτω [in LXX chiefly for כָּסָה pi. ;] to cover up; mid., to cover or veil oneself: 1Co.11:6; τ. κεφαλήν, 1Co.11:7.† (AS)

G2626.strongs_def: κατα-κλύζω [in LXX for שָׁטַף, Psa.78:20, al. ;] to inundate, deluge: pass., 2Pe.3:6.† (AS)

G2633.strongs_def: κατά-κρισις, -εως, ἡ (κατακρίνω), condemnation: 2Co.3:9 7:3 (cf. Deiss., LAE, 91 f.).† (AS)

G2636.strongs_def: κατα-λαλιά, -ᾶς, ἡ (κατάλαλος), [in LXX: Wis.1:11 * ;] evil-speaking, railing: p1., 2Co.12:20, 1Pe.2:1.† (AS)

G2639.strongs_def: κατα-λέγω [in LXX: Deu.19:16 (עָנָה), 2Ma.7:30 R * ;] __1. to lay down; mid. (in Hom.), to lie down. __2. to narrate (LXX, ll. with). __3. to choose out, hence, to enrol (as of soldiers, Hdt., Thuc., a1., see LS, see word): of widows, pass., 1Ti.5:9 (cf. Ellic.; CGT, in l).† (AS)

G2655.strongs_def: κατα-ναρκάω, -ῶ (ναρκάω, to grow numb, in LXX, in causal sense, for יָקַע, Gen.32:25 (26); without Heb. equiv., Gen.32:32 (33) Job.33:19, Dan LXX 11:6*); __1. to cause to grow numb. __2. Intrans., to grow numb; hence metaphorically, to be inactive, be burdensome to with genitive, 2Co.11:9 12:13-14; pass., to be quite numb (Hippocr.).† (AS)

G2676.strongs_def: κατ-άρτισις, -εως, ἡ (καταρτίζω), a strengthening, making fit: in ethical sense, 2Co.13:9.† (AS)

G2689.strongs_def: κατα-στολή, -ῆς, ἡ (καταστέλλω), [in LXX: Isa.61:3 (מַעֲטֶה)* ;] __1. a letting down, checking. __2. steadiness, quietness in demeanour. __3. LXX and NT (cf. Plut., ii, 65 D; -ίζω = vestire), a garment, dress, attire: 1Ti.2:9 (but see Ellic., in l).† (AS)

G2691.strongs_def: κατα-στρηνιάω, -ῶ to wax wanton against: with genitive, 1Ti.5:11 (AS)

G2692.strongs_def: κατα-στροφή, -ῆς, ἡ (καταστρέφω), [in LXX: Job.21:17, Pro.1:27 (אֵיד), al. ;] __1. overthrow: 2Pe.2:6 (WH, om.). __2. Metaphorical, subversion, upsetting (cf. καθαίρεσις, 2Co.13:10): 2Ti.2:14.† (AS)

G2693.strongs_def: κατα-στρώννυμι [in LXX: Num.14:16 (שָׁחַט), Job.12:23 (שָׁטַח), שָׁטַח), Jdt.4.1-15; Jdt.2.1-28 Mac.4 ;] __1. to strew or spread over. __2. to lay low, overthrow: 1Co.10:5.† (AS)

G2699.strongs_def: κατα-τομή, -ῆς, ἡ [in Sm.: Jer.31:37 (κατατέμνω is used in LXX of forbidden mutilations: Lev.21:5, al.) ;] __1. incision. __2. excision, concision, mutilation: in sarcasm, by paronomasia, in contrast to (true) περιτομή (v3), of Judaizing Christians, Php.3:2 (see Lft., in l; Cremer, 883).† (AS)
G2699.derivation: from a compound of 2596 and temno (to cut)

G2704.strongs_def: κατα-φθείρω [in LXX chiefly for שָׁחַת hi., Gen.6:12, al. ;] __1 1 to destroy entirely. __2. In moral sense (as LXX), to deprave, corrupt: pass. pf. ptcp., before τ. νο ν, 2Ti.3:8.† (AS)

G2709.strongs_def: κατα-χθόνιος, -ον (χθών, the earth), subterranean, under the earth (in cl., of the infernal gods): of the departed in Hades, opposite to ἐπουράνιος, ἐπίγειος, Php.2:10.† (AS)

G2710.strongs_def: κατα-χράομαι, -ῶμαι [in LXX: Ep. Je.28, 3Ma.4:5 3Mac 5:22 * ;] to make full use of, use to the uttermost, use up: 1Co.7:31; with dative, 1Co.9:18 (for other senses, see LS, see word)..† (AS)

G2726.strongs_def: κατήφεια, -ας, ἡ (κατηφής, downcast, Wis.17:4 *), dejection: Jas.4:9.† (AS)
G2726.derivation: from a compound of 2596 and perhaps a derivative of the base of 5316 (meaning downcast in look)

G2733.strongs_def: κατ-οικία, -ας, ἡ (κατοικέω), [in LXX chiefly for מוֹשָׁב, Exo.35:3, al. ;] __1. a dwelling: Act.17:26. __2. a settlement (Polyb.).† (AS)

G2734.strongs_def: κατοπτρίζω (κάτοπτρον, a mirror), to show as in a mirror. Mid., to see oneself mirrored (see MM, Exp., xv); with accusative of thing(s) (R, txt., but see mg.), to reflect as a mirror: 2Co.3:18 (cf. Abbott, Essays, 94).† (AS)
G2734.derivation: middle voice from a compound of 2596 and a derivative of 3700 [cf 2072]

G2740.strongs_def: καῦσις, -εως, ἡ (καίω), [in LXX for בָּעַר pi., etc. ;] burning: Heb.6:8.† (AS)

G2741.strongs_def: καυσόω, -ῶ (καῦσος, burning heat, fever), only in pass., __1. to burn with fever (Galen., al.). __2. In NT, to burn with great heat: 2Pe.3:10 3:12 (V. Mayor, in l).† (AS)

G2743.strongs_def: καυστηριάζω (Rec. καυτηρ-, and so usually in Gk. writers, see Soph., Lex., see word) to mark by branding, brand (AV, scar, but see CGT, in l): metaphorically, pass. pf. ptcp., 1Ti.4:2 (cf. καυτήριον, 4Ma.15:22 *).† (AS)

G2752.strongs_def: κέλευσμα, -τος, τό (κελεύω), [in LXX: Pro.30:27 * ;] a call, summons, shout of command: 1Th.4:16 (see M, Th., in l).† (AS)

G2757.strongs_def: κενοφωνία, -ας, ἡ (κενός, φωνέω), [cf. κενολογέω (צָפַף), Isa.8:19 * ;] empty talk, babbling: pl., 1Ti.6:20, 2Ti.2:16.† (AS)
G2757.derivation: from a presumed compound of 2756 and 5456

G2781.strongs_def: κηρίον, -ου, τό (κηρός, wax), [in LXX for נֹפֶת, צוּף, Psa.19:10 118:12, Pro.16:24, al. ;] honeycomb: κ. μελίσσιον, Luk.24:42 (Rec.; WH, txt., R, txt., omit).† (AS)

G2783.strongs_def: κῆρυξ (κήρ-, T), -υκος, ὁ [in LXX: Dan LXX TH Dan.3:4 (כָּרוֹז), Gen.41:43, Sir.20:15, 4Ma.6:4 * ;] a herald: 1Ti.2:7, 2Ti.1:11, 2Pe.2:5.† (AS)

G2809.strongs_def: κλέμμα, -τος, τό (κλέπτω), [in LXX: Gen.31:39, Exo.22:3-4 (2-3) (גָּנַב, גְּנֵבָה)* ;] __1. a thing stolen (Arist., LXX) __2. = κλοπή, theft (Plato, al.): pl., Rev.9:21.† (AS)

G2811.strongs_def: κλέος, -ους, τό [in LXX: Job.28:22 (שֵׁמַע) Job.30:8 * ;] __1. a rumour, report. __2. good report, fame, glory: 1Pe.2:20.† (AS)

G2828.strongs_def: κλισία, -ας, ή (κλίνω), [in LXX: 3Ma.6:31 A* ;] __1. a place for reclining; hence, __(a) a hut; __(b) an easy chair; __(with) a couch. __2. a company reclining: pl., Luk.9:14 (cf. FlJ, Ant., xii, 2, 12) (AS)

G2833.strongs_def: κνήθω (late form of κνάω), __1. to scratch. __2. to tickle; pass., to itch: 2Ti.4:3.† (AS)

G2835.strongs_def: κοδράντης, -ου, ὁ (Lat. quadrans, the fourth part of an as), a quadrans (AV, farthing): Mat.5:26, Mrk.12:42.† (AS)

G2843.strongs_def: κοινωνικός, -ή, -όν (κοινωνία), __1. sociable. __2. ready to com­municate or impart (R, mg., ready to sympathize, see Field, Notes, 213 f.): 1Ti.6:18.† (AS)

G2850.strongs_def: κολακία (Rec. -εία), -ας, ἡ (κολακεύω, to flatter), flattery: 1Th.2:5 (see Lft., Notes, 23).† (AS)
G2850.derivation: from a derivative of kolax (a fawner)

G2858.strongs_def: Κολασσαεύς (Rec. Κολοσ-), -έως, ὁ a Colossian: pl., Col., tit. (and subscr., Rec., Tr.).† (AS)

G2864.strongs_def: κόμη, -ης, ἡ [in LXX: Num.6:5, Eze.44:20 (פֶּרַע), al. ;] the hair: 1Co.11:15.† (AS)

G2879.strongs_def: Κορέ indecl. (in FlJ, -έου), ὁ (Heb. קֶרַח) Korah: Ju 11.† (AS)

G2887.strongs_def: κόσμιος, -ον (in cl. -α, -ον), (κόσμος), [in LXX: Ecc.12:9 (תָּקַן)* ;] orderly, decent, modest: 1Ti.2:9 (WH, mg., -ίως, which see) 1Ti.3:2.† (AS)

G2900.strongs_def: κραταιός, -ά, -όν (κράτος), (in cl. poët, form of κρατερός), [in LXX chiefly for חָזַק and cognates ;] strong, mighty: 1Pe.5:6.† (AS)

G2908.strongs_def: κρείσσων (Epic and old Att..) and κρείττων (later Att..), prop. comparat. of κρατύς, strong, but in sense often (as in cl., see LS, see word) as comparat. of ἀγαθός, [in LXX chiefly for טוֹב ;] better; __(a) as to ad­vantage or usefulness: 1Co.11:17, Heb.11:40 12:24; πολλῷ μᾶλλον κ., Php.1:23; κρεῖσσον ποιεῖν, 1Co.7:38; ἐστιν, before inf., 1Co.7:9, 2Pe.2:21; __(b) as to excellence: Heb.1:4 6:9 7:7, 19 7:22 8:6 9:23 10:34 11:16, 35; κ. ἐστι, before inf., 1Pe.3:17.† (AS)
G2908.derivation: neuter of an alternate form of 2909

G2922.strongs_def: κριτήριον, -ου, τό (κριτής), [in LXX: 3Ki.7:7 (מִשְׁפָּט), Dan LXX TH Dan.7:10, 26, (דִּין), Su 1:49, Exo.21:6, Jdg.5:10 * ;] __1. a means of judging, test, criterion. __2. a tribunal: 1Co.6:2 6:4, Jas.2:6.† (AS)

G2929.strongs_def: κρυσταλλίζω (κρύσταλλος), to shine like crystal, be crystal-clear: Rev.21:11 (ἅπ, λεγ.).† (AS)

G2939.strongs_def: κτίστης, -oυ, ὁ (κτίζω), [in LXX: 2Ki.22:32 (Heb., al.), Jdth.9:12, Sir.24:8, 2 24:1-34; 4Ma.5:1-38 * ;] __1. (cl.) a founder. __2. a creator: of God, 1Pe.4:19.† (AS)

G2941.strongs_def: κυβέρνησις, -εως, ἡ (κυβερνάω, Lat. gubernare, to guide), [in LXX: Pro.1:5 11:14 24:6 (תַּחְבֻּלָה) * ;] __1. steering, pilotage (Plat.). __2. Metaphorical, government: pl., 1Co.12:28.† (AS)
G2941.derivation: from kubernao (of Latin origin, to steer)

G2946.strongs_def: κύλισμα, -τος, τό (κυλίω), [in Sm.: Eze.10:13 * ;] __1. a roll. __2. = κυλισμός (which see), a rolling, wallowing (or, as κυλίστρα, Xen., Eq., see 3, a rolling place): 2Pe.2:22 (Rec.).† (AS)

G2950.strongs_def: κύμβαλον, -ου, τό (κύμβη, a cup), [in LXX chiefly for מְצִלָּה ;] a cymbal: 1Co.13:1.† (AS)
G2950.derivation: from a derivative of the base of 2949

G2959.strongs_def: κυρία (Κυρία, T, WH, mg.), -ας, ἡ, [in LXX chiefly for גְּבֶרֶת ;] a lady: 2Jn.1 Jn 5 (on the interpretation, see ICC, 167 ff.).† (AS)

G2984.strongs_def: Λάμεχ, ὁ indecl. (Heb. לֶמֶךְ), Lamech (Gen.5:25): Luk.3:36.† (AS)

G2996.strongs_def: Λασέα (Rec. -αία), -ας, ἡ Lasea, a city of Crete, otherwise un­known: Act.27:8.† (AS)

G3006.strongs_def: λεῖος, -εία, -εῖον [in LXX: Gen.27:11, 1Ki.17:40 R (חָלַק, חַלֻּק); ὁδὸς λ., Isa.40:4 Α (בִּקְעָה); Pro.2:20 12:13 26:23 * ;] smooth: opposite to τραχύς, Luk.3:5 (LXX).† (AS)

G3024.strongs_def: λήθη, -ης, ἡ (λήθω = λανθάνω) [in LXX: Lev.5:15 (מַעַל), Wis.16:11, Sir.14:7, al. ;] forgetfulness: λ. λαβεῖν (on the phrase, see Mayor, in l): 2Pe.1:9.† (AS)

G3044.strongs_def: 1. Linos , a mythical minstrel, son of Apollo and Urania (Calliope), teacher of Orpheus, (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus), etc. 2. as appellative, the song or lay of Linos , sung by a boy to the cithara while the vintagers are at work, Λίνον ὑπὸ καλὸν ἄειδεν sang the lovely lay of Linos in accompaniment, (Iliad by Homer):—;compare αἴλινος which is a mournful song. (ML)

G3048.strongs_def: λογία (prop., -εία, see BS, 142 ff.), -ας, ἡ (λογεύω, to collect, a word found in π., see Deiss., BS, l.with; LAE, 70, 103; MM, xvi), a collection: 1Co.16:1-2.† (AS)

G3054.strongs_def: λογομαχέω, -ῶ (λόγος, μάχομαι), to strive with words: 2Ti.2:14.† (AS)

G3055.strongs_def: λογομαχία, -ας, ἡ (λογομαχέω), a strife of words: pl., 1Ti.6:4.† (AS)

G3059.strongs_def: λοιδορία, -ας, ἡ (λοιδορέω), [in LXX chiefly for רִיב, מְרִיבָה ;] abuse, railing: 1Ti.5:14, 1Pe.3:9.† (AS)

G3060.strongs_def: λοίδορος, -ον [in LXX: Pro.25:24 26:21 27:15 (מִדְיָן) Sir.23:8 * ;] railing, abusive; as subst., ὁ λ., a railer: 1Co.5:11 6:10.† (AS)

G3073.strongs_def: Λυκία, -ας, ἡ Lydia, a region of Asia Minor; Act.27:5.† (AS)

G3080.strongs_def: λύσις, -εως, ἡ (λύω), [in LXX: Ecc.8:1 (Ecc.8:1) (פֵּשֶׁר), Dan LXX 12:8, Wis.8:8 * ;] a loosing: of divorce, 1Co.7:27.† (AS)

G3093.strongs_def: Μαγαδάν Magadan, an unidentified place on the coast of the Sea of Galilee: Mat.15:39 (Rec. Μαγδαλά; cf. Mrk.8:10, where for Δαλμανουθά, D* has Μελεγαδά, D1 Μαγαιδά, some cursives Μαγαδά, and Euseb. Onomast. Μεγαιδάν; cf. DB, iii, see word).† Μαγδαλά (Aram. מַגְדְֺּלָא = Heb. H4026, which in Jos.15:37 B is rendered Μαγαδά), Magdala: Mat.15:39 (Rec. for Μαγαδάν, which see).† (AS)

G3095.strongs_def: μαγία (Rec. -εία), -ας, ἡ (μάγος), __1. the lore of the Magians (Plat.). __2. magic: pl., magic arts, sorceries: Act.8:11.† (AS)

G3111.strongs_def: μάκελλον, -ου, τό (Lat. macellum), a meat-market: 1Co.10:25 (see Deiss., LAE, 274; MM, xvi).† (AS)

G3116.strongs_def: μακροθύμως adv., with forbearance, patiently: Act.26:3.† (AS)

G3124.strongs_def: Μάλχος, -ου, ὁ (Hellenistic form of Heb. מֶלֶךְ), Malchus: Jhn.18:10.† (AS)

G3125.strongs_def: μάμμη, -ης, ἡ (onomatop.), [in LXX: 4Ma.16:9 * ;] __1. in cl., a child's name for mother. __2. In late Gk. (= cl., τήθη), a grandmother: (LXX, l.with), 2Ti.1:5.† (AS)

G3130.strongs_def: μανία, -ας, ἡ (μαίνομαι) [in LXX: Hos.9:7-8 מַשְׂטֵמָה), Wis.5:4, al. ;] frenzy, madness: Act.26:24.† (AS)

G3132.strongs_def: μαντεύομαι (μαντίς, a seer, diviner), [in LXX for קָסַם, Deu.18:10, al. ;] to divine, practise divination: Act.16:16.† SYN.: προφητεύω, which see, in distinction from which μ. is used in LXX and NT only of false prophets and those who practise the heathen arts of divination and soothsaying (cf. 1Ki.28:8, and see Tr., Syn., § vi) (AS)
G3132.derivation: from a derivative of 3105 (meaning a prophet, as supposed to rave through inspiration)

G3134.strongs_def: μαρὰν ἀθά (Rec. μαραναθά; Aram.: on the original form see Dalman, Gr., § 41, 1; 74, 3; Words, 328), Maranatha, i.e. the Lord cometh (but see Dalman, ll. with; Field, Notes, 180; ICC, in l): 1Co.16:22.† (AS)
G3134.derivation: of Aramaic origin (meaning our Lord has come)

G3139.strongs_def: μάρμαρος, -ου, ὁ (μαρμαίρω, to glisten), [in LXX: Ep. Jer.7:2 * ;] __1. any crystalline stone (Hom., Eur., al.). __2. In later writers, marble: Rev.18:12.† (AS)

G3150.strongs_def: ματαιολογία, -ας, ἡ (ματαιολόγος), idle or foolish talk: 1Ti.1:6.† (AS)

G3169.strongs_def: μεγαλοπρεπής, ές (= μεγάλῳ πρέπων), [in LXX: Deu.33:26 (גַּאֲוָה) 2Ma.8:15 2Mac 15:13, 3Ma.2:9 * ;] befitting a great man, magnificent, majestic: 2Pe.1:17 (cf. MM, xvi).† (AS)

G3176.strongs_def: μέγιστος, see: μέγας. μέγας, μεγάλη, μέγα, [in LXX chiefly for גָּדוֹל, also for מַרְבֶּה ,רַב (incl. μείζων), רֹב (μέγιστος) ;] great; __1. of external form, bodily size, measure, extent: λίθος, Mat.2:60; δράκων, Rev.12:3; ἰχθῦς, Jhn.21:11; πόλις, Rev.11:8; μάχαιρα, Rev.6:4, al. __2. Of intensity and degree: δύναμις, Act.4:33; φόβος, Mrk.4:41; ἀγάπη, Jhn.15:13; ἄνεμος, ib. 6:18; κραυγή, Act.23:9; φῶς, Mat.4:16; πυρετός, Luk.4:38; θλίψις, Mat.24:21. __3. Of rank; __(a) of persons: θεός (MM, xvi), Tit.2:13; Ἄρτεμις, Act.19:27; compar. (see infr.), Mat.18:1 (cf. Dalman, Words, 113f.); neut. for masc. (Bl., §32, 1), Mat.12:6; __(b) of things: ἁμαρτία, Jhn.19:11; μυστήριον, Eph.5:32; = μεγίστη (see infr., and cf. Field, Notes, 16f.), Mat.22:36; compar. for superl. (M, Pr., 78), 1Co.13:13. __4. __(a) Compar., μείζων: Mat.11:11 23:17, al.; neut. pl., μείζονα, contr. μείζω, Jhn.1:51; double compar., μειζότερος (M, Pr., 236; Bl., §11, 4), III Jo 4; __(b) superl, μέγιστος (Deiss., BS, 365), 2Pe.1:4. (AS)

G3183.strongs_def: μέθυσος, -α, -ον (also -ος, -ον; prop., only of women, but in late writers also = μεθυστικός, of men), [in LXX: Pro.23:21 (סָבָא) Pro.26:9 (שִׁכּוֹר), Sir.19:1 26:8, 4Ma.2:7 * ;] drunken: 1Co.5:11 6:10.† (AS)

G3186.strongs_def: μειζότερος, see: μέγας. μέγας, μεγάλη, μέγα, [in LXX chiefly for גָּדוֹל, also for מַרְבֶּה ,רַב (incl. μείζων), רֹב (μέγιστος) ;] great; __1. of external form, bodily size, measure, extent: λίθος, Mat.2:60; δράκων, Rev.12:3; ἰχθῦς, Jhn.21:11; πόλις, Rev.11:8; μάχαιρα, Rev.6:4, al. __2. Of intensity and degree: δύναμις, Act.4:33; φόβος, Mrk.4:41; ἀγάπη, Jhn.15:13; ἄνεμος, ib. 6:18; κραυγή, Act.23:9; φῶς, Mat.4:16; πυρετός, Luk.4:38; θλίψις, Mat.24:21. __3. Of rank; __(a) of persons: θεός (MM, xvi), Tit.2:13; Ἄρτεμις, Act.19:27; compar. (see infr.), Mat.18:1 (cf. Dalman, Words, 113f.); neut. for masc. (Bl., §32, 1), Mat.12:6; __(b) of things: ἁμαρτία, Jhn.19:11; μυστήριον, Eph.5:32; = μεγίστη (see infr., and cf. Field, Notes, 16f.), Mat.22:36; compar. for superl. (M, Pr., 78), 1Co.13:13. __4. __(a) Compar., μείζων: Mat.11:11 23:17, al.; neut. pl., μείζονα, contr. μείζω, Jhn.1:51; double compar., μειζότερος (M, Pr., 236; Bl., §11, 4), III Jo 4; __(b) superl, μέγιστος (Deiss., BS, 365), 2Pe.1:4. (AS)

G3188.strongs_def: μέλαν, τό, see: μέλας. μέλας, -αινα, -αν genitive, -ανος, -αίνης, -ανος, [in LXX: Sng.1:5, Zec.6:2 (שָׁחֹר), etc. ;] black: Rev.6:5, 12; opposite to λευκός, Mat.5:36; neut., τὸ μ., ink : 2Co.3:3, II Jn 12, 3Jn.13.† (AS)

G3194.strongs_def: Μελίτη (Rec., R, txt.), Μελιτήνη (WH, R, mg., see WH, App., 160), Melita, Melitene (mod. Malta) : Act.28:1.† (AS)

G3336.strongs_def: μετά-λημψις (Rec. -ληψις), -εως, ἡ (μεταλαμβάνω) participation, taking, receiving: of food, 1Ti.4:3.† (AS)

G3349.strongs_def: μετ-εωρίζω (μετέωρος, (a) in mid air; (b) buoyed up; (with) in suspense; Thuc.; in π. opposite to ἀμέριμνος, see Zorell, see word) [in LXX: Ob 4 (גָּבַהּ hi.), Mic.4:1 (נָשָׂא ni.), Psa.131:1, Eze.10:16-17, 19 (רוּם), 2Ma.5:17 2Mac 7:34, 3Ma.6:5 * ;] to raise on high (Thue., Xen., al.; Ob, Mi, Ez, ll with). Metaphorical, __(a) to buoy up; pass., to be elated, puffed up (Polyb., al., Psa.2:1-12, 3 Mac, ll. with) __(b) to be anxious, in suspense (Polyb., see 70, 10; FlJ, BJ, iv, 2, 5) : Luk.12:29.† (AS)
G3349.derivation: from a compound of 3326 and a collateral form of 142 or perhaps rather 109 (cf \"meteor\")

G3352.strongs_def: μετοχή, -ῆς, ἡ (μετέχω), [in LXX: Psa.122:3 א R (חָבַר pu.) * ;] sharing, fellowship: 2Co.6:14.† (AS)

G3386.strongs_def: μή-τι-γε (μήτι γε, Rec., L; μή τι γε, Tr.), strengthened form of μήτι, let alone: i.e. according to context; __(a) much less; __(b) much more: 1Co.6:3.† (AS)

G3389.strongs_def: μητρολῴας (Rec. -αλῴας, in cl., -αλοίας, see B1., § 3, 3; 6, 2), -ου, ὁ (μήτρρ + ἀλοιάω, to smite) __(a) a matricide: 1Ti.1:9 (AV, R, txt., but see infr.); __(b) a smiter of his mother: 1Ti.1:9 (R, mg., cf. Exo.21:15, and see Ellic., CGT, in l).† (AS)

G3390.strongs_def: μητρό-πολις, -εως, ἡ [in LXX for אָב etc. ;] a metropolis, chief city: ITi, subscr. (Rec.).† (AS)

G3393.strongs_def: μίασμα, -τος, τό (μιαίνω), chiefly in trag. and late writers; [in LXX: Lev.7:8, 18, (פִּגּוּל), Jer.32:34 (שִׁקּוּץ), Eze.33:31 (בֶּצַע), Jdth.9:2, 4 13:16, 1Ma.13:50 * ;] a stain, defilement: pl., 2Pe.2:20.† (AS)

G3394.strongs_def: μιασμός, -οῦ, ὁ (μιαίνω), [in LXX: Wis.14:26, 1Ma.4:43 * ;] __1. prop., the act of defiling. __2. = μίασμα (which see) : 2Pe.2:10 (cf. Plut., Mor., 393c).† (AS)

G3405.strongs_def: μισθαποδοσία, -ας, ἡ (μισθός, ἀποδίδωμι; cl. μισθοδοσία), pay­ment of wages, recompense; meton., __(a) of reward: Heb.10:35 11:26; __(b) of punishment : Heb.2:2.† (AS)

G3412.strongs_def: Μιτυλήνη, -ης, ἡ (late form - Strab., Plut. - of cl. Μυτιλ-), Mytilene, Mitylene, chief city of Lesbos: Act.20:14.† (AS)

G3420.strongs_def: μνήμη, -ης, ἡ (μνάομαι), [in LXX for זֵכֶר, זִכְרוֹן ;] memory, remembrance, mention: μ. ποιεῖσθαι, with genitive, to remember, 2Pe.1:15 (but in cl., π., μ. π. more frequently = to make mention, and so perh. here, cf. Mayor, in l; and for ex. from π., see Zorell, see word).† SYN.: μνεία, q.v (AS)

G3436.strongs_def: μολυσμός, -οῦ, ὁ (μολύνω), [in LXX: Jer.23:15 (חֲנֻפָה), I Est.8:83, 2Ma.5:27 * ;] defilement: with genitive obj., 2Co.7:1 (Plut., FlJ).† (AS)

G3443.strongs_def: μονόω, -ῶ (μόνος), [in Aq.: Gen.49:6 ;] to leave alone, forsake: of a childless widow, pf. ptcp. pass., 1Ti.5:5.† (AS)

G3449.strongs_def: μόχθος, -ου, ὁ (= Hom. μόγος), in cl. chiefly poët., [in LXX for תְּלָאָה, עָמָל, etc. ;] toil, labour, hardship, distress: 2Co.11:27, 1Th.2:9, 2Th.3:8.† SYN.: κόπος (which see), πόνος (AS)

G3467.strongs_def: μυ-ωπάζω (μύωψ, closing the eyes, short-sighted; μύω, ὤψ) to be short-sighted: 2Pe.1:9 (R, mg., closing his eyes; see ICC, in l).† (AS)
G3467.derivation: from a compound of the base of 3466 and ops (the face, from 3700)

G3468.strongs_def: μώλωψ, -ωπος, ὁ [in LXX for חַבּוּרָה, Exo.21:25, al. ;] a bruise, wound from a stripe: 1Pe.2:24 (LXX) (Arist., Plut., al.).† (AS)
G3468.derivation: from molos (\"moil\", probably akin to the base of 3433) and probably ops (the face, from 3700)

G3469.strongs_def: μωμάομαι, -ῶμαι (μῶμος), poët. and late prose, [in LXX: Pro.9:7 (מאוּם), Wis.10:14, Sir.31:18 * ;] to find fault with, blame: 2Co.8:20; pass., 2Co.6:3.† (AS)

G3470.strongs_def: μῶμος, -ου, ὁ [in LXX, of physical blemishes : Lev.21:17 ff., Deu.15:21, Sng.4:7, al. (מאוּם); of mental defect, Sir.20:24, al. ;] __1. in cl. poets and late prose, blame, disgrace. __2. In LXX, perb. because of resemblance to a physical blemish (cf. ἄμωμος, 1Pe.1:19, and see Hort., in l); metaphorically, of licentious persons, 2Pe.2:13.† (AS)

G3489.strongs_def: ναυαγέω, -ῶ (ναῦς, + ἄγνυμι, to break) to suffer shipwreck: 2Co.11:25; metaphorically, before περὶ τ. πίστιν, 1Ti.1:19.† (AS)

G3493.strongs_def: Ναχώρ, ὁ indecl. (Heb. נָחוֹר), Nahor: Luk.3:34.† (AS)

G3496.strongs_def: Νεάπολις, -εως, ἡ Rec. for Νέα Πόλις (WH), the more frequently form (LS, see word), Neapolis, a maritime city of Macedonia: Act.16:11.† (AS)

G3504.strongs_def: νεό-φυτος, -ον (νέος, φύω) [in LXX: Job.14:9, Psa.144:12, Isa.5:7 (נֶטַע), Psa.128:3 (שְׁתִל)* ;] newly planted (LXX). Metaphorical, as subst., ὁ ν., a new convert, neophyte, novice: 1Ti.3:6† (AS)

G3512.strongs_def: νεωτερικός, -ή, -όν (νεώτερος), [in LXX: 3Ma.4:8 * ;] = νεανικός, youthful, esp. of qualities: ἐπιθυμίαι, 2Ti.2:22 (Polyb.).† (AS)

G3513.strongs_def: νή particle of affirmation employed in oaths, [in LXX: see τ. ὑγίειαν, Gen.42:15-16 (חַי) * ;] by: with accusative, 1Co.15:31.† (AS)

G3515.strongs_def: νηπιάζω (νήπιος), (Hippocr., = νηπιαχεύω, Hom.) to be a babe: 1Co.14:20.† (AS)

G3518.strongs_def: Νηρεί (Rec. -ρί), ὁ, indecl. (Heb. נֵרִיָּה), Neri: Luk.3:27.† (AS)

G3525.strongs_def: νήφω to be sober, abstain from wine; metaphorically, of moral alertness, to be sober, calm, circumspect: 1Th.5:6 5:8, 2Ti.4:5 (see Ellic., in l), 1Pe.1:13 4:7 5:8 (cf. ἐκ-, ἐκ-νήφω, and see MM, xvii).† SYN.: ἀγρυπνέω, γρηγορέω (AS)

G3529.strongs_def: νίκη, -ης, ἡ [in LXX: 1Ch.29:11 (נֶצַח), frequently in 1-4 Mac ;] victory: 1Jn.5:4.† (AS)

G3534.strongs_def: νῖκος, -ους, τό late form of νίκη, [in LXX: La 3:18 (נֶצַח), I Est.3:9, 2Ma.10:38, 4Ma.17:12; εἰς ν. (instead of εἰς τέλος, Job.14:20), 2Ki.2:26, Job.36:7, Amo.1:11 8:7, Jer.3:5, La 5:20 (נֶצַח, as נ֝ in Syr., = victory)* ;] victory: Mat.12:20 (Isa.42:3, LXX ἀλήθεια), 1Co.15:54 (Isa.25:8, Aq., Th.), 1Co.15:55 (Hos.13:14, LXX δίκη), 1Co.15:57.† (AS)

G3542.strongs_def: νομή, -ῆς, ἡ (νέμω, to pasture), [in LXX chiefly for מִרְעֶה, also for נָוֶה, etc. ;] __1. a pasture, pasturage: figuratively, Jhn.10:9 __2. a grazing, feeding; metaphorically, of a spreading sore, 2Ti.2:17 (Polyb.).† (AS)

G3545.strongs_def: νομίμως adv. (νόμιμος, conformable to law), [in LXX: 4Ma.6:18 * ;] rightly, lawfully: 1Ti.1:8, 2Ti.2:5.† (AS)

G3552.strongs_def: νοσέω, -ῶ (νόσος), [in LXX (metaphorically): Wis.17:8 * ;] to be sick: metaphorically, of mental ailment, before περί, 1Ti.6:4 (cf. Plat., Mor., 546 d).† (AS)

G3574.strongs_def: νυχθήμερος, -α, -ον (νύξ, ἡμέρα, see B1., § 28, 4), lasting a night and a day; as subst., (τὸ) ν., a night and a day: 2Co.11:25 (pl., Or. Sib., 8, 203).† (AS)

G3580.strongs_def: ξενοδοχέω late Gk. for -κέω (ξένος, δέχομαι), to entertain strangers: 1Ti.5:10.† (AS)

G3615.strongs_def: οἰκιακός (in Plut., al., -ειακός), ή, όν (οἰκία), = οἰκεῖος belonging to the household, one's own: Mat.10:36; opposite to οἰκοδεσπότης, Mat.10:25.† (AS)

G3620.strongs_def: οἰκοδομία, -ας, ἡ (οἰκοδομέω), the act of building: metaphorically, 1Ti.1:4 (BE for οἰκοδομία, which see).† (AS)

G3621.strongs_def: οἰκονομέω, -ῶ (οἰκονόμος), [in LXX: Psa.112:5 (כּוּל pilp.), 2Ma.3:14 * ;] to manage as house-steward, be a steward: absol., Luk.16:2; hence, generally (see: οἰκονομία), to manage, regulate, arrange (cl., 2Mac, Lc., 3Ma.3:2 R).† (AS)

G3632.strongs_def: οἰνοφλυγία, -ας, ἡ (φλύω, to bubble up, overflow), cf. -γέω, Deu.21:20 drunkenness, debauchery: 1Pe.4:3.† SYN.: see: κραιπάλη (AS)
G3632.derivation: from 3631 and a form of the base of 5397

G3639.strongs_def: ὄλεθρος, -ον (ὄλλυμι, to destroy), [in LXX for שֹׁד. שָׁדַד, etc. ;] ruin, destruction, death: 1Th.5:3, 1Ti.6:9; αἰώνιος, 2Th.1:9 (L, txt., ὀλέθριος, which see); εἰς ὄ. τῆς σαρκός, for physical discipline, to destroy carnal lusts, 1Co.5:5.† (AS)
G3639.derivation: from a primary ollumi (to destroy, a prolonged form)

G3642.strongs_def: ὀλιγόφυχος, -ον [in LXX: Isa.35:4 (מָהַר ni.), etc. ;] faint-hearted: 1Th.5:14.† (AS)

G3644.strongs_def: ὀλοθρευτής (Rec. όλ-), -οῦ, ὁ (ὀλοθρεύω), a destroyer: 1Co.10:10 (not elsewhere).† (AS)

G3651.strongs_def: ὁλοτελής, -ές (ὅλος, τίλος), complete, perfect.. 1Th.5:23.† SYN.: ὁλόκληρος (which see), τέλειος. "As regards meaning, ὁλόκληρος can hardly be distinguished from ὁλοτελής though, in accordance with its derivation, it draws more special attention to the several parts to which the wholeness spoken of extends, no part being wanting or lacking in completeness" (M, Th., 78) (AS)

G3657.strongs_def: όμιλία, -ας, ή (όμιλος), [in LXX: Exo.21:10 (עוֹנָה), al. ;] company, association: 1Co.15:33.† (AS)

G3662.strongs_def: ὁμοιάζω (ὅμοιος), to be like: Mat.23:27 (L, Tr., txt., WH, mg.) Mat.26:73 (WH, mg.) (not found elsewhere. cf. παρ-ομοιάζω.) † (AS)

G3672.strongs_def: ὁμολογουμένως adv. (ὁμ oλογέω), [in LXX: 4Ma.6:31 4Mac 7:16 4Mac 16:1 * ;] __1. as agreed, conformably with. __2. confessedly, by common consent: 1Ti.3:16.† (AS)

G3675.strongs_def: ὁμόφρων, -ον (ὁμός, φρήν), = ὁμόνοος, agreeing, of one mind: 1Pe.3:8.† (AS)

G3695.strongs_def: ὁπλίζω (ὅπλον), [in Sm.: Jer.52:25 * ;] to make ready, equip; of soldiers, to arm. Mid., to arm oneself; figuratively, ἔννοιαν: 1Pe.4:1 (cf. θράσος ὁ., Soph., Elec., 995), (cf. καθ-ὁπλίζω).† (AS)

G3718.strongs_def: ὀρθοτομέω, -ῶ (- ὀρθός, τέμνω), [in LXX: Pro.3:6 11:6 (יָשַׁר pi.)* ;] to cut straight, as a road (τ. ὁδούς, figuratively, Pr, ll with). Metaphorical, τ. λόγον τ. ἀληθείας, 2Ti.2:15 (V. Ellic. and CGT, in l; not found elsewhere).† (AS)
G3718.derivation: from a compound of 3717 and the base of 5114

G3743.strongs_def: ὁσίως (ὅσιος), adv., [in LXX: 3Ki.8:61, Wis.6:10 * ;] piously, holily: ὁ. καὶ δικαίως κ. ἀμέμπτως (on the distinction here between these synonyms, see M, Th., 24 f.), 1Th.2:10.† (AS)

G3749.strongs_def: ὀστράκινος -η, -ον (ὄστρακον, an earthen vessel or potsherd), [in LXX chiefly for חֶרֶשׂ ;] made of clay, earthen: 2Co.4:7, 2Ti.2:20.† (AS)
G3749.derivation: from ostrakon [\"oyster\"] (a tile, i.e. terra cotta)

G3750.strongs_def: ὄσφρησις, -εως, ἡ (ὀσφραίνομαι, to smell), the sense of smell, smell­ing: 1Co.12:17.† (AS)

G3794.strongs_def: ὀχύρωμα, -τος, τό (ὀχυρόω, to fortify, make firm), [in LXX for מִבְצָר, etc. ;] a stronghold, fortress (Psa.89:40, Nam.3:12, 14 al.); in LXX and NT, also metaphorically of that in which confidence is placed (Pro.10:29 21:22, al.): 2Co.10:4.† (AS)
G3794.derivation: from a remote derivative of 2192 (meaning to fortify, through the idea of holding safely)

G3812.strongs_def: παιδιόθεν (παιδίον), adv., [in LXX: Gen.47:3 * ;] = cl. ἐκ παιδός, παιδίον, from childhood: Mrk.9:21.† (AS)

G3815.strongs_def: παίζω (παῖς), [in LXX: Gen.21:9 26:8, Exo.32:6 (צָחַק pi.); and more frequently (Jdg.16:25, al.) for (שָׂחַק pi. ;] prop., to play as a child, hence, generally, to play (as with singing and dancing) : 1Co.10:7 (LXX) (cf. ἐμ-παίζω).† (AS)

G3818.strongs_def: Πακατιανή, -ῆς, ἡ Pacatiana, the Western part of the Province of Phrygia, as constituted in 4/A.D.: 1Ti subscr. (Rec.).† (AS)
G3818.derivation: feminine of an adjective of uncertain derivation

G3835.strongs_def: πανοῦργος, -ον [in LXX chiefly for עָרוּם ;] ready to do anything; __(a) in cl., chiefly in bad sense, knavish, crafty: 2Co.12:16; __(b) in good sense, skilful, clever (Pro.13:1 28:2).† (AS)

G3836.strongs_def: πανταχόθεν adv., [in LXX: 4Ma.13:1 4Mac 15:32 * ;] from all sides: Mrk.1:45, Rec.† (AS)

G3859.strongs_def: παρα-δια-τριβή, -ῆς, ἡ useless wrangling: seel. in Rec. for διαπαρατριβή (which see), 1Ti.6:5.† δια-παρα-τριβή, -ῆς, ἡ (παρατριβή, friction, irritation) mutual irritation (Field, Notes, 211), wrangling: 1Ti.6:5 (Rec. παραδιατριβή).† (AS)

G3866.strongs_def: παρα-θήκη, -ης, ἡ (παρατίθημι), [in LXX: Lev.6:2, 4 (Lev 5:21, 23) (פִּקָּדוֹן), and in Tob 10:13, 2Ma.3:10 2Mac 3:15, seel. for παρακαταθήκη (which see) * ;] a deposit or trust: 1Ti.6:20, 2Ti.1:12 1:14 (for exx. of this form, see MM, Exp., iii, xviii).† (AS)

G3872.strongs_def: παρα-κατα-θήκη, -ης, ἡ (παρακατατίθημι) [in LXX: Exo.22:8, 11 (מְלָאכָה), and elsewhere as seel. for παραθήκη, which see ;] more usual than its variant in Gk. writers for a trust or deposit: 1Ti.6:20, 2Ti.1:14, Rec.† (AS)

G3889.strongs_def: παραμυθία, -ας, ἡ (παραμυθέομαι) [in LXX: Est.8:13, Wis.19:12 * ;] __1. encouragement, exhortation. __2. comfort, consolation: 1Co.14:3 .† SYN.: παράκλησις (AS)

G3891.strongs_def: παρα-νομέω, ῶ [in LXX for הָלַל, etc., chiefly in Pss and 2Mac ;] to be a παράνομος, to transgress the law: Act.23:3.† (AS)

G3892.strongs_def: παρανομία, -ας, ἡ [in LXX: Psa.37:7 (מְזִמָּה), etc. ;] law-breaking, transgression: 2Pe.2:16.† (AS)

G3901.strongs_def: παρα-ρρέω [in LXX: Isa.44:4 (יָבַל), Pro.3:21 * ;] to flow by, drift away, slip away: Heb.2:1.† (AS)

G3907.strongs_def: παρα-τήρησις, -εως, ἡ [in Aq.: Exo.12:42 (see: παρατηρέω) * ;] obser­vation: Luk.17:20 (Polyb., Plut., al.).† (AS)

G3909.strongs_def: παρα-τυγχάνω to happen to be near or present: Act.17:17.† (AS)

G3910.strongs_def: παρ-αυτίκα adv. (πάραυτα = παρ ̓ αὐτά, sc. τὰ πράγματα) [in LXX: Psa.70:3, Tob.4:14 * ;] __1. immediately. __2. C. subst., to express brief duration (cf. ἡ π. λαμπρότης, Thuc., ii, 64), momentary, for a moment: 2Co.4:17.† (AS)

G3912.strongs_def: παρα-φρονέω (ιαρά, φρήν), [in LXX: Zec.7:11 (סָרַר)* ;] to be beside oneself, be deranged: 2Co.11:23.† (AS)

G3919.strongs_def: παρ-εισ-άγω __1. to lead in by one's side, bring forward, introduce. __2. In late writers, to introduce or bring in secretly: 2Pe.2:1.† (AS)

G3923.strongs_def: παρ-εισ-φέρω to bring in or supply besides: σπουδὴν π. (late Gk. for cl. σ. ποιεῖσθαι; cf. Deiss., BS, 361), 2Pe.1:5.† (AS)

G3932.strongs_def: παρθενία, -ας, ἡ (παρθένος), [in LXX: Jer.3:4 (נָעוּר), Sir.15:2 42:10, 4Ma.18:8 * ;] virginity: Luk.2:36.† (AS)

G3938.strongs_def: πάρ-οδος, -ου, ἡ [in LXX: Gen.38:14 (דֶּרֶךְ), etc. ;] a passing or passage: ἐν π., in passing, 1Co.16:7.† (AS)

G3950.strongs_def: παρ-οργισμός, -οῦ, ὁ (παροργίζω), [in LXX: 3Ki.15:30, 4Ki.23:26 (כַּעַס); 4Ki.19:3, Neh.9:18, 26 (נְאָצָה); Jer.21:5 A (קֶצֶף) * ;] irritation ("distinguished from ὀργή as implying a less permanent state"; ICC, Eph., 140; and see Tr., Syn., § xxxvii) : Eph.4:26.† (AS)

G3959.strongs_def: Πάταρα, -ων, τὰ Patara, a maritime city of Lycia: Act.21:1.† (AS)

G3964.strongs_def: πατρολῴας (-αλῴας, Rec.; in cl. -αλοίας, see Bl., § 3, 3; 6, 2, and cf. μητρολῴας), -ου, ὁ (πατήρ + ἀλοιάω, to smite), __(a) a parricide: 1Ti.1:9 (Av, R, txt.); __(b) a smiter of his father : ib. (R, mg.).† (AS)
G3964.derivation: from 3962 and the same as the latter part of 3389

G3967.strongs_def: πατρικίς, -ή, -όν (πατήρ), [in LXX for אָב, Gen.50:8, al. ;] paternal, ancestral: Gal.1:14.† (AS)

G3970.strongs_def: πατρο-παρά-δοτος, -ον (πατήρ, παραδίδωμι), handed down from one's fathers, inherited: 1Pe.1:18 (Diod., al.).† (AS)
G3970.derivation: from 3962 and a derivative of 3860 (in the sense of handing over or down)

G3978.strongs_def: πεζεύω (πεζός) to travel on foot or by land: Act.20:13.† (AS)

G3981.strongs_def: πειθός (πιθός, WH), -ή, -όν (πείθω), = cl. πιθανός, persuasive: 1Co.2:4 (not found elsewhere).† (AS)

G3993.strongs_def: πένης, -ητος, ὁ (πένομαι, to work for one's daily bread), [in LXX for אֶבְיוֹן, עָנִי, דַּל, etc. ;] one who works for his living, a labourer, a poor man: 2Co.9:9.† SYN.: πτωχός, properly a beggar and implying deeper poverty than π. (see Tr., Syn., § xxxvi, Abbott, Essays, 78) (AS)
G3993.derivation: from a primary peno (to toil for daily subsistence)

G4020.strongs_def: περι-εργάζομαι [in LXX: Wis.8:5 א1, Sir.3:23 * ;] __1. to waste one's labour about a thing. __2. to be a busybody: 2Th.3:11 (cf. Plat., Apol., 19 B).† (AS)

G4025.strongs_def: περί-θεσις, -εως, ἡ (περιτίθημι), [in Sm.: Psa.32:9 * ;] a putting around, putting on: 1Pe.3:3.† (AS)

G4027.strongs_def: περι-κάθαρμα, -τος, τό (περικαθαίρω, to purify on all sides or completely, Deu.18:10, Jos.5:4, 4Ma.1:29*), [in LXX: Pro.21:18 (כֹּפֶר)* ;] __1. a victim, expiation (Pr, l.with). __2. refuse, rubbish: pl., 1Co.4:13 (see ICC, in l).† (AS)

G4035.strongs_def: περι-λείπομαι depon. mid, and pass., [in LXX: 2Ch.34:21 A (שָׁאַר ni.), 2Ma.1:31 2Mac 8:14, 4Ma.12:6 4Mac 13:18 * ;] to be left remaining, remain over, survive: 1Th.4:15 4:17† (AS)

G4044.strongs_def: περι-πείρω to put on a spit, hence, to pierce: metaphorically, ἑαυτὸν . . . ὀδύναις, 1Ti.6:10.† (AS)

G4067.strongs_def: περί-ψημα, -τος, τό (περιψράω, to wipe off all round), [in LXX: Tob.5:18 * ;] that which is wiped off, offscouring: metaphorically (assoc. with περικάθαρμα, which see), 1Co.4:13 (and so prob., To, l.with, as EV; but see Thayer, see word, for the meaning expiation, ransom, in To; and cf. LS, see word κάθαρμα; Lft., Notes, 200 f., and on Ign., Eph., 8).† (AS)
G4067.derivation: from a comparative of 4012 and psao (to rub)

G4068.strongs_def: περπερεύοραι (περπερος, vainglorious) to boast or vaunt oneself: 1Co.13:4 (elsewhere. only in Antonin.; see Abbott, Essays, 87).† (AS)
G4068.derivation: middle voice from perperos (braggart, perhaps by reduplication of the base of 4008)

G4070.strongs_def: πέρυσι adv. (πέρας), last year, a year ago: ἀπὸ π. (as in π. see Deiss., BS, 221; LAE, 70), 2Co.8:10 9:2.† (AS)

G4086.strongs_def: πιθανολογία, -ας, ἡ (πιθανός, persuasive, plausible), in cl. (Plat), the use of probable arguments, as opposite to demonstration (ἀπόδειξις); hence, persuasive speech: Col.2:4 (see ICC, in l).† (AS)
G4086.derivation: from a compound of a derivative of 3982 and 3056

G4090.strongs_def: πικρῶς adv. (πικρός), [in LXX for מַר, מָרַר pi. ;] bitterly: metaphorically, (cf. πικρὸν δάκρυον, Hom.), ἔκλαυσε π., Mat.26:75, Luk.22:62 (see MM, xviii, see word παρακολουθέω).† (AS)

G4104.strongs_def: πιστόω, -ῶ (πιστός), [in LXX chiefly for אָמֵן ni. ;] to make trustworthy (Thuc., 3Ki.1:36), hence, to establish (1Ch.17:14). Pass. and mid., to be assured of: with accusative of thing(s), 2Ti.3:14.† (AS)

G4112.strongs_def: πλαστός, -ή, -όν (πλάσσω), __1. formed, moulded (Hes., Plat., al.). __2. Metaphorical, made up, fabricated, feigned (Hdt., Xen., al.): 2Pe.2:3.† (AS)

G4117.strongs_def: πλέγμα, -τος, τό (πλέκω), [in Aq., Th.: Isa.28:5 * ;] what is woven or twisted (as basket-work, nets, etc.); a braiding (sc. τριχῶν, cf. 1Pe.3:3) : pl., 1Ti.2:9.† (AS)

G4122.strongs_def: πλεονεκτέω, -ῶ (πλεονέκτης, which see), [in LXX: Hab.2:9, Eze.22:27 (בָּצַע), Jdg.4:11 B* ;] __1. intrans., to have more, to have an advantage (cl., with genitive of person(s)). __2. Trans., in late writers (see M, Pr., 65), to over­reach, defraud: with accusative of person(s), 2Co.7:2 12:17-18; ἐν τ. πράγματιι, 1Th.4:6 (see M, Th., in l); pass., 2Co.2:11 (as also in cl.; see LS, see word).† (AS)
