G4148.strongs_def: πλουτίζω (πλοῦτος), [in LXX chiefly for עָשַׁר hi. ;] to make rich, enrich: with accusative of person(s), pass., 2Co.9:11. Metaphorical, of spiritual riches, with accusative: of person(s), 2Co.6:10; before ἐν, pass., 1Co.1:5.† (AS)

G4162.strongs_def: ποίησις, -εως, ἡ (ποιέω) [in LXX chiefly for מַעֲשֶׂה and cognate forms ;] __1. a making (Hdt., Thuc., al.). __2. a doing (Sir.19:18 51:19): Jas.1:25.† (AS)

G4180.strongs_def: πολυλογία, -ας, ἡ [in LXX: Pro.10:19 (דָּבָר רֹב)* ;] much speaking, loquacity: Mat.6:7.† (AS)

G4200.strongs_def: πορισμός, -ου, ὁ (πορίζω, to procure), [in LXX: Wis.13:19 14:2 * ;] __1. a providing. __2. a means of gain: 1Ti.6:5-6 (Polyb., al.).† (AS)
G4200.derivation: from a derivative of poros (a way, i.e. means)

G4216.strongs_def: ποταμο-φόρητος, -ον carried away by a stream: Rev.12:15 (for two exx. in π., see MM, xxi).† (AS)

G4223.strongs_def: Ποτίολοι, -ων, οἱ Puteoli (mod. Pozzuoli), a city on the Bay of Naples: Act.28:13.† (AS)

G4224.strongs_def: πότος, -ου, ὁ (πίνω), [in LXX chiefly for מִשְׁתֶּה ;] a drinking bout, carousal: 1Pe.4:3.† SYN.: see: κραιπάλη (AS)

G4227.strongs_def: Πούδης (in π., genitive -εντος, see Zorell, see word), ὁ (Latin) Pudens: 2Ti.4:21.† (AS)

G4230.strongs_def: πραγματία (Rec. -εία, as in cl.), -ας, ἡ (πραγματεύομαι) [in LXX for חֲשַׁל, etc. ;] __1. careful application, hard work. __2. business, occupation: pl., 2Ti.2:4.† (AS)

G4251.strongs_def: Πρίσκα, -ας, ἡ (Lat.), and Πρίσκιλλα, -ης, ἡ, Prisca: Rom_16:3, 1Co_16:19, 2Ti_4:19; Priscilla: Act_18:2; Act_18:18; Act_18:26; the wife of Aquila, vs. Ἀκύλας.† (AS)

G4255.strongs_def: προ-αιρέω, -ῶ [in LXX: for חָשַׁק, etc. ;] to bring forth or forward. Most frequently in mid., to take by choice, prefer, propose: 2Co.9:7.† (AS)

G4269.strongs_def: πρό-γονος, -ον (προγίνομαι), [in LXX: Est.4:17, Sir.8:4, al. ;] __1. born before. __2. As subst., in pl., οἱ π., ancestors, forefathers: 2Ti.1:3; of living parents (so Plat.), 1Ti.5:4.† (AS)

G4278.strongs_def: προ-ενάρχομαι to begin before: 2Co.8:6; with accusative, τὸ θέλειν, 2Co.8:10 (not elsewhere).† (AS)

G4290.strongs_def: προθύμως [in LXX: 2Ch.29:34 (יָשָׁר לֵבָב), Tob.7:8, al. ;] eagerly, readily, with a ready mind: 1Pe.5:2.† (AS)

G4299.strongs_def: πρό-κριμα, -τος, τό (cl. προκρίνειν, 1. to prefer. 2. to judge beforehand), pre-judging, prejudice: 1Ti.5:21 (see Cremer, 378).† (AS)

G4303.strongs_def: προ-μαρτύρομαι to protest beforehand (cf. μαρτύρομαι, and V. Hort, in l): 1Pe.1:11 (elsewhere only in Theod. Met., xiv/AD.).† (AS)

G4310.strongs_def: to suffer first or beforehand , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.: to be ill-treated before , ὑπό τινος (Thucydides):—;also, ἀγαθὸν πρ. (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G4312.strongs_def: προπετής, -ές (προπίπτω), [in LXX: Pro.10:14 (אֱוִיל) Pro.13:3 (פָּשַׂק) Sir.9:18 * ;] falling forwards, headlong. Metaphorical, precipitate, rash, reck­less: of persons, 2Ti.3:4; of things, Act.19:36.† (AS)

G4315.strongs_def: προ-σάββατον, -ου, τό [in LXX: Psa.92:1-15 title. א (שַׁבָּת) שַׁבָּת) Psa.93:1-5 title., Jdth.8:6 * ;] the day before the Sabbath: Mrk.15:42 (L, Tr., txt., πρὸς σ.).† (AS)

G4319.strongs_def: προσ-αιτέω, -ῶ [in LXX: Job.27:14 * ;] __1. to ask besides. __2. to continue asking; hence, to importune, beg, ask alms: Jhn.9:8.† (AS)

G4322.strongs_def: προσ-αναπληρόω, -ῶ [in LXX: Wis.19:4 * ;] to fill up by adding to, to supply fully: 2Co.9:12 11:9.† (AS)

G4332.strongs_def: προσεδρεύω (πρόσεδρος, sitting near), [in LXX: 1Ma.11:40 * ;] __1. to sit near. __2. to attend regularly: with dative, 1Co.9:13, Rec. (see: παρεδρεύω).† παρ-εδρεύω [in LXX: Pro.1:21 8:3 * ;] to sit constantly beside, attend constantly (cf. MM, xix): τ. θυσιαστηρίω, 1Co.9:13.† (AS)
G4332.derivation: from a compound of 4314 and the base of 1476

G4349.strongs_def: προσκοπή, -ῆς, ή (προσκόπτω), [in Gr. Ven.: Pro.16:18 (כִּשָּׁלוֹן) * ;] an occasion of stumbling, offence: 2Co.6:3.† (AS)

G4358.strongs_def: προσ-ορμίζω (ὅρμος, an anchorage), to bring a ship to anchor at; usually in mid., to come to anchor near, and so pass. in late writers (Ael., Dio Cass.): Mrk.6:53.† (AS)
G4358.derivation: from 4314 and a derivative of the same as 3730 (meaning to tie [anchor] or lull)

G4381.strongs_def: προσωπο-λήμπτης (Rec. -λήπτης, see Bl., § 6, 8), -ου, ὁ (πρόσωπον λαμβάνειν, see: πρόσωπον), a respecter of persons: Act.10:34 (on this group of cognate forms, see Mayor, da., 78 f.; and cf. Thackeray, Gr., 44).† (AS)

G4409.strongs_def: πρωτεύω (πρῶτος) [in LXX: Est.5:11, 2Ma.6:18 2Mac 13:15 * ;] to be first, pre-eminent, have the first place: Col.1:18.† (AS)

G4415.strongs_def: πρωτοτόκια, -ων, τά (πρωτότοκος) [in LXX (with seel. -εῖα, -εία): Gen.25:31 ff. Gen.27:36, Deu.21:17, 1Ch.5:1 (בְּכוֹרָה) * ;] the rights of the first-born, birthright (= cl. ἡ πρεσβεία): Heb.12:16.† (AS)

G4421.strongs_def: πτηνός, -ή, -όν (πέτομαι), [in Aq.: Job.5:7 * ;] winged; as subst., π., birds: 1Co.15:39.† (AS)

G4423.strongs_def: πτόησις, -εως, ἡ (πτοέω) [in LXX: Pro.3:25 (פַּחַד), Sir 50:4 א1, 1Ma.3:25 R * ;] a fluttering, excitement, caused by any emotion, but esp. by fear, hence, terror: φοβεῖσθαι πτόησιν, to be afraid with (cogn. accusative) or of any terror (see ICC, in l): 1Pe.3:6.† (AS)

G4433.strongs_def: πτωχεύω (πτωχός), [in LXX: Jdg.6:6, Psa.79:8 (דָּלַל); Jdg.14:15 A, Pro.23:21 (יָרַשׁ); Psa.34:10 (רוּשׁ), Tob.4:21 * ;] __1. to be a beggar, to beg (so chiefly in cl.). __2. to be poor as a beggar, to be destitute, poor: opposite to πλούσιος ὤν, 2Co.8:9.† (AS)

G4438.derivation: from a derivative of the same as 4435

G4452.strongs_def: πω enclit. part., yet, see: μή-πω, μηδέ-πω, οὔ-πω, οὐδέ-πω, πώ-ποτε πώ-ποτε adv., ever yet: Luk.19:30, Jhn.1:18 5:37 6:35 8:33, 1Jn.4:12.† (AS)
G4452.derivation: another form of the base of (4458)

G4463.strongs_def: ῥαβδίζω (ῥάβδος), [in LXX: Jdg.6:11 Rut.2:17 (חָבַט) * ;] to beat with a rod: Act.16:22, 2Co.11:25.† (AS)

G4490.strongs_def: ῥητῶς adv. (ῥητός, stated, specified), in stated terms, expressly: 1Ti.4:1.† (AS)

G4493.strongs_def: ῥιπή, ῆς, ἡ (ῥίπτω), poët. in cl., any rapid movement such as the throw or flight of a javelin, the rush of wind or flame, the flapping of wings, the twinkling of lights; ῥ. ὀφθαλμοῦ, the twinkling of an eye: 1Co.15:52 (L, mg., ῥοπή, which see).† (AS)

G4494.strongs_def: ῥιπίζω (ῥιπίς, a fan) [in LXX: Dan LXX 2:35 (נְשָׂא) * ;] primarily, to fan a fire, hence generally, to make a breeze (Plut., al.). In pass. (cf. Philo, de inter. round., 24), to be tossed or blown by the wind: of waves, ἀνεμιζομένῳ καὶ ῥιπιζομένῳ, blown and raised with the wind (Hort, in l), Jas.1:6.† (AS)
G4494.derivation: from a derivative of 4496 (meaning a fan or bellows)

G4500.strongs_def: ῥοιζηδόν adv. (ῥοῖζος, the whistling of an arrow), with rushing sound (as of roaring flames): 2Pe.3:10.† (AS)
G4500.derivation: from a derivative of rhoizos (a whir)

G4509.strongs_def: ῥύπος, -ου, ὁ [in LXX: Isa.4:4 (צוֹאָה), Job.14:4 (טָמֵא), etc. ;] dirt, filth: 1Pe.3:21.† (AS)

G4517.strongs_def: ῥώννυμι [in LXX: 2Ma.9:20 2Mac 11:21 2Mac 11:28 2Mac 11:33 2Mac 11:1-38; 3Ma.6:1-41 * ;] to strengthen; most frequently in pf., ἔρρωμαι, to put forth strength, be strong, hence, often in imperat., ἔρρωσο, ἔρρωσθε, farewell (Lat. vale): Act.15:29 23:30 Rec., R, mg.† (AS)
G4517.derivation: prolongation from rhoomai (to dart, probably akin to 4506)

G4525.strongs_def: σαίνω __1. prop. (Hom., al.), of dogs, to wag the tail, fawn. __2. Metaphorical, of persons, with accusative, to fawn upon, flatter, beguile: pass., 1Th.3:3 (for conjectural emendations of the text, see ICC, and M, Th., in l).† (AS)

G4527.strongs_def: Σαλά, ὁ indecl. (Heb. שֶׁלַח), Sala, Shalah: Luk.3:32 (R, txt., Σαλμών, which see), Luk.3:35.† (AS)

G4534.strongs_def: Σαλμώνη, -ης, ἡ Salmone, a promontory of Crete: Act.27:7.† (AS)

G4553.strongs_def: σαργάνη, -ης, ἡ __1. a plaited rope (Æsch.). __2. a hamper, a basket made of ropes: 2Co.11:33.† (AS)

G4560.strongs_def: σάρκινος, -η, -ον (σάρξ), [in LXX: 2Ch.32:8, Eze.11:19 36:26 (בָּשָׂר), Est.4:17, Pro.24:23 (Pro.29:27) * ;] = Lat. carneus (the termination -ινος denoting the substance or material of a thing; see Tr., Syn., § LXXii; Lft., Notes, 184; and for illustrations from π., see MM, xxii), of the flesh, of flesh, fleshy (Plat., Arist., Plut., al.): Rom.7:14, 1Co.3:1, 2Co.3:3, Heb.7:16. (Rec. has -ικός in all these passages except 2Co.3:3, but the evidence is decisive against it.)† SYN.: σαρκικός, q.v (AS)

G4566.strongs_def: Satan , i. e. an adversary, enemy : name for the Devil , (New Testament) Hebr. word. (ML)

G4577.strongs_def: σειρά, -ᾶς, ἡ [in LXX: Jdg.16:13-14, 19 (מַחְלָפָה), Pro.5:22 (חֶבֶל) * ;] __1. (a) a cord; __(b) a chain (cf. Pr., l.with): σειραὶ ζόφου, 2Pe.2:4, Rec., R, mg. (see: σειρός). __2. a lock of hair (Jg, ll. with).† (AS)
G4577.derivation: probably from 4951 through its congener eiro (to fasten, akin to 138)

G4593.strongs_def: σημειόω, -ῶ (σημεῖον), [in LXX: Psa.4:6 (נָשָׂא)* ;] to mark, note. Mid., to note for oneself: 2Th.3:14 (frequently in π.; see ICC, M, Th., in l).† (AS)

G4598.strongs_def: σητό-βρωτος, -ον (οής, βιβρώσκω), [in LXX: Job.13:28 (אָכַל עָשׁ) * ;] moth-eaten: Jas.5:2.† (AS)

G4599.strongs_def: σθενόω, -ῶ (σθένος, strength), to strengthen: with accusative, 1Pe.5:10 (Hesych.).† (AS)
G4599.derivation: from sthenos (bodily vigour, probably akin to the base of 2476)

G4607.strongs_def: σικάριος, -ου, ὁ (Lat.; sica, a dagger carried under their clothing by the Sicarii), a bandit, assassin, one of the Sicarii (FlJ, B.J., ii, 17, 6, al.): Act.21:38.† (AS)

G4610.strongs_def: Σιλουανός (in MSS also Σιλβανός, a form frequently in π.), -οῦ, ὁ, Silvanus, latinized name of Silas: 2Co.1:19, 1Th.1:1, 2Th.1:1, 1Pe.5:12.† (AS)

G4629.strongs_def: σκέπασμα, -τος, τό (σκεπάζω, to cover), a covering, esp. clothing: 1Ti.6:8.† (AS)
G4629.derivation: from a derivative of skepas (a covering; perhaps akin to the base of 4649 through the idea of noticeableness)

G4635.strongs_def: σκηνοποιός, -όν (σκηνή, ποιέω), making tents; as subst., ὁ σ., a tent-maker: Act.18:3.† (AS)

G4636.strongs_def: σκῆνος, -ους, τό [in LXX: Wis.9:15 * ;] = σκηνή, a tent, tabernacle (C.1., 3071). Metaphorical, of the body as the tabernacle of the soul: 2Co.5:1 5:4.† (AS)

G4647.strongs_def: σκόλοψ, -οπος, ὁ [in LXX: Num.33:55 (שֵׂךְ), Hos.2:6 (8) (סִיר), Eze.28:24 (סִלּוֹן), Sir.43:19 * ;] anything pointed, esp. __1. in cl., a stake __2. In Hellenistic vernacular, a thorn (cf. LXX, ll. with): σ. τῇ σαρκί, 2Co.12:7 (cf. MM, i., xxiii; DB, iii, 700 f.; Deiss., St. Paul, 62 f.; Field, Notes, 187).† (AS)
G4647.derivation: perhaps from the base of 4628 and 3700

G4661.strongs_def: σκῦλον (Rec. σκύλον), -ου, τό [in LXX chiefly for שָׁלָל ;] mostly in pl., σκίλα, arms stripped from a foe, spoils: Luk.11:22.† (AS)

G4664.strongs_def: σμαράγδινος (σμάραγδος, which see), __1. of emerald (Luc., V.H., ii, 11). __2. As in π. (Deiss., BS, 267), emerald-green: Rev.4:3 (for the construction, see Swete, in l; Zorell, see word).† (AS)

G4665.strongs_def: σμάραγδος, -ου, ἡ (and in late writers also ὁ), [in LXX: Exo.28:9 (שֹׁהַם) Exo.36:17 (Exo.39:10) (בָּרֶקֶת), Eze.28:13 (יַהֲלֹם), etc. ;] emerald or other trans parent green stone (LS, see word; DB, iv, 620; Swete, Ap., 67, 288): Rev.21:19.† (AS)

G4679.strongs_def: σοφίζω (σοφός), [in LXX chiefly for חָכָם ;] to make wise, instruct: with accusative of person(s), 2Ti.3:15 (cf. Psa.19:8 (Psa.119:98). As depon., -ομαι; __(a) intrans., to become wise (I2Ki.4:27 (3Ki.5:11), Ecc.2:15, and frequently in Sir.7:5, al.); __(b) trans., to invent, devise cleverly: pass., 2Pe.1:16 (cf. κατα-σοφίζομαι).† (AS)

G4701.strongs_def: σπορά, -ᾶς, ἡ (σπείρω), [in LXX: 4Ki.19:29 (זָרַע), 1Ma.10:30 * ;] __1. a sowing. __2. seedtime. __3. seed sown (of human offspring, Soph., Tr., 316, 420): 1Pe.1:23 (cf. σπέρμα, and see Milligan, NTD, 105 f.).† (AS)

G4705.strongs_def: σπουδαῖος, -α, -ον (σπουδή), [in LXX: Eze.41:25 * ;] in haste; hence, zealous, eager, diligent, earnest: before ἐν, 2Co.8:22; compar., -οτεροσς 2Co.8:17 (here in superl. sense, see Bl., § 44, 3) 2Co.8:22.† (AS)

G4706.strongs_def: - more earnestly diligently, seriously, earnestly than others), i.e. very promptly

G4722.strongs_def: στέγω (cf. Lat. tego), [in LXX: Sir.8:17 * ;] __1. prop., to cover closely, to protect by covering, esp. to keep water in or out (Soph., Plat., al.). __2. to cover, keep secret, conceal (Sir, l.with, Polyb., al.): 1Co.13:7, R, mg. __3. By covering to ward of, bear up under, endure (for exx., see, Lft., Notes, 40; M, Th., 36): 1Co.9:12 13:7, 1Th.3:1 3:5.† (AS)

G4724.strongs_def: στέλλω [in LXX (mid.): Mal.2:5 (חָתַת ni.), Pro.31:24 (26), Wis.7:14 14:1, 2Ma.5:1, 3Ma.1:19 3Mac 4:11 * ;] __1. prop., to set, place, arrange, fit out; hence, mid., to set oneself for, prepare (Wis, xi Mac, ll. with). __2. to bring together, gather up (in Hom. of furling sails), hence to restrain, check; mid., to restrain or withdraw oneself, hold aloof, avoid: 2Co.8:20; before ἀπό, 2Th.3:6 (cf. ἀπο-, ἐξ-απο-, συν-απο-, δια-, ἐπι-, κατα-, συ(ν)-, ὑπο-στέλλω).† (AS)
G4724.derivation: probably strengthened from the base of 2476

G4729.strongs_def: στενο-χωρέω, -ῶ (στενός + χῶρος, space) [in LXX: Jos.17:15 (אוּץ), Jdg.16:16 (אָלַץ pi.), Isa.28:19 (20) (קָצַר) Isa.49:19 (צָרַר), 4Ma.11:11 * ;] __1. to be straitened (cf. Isa.49:19); metaphorically, to be anxious (Hipp., al.). __2. In late writers, trans., to straiten, compress (LXX, Diod., al.; π. ap. MM, xxiii): pass., trop., 2Co.4:8 6:12.† (AS)

G4740.strongs_def: στηριγμός, -οῦ, ὁ (στηρίζω), [in Sm.: Isa.3:1 * ;] __1. a setting firmly, supporting. __2. fixedness, firmness, steadfastness: 2Pe.3:17.† (AS)

G4751.strongs_def: στόμαχος, -ου, ὁ (στόμα), prop., a mouth, an opening; __(a) in early Gk. writers, the throat; __(b) of the opening of the stomach (Arist.); __(with) in later writers (Plut., al.), the stomach: 1Ti.5:23.† (AS)

G4752.strongs_def: στρατεία (on the orthogr., see Deiss., BS, 181 f.), -ας, ἡ (οτρατεύω), [in LXX chiefly for צָבָא ;] an expedition, a campaign, warfare: metaphorically, 2Co.10:4 (-τιά, T), 1Ti.1:18.† (AS)

G4758.strongs_def: στρατολογέω, -ῶ (στρατός, λέγω), to levy a troop, enlist soldiers: 2Ti.2:4 (Diod., Plut., al.).† (AS)
G4758.derivation: from a compound of the base of 4756 and 3004 (in its original sense)

G4761.strongs_def: στρεβλόω, -ῶ (στρέφω), [in LXX: 2Ki.22:27 (פָּתַל hithp.), 3Ma.4:14, 4Ma.9:17 4Mac 12:4 4Mac 12:11 4Mac 15:14 * ;] to twist, torture. Metaphorical (cf. 2Ki, l.with), to twist or pervert language: 2Pe.3:16.† (AS)

G4764.strongs_def: στρῆνος, -ους, τό (cf. Lat. strenuus), [in LXX: 4Ki.19:28 (שַׁאֲנָן)* ;] insolent luxury, wantonness: Rev.18:3 (a late word, first found in a Comic poet, B.C. 300, see Kennedy, Sources, 41, cf. στρηνιάω).† (AS)

G4774.strongs_def: συν-γνώμη (Rec. συγγ-), -ης, ἡ (συγγιγνώσκω, (a) to agree with; (b) to pardon), [in LXX: Sir prol.14 (B1N1 cm.) 313, 2Mac 14:20* ;] __1. confession. __2. fellow feeling; hence, concession, allowance: 1Co.7:6 (see ICC, in l). __3. pardon.† (AS)

G4777.strongs_def: συν-κακοπαθέω (Rec. συγκ-), -ῶ, to bear evil treatment along with, take one's share of ill-treatment: 2Ti.2:3; with dative commod., τ. εὐαγγελίῳ, 2Ti.2:18.† (AS)

G4783.strongs_def: συν-κατά-θεσις (Rec συγκ-), -εως, ἡ (συνκατατίθημι) concord, agreement: 2Co.6:16 (Polyb., Plut., al.).† (AS)

G4793.strongs_def: συν-κρίνω (Rec. συγκ-) [in LXX chiefly for פָּתַר ;] __1. to compound, combine: 1Co.2:13, R, mg.1 (Lft., Notes, 180 f.). __2. In Arist. and later writers (Wis.7:29, a1.) = παραβάλλω, to compare: 1Co, l.with, R, txt. (Field, Notes, 168), 2Co.10:12 __3. In LXX, of dreams, to interpret (Gen.40:8, 1Co, l.with, R, mg. 2 (but see reff. supr.).† (AS)

G4804.strongs_def: συν-ζητητής (Rec. συζ-), -οῦ, ἁ (συνζητέω), a disputer, disputant: 1Co.1:20.† (AS)

G4813.strongs_def: συλάω, -ῶ [in LXX: Ep. Jer.1:18 * ;] with accusative of person(s), to strip, plunder, spoil: 2Co.11:8.† (AS)
G4813.derivation: from a derivative of sullo (to strip, probably akin to 138, cf 4661)

G4821.strongs_def: συμ-βουλεύω [in LXX chiefly for יָעַץ ;] __1. to advise, counsel: with dative of person(s), Jhn.18:14; id. before inf., Rev.3:18. __2. Mid., to take counsel, consult: before ἵνα, Mat.26:4 ("reciprocal middle," see M, Pr., 157); with inf., Act.9:23.† (AS)

G4825.strongs_def: σύμβουλος, -ου, ὁ (σύν, βουλή), [in LXX for יָעַץ and cogn. forms ;] a counsellor, adviser: Rom.11:34 (LXX).† (AS)

G4829.strongs_def: συν-μερίζω (Rec. συμμ-), [in LXX: Pro.29:24 א2 (חָלַק) * ;] to distri­bute in shares. Mid., to have a share in: 1Co.9:13 (Diod., al.).† (AS)

G4835.strongs_def: συμπαθής, -ές (σύν, πάσχω) [in LXX: Job.29:25 A (אָבֵל), 4Ma.5:25 א, 4Ma.13:23 4Mac 15:4 * ;] __1. affected by like feelings, sympathetic: 1Pe.3:8. __2. exciting sympathy (Jb, l.with; Dion. H.).† (AS)

G4842.strongs_def: συν-πέμπω (Rec. συμπ-) to send together with: with accusative and dative, 2Co.8:22; id. before μετά, with genitive, 2Co.8:18.† (AS)

G4853.strongs_def: συμ-φυλέτης, -ου, ὁ (σύν, φυλή; cf. σύμφυλος, Aq.: Zec.13:7; and see Rutherford, NPhr., 255 f.) a fellow-tribesman, fellow-countryman: 1Th.2:14 (see M, Th., in l, and Intr. liii). Not found elsewhere.† (AS)

G4857.strongs_def: συμ-φώνησις, -εως, ἡ (συμφωνέω), concord, agreement: before πρός, with accusative of person(s), 2Co.6:15.† (AS)

G4859.strongs_def: σύμφωνος, -ον (ούν, φωνή), [in LXX: Ecc.7:14 (עֻמָּה), 4Ma.7:7 4Mac 14:7 * ;] agreeing in sound. Metaphorical, harmonious, agreeing: ἐκ συμφώνου (for exx. from π., see Deiss., BS, 255), by agreement, 1Co.7:5.† (AS)

G4874.strongs_def: συν-ανα-μίγνυμι (accusative to Bl., 8, -μείγνυμι), [in LXX: Hos.7:8 A ( hithpo.), Eze.20:18 A * ;] to mix up together; pass., reflex, and metaphorically, to associate with (Plut., Ath., al.): 1Co.5:9 5:11, 2Th.3:14 (see M, Th., 117).† (AS)
G4874.derivation: from 4862 and a compound of 303 and 3396

G4882.strongs_def: συν-απο-στέλλω [in LXX: Exo.33:2, 12 (שָׁלַח), I Est.5:2 * ;] to send along with: with accusative, 2Co.12:18 (cf. MM, xxiv).† (AS)

G4899.strongs_def: συν-εκ-λεκτός, -ή, -όν chosen together with, co-elect: ἡ ἐν Βαβυλῶνι συνεκλεκτή (on the meaning, see ICC, in l), 1Pe.5:13.† (AS)

G4924.strongs_def: συν-οικέω, -ῶ [in LXX for בַּעַל etc. ;] to dwell together: of man and wife (Hdt., al.), with dative of person(s), 1Pe.3:7,† (AS)

G4935.strongs_def: συν-τόμως, adv. (συντέμνω) [in LXX: Pro.13:23 23:28, 3Ma.5:25 * ;] concisely, briefly: Act.24:4 (for a similar ex., see MM, xxiv).† (AS)

G4943.strongs_def: συν-υπουργέω, -ῶ to help together, join in serving: with dative instr., 2Co.1:11.† (AS)
G4943.derivation: from 4862 and a derivative of a compound of 5259 and the base of 2041

G4945.strongs_def: συνωμοσία, -ας, ή (συνόμνυμι, to conspire), [in Sm.: Eze.22:25 * ;] a conspiracy: Act.23:13.† (AS)

G4948.strongs_def: Σύρος, -ου, ὁ, fem. Σύρα a Syrian: Luk.4:27, Mrk.7:26, WH, mg.† (AS)

G4956.strongs_def: συ-στατικός (Tr. συν-), -ή, -όν (συνίστημι), __1. for putting together, constructive. __2. for bringing together, introductory, commendatory: ἐπιστολή (Arist., Diog. L., al.; and see MM, xxiv), 2Co.3:1.† (AS)

G4985.strongs_def: σωματικῶς adv., bodily, corporeally: Col.2:9 (see ICC, Lft., in l).† (AS)

G4995.strongs_def: σωφρονισμός, -οῦ, ὁ (σωφρονίζω), __(a) an admonishing (F1J, Plut., al.); __(b) self-control, self-discipline: 2Ti.1:7 (on the reflexive meaning here, see Ellic., in l).† (AS)

G4997.strongs_def: σωφροσύνη, -ης, ἡ [in LXX: Est.3:13, Wis.8:7, 2Ma.4:37, 4Ma.6:1-35 * ;] __(a) soundness of mind, good sense, sanity (opposite to μανία, Xen.): Act.26:25; __(b) self-control, sobriety: 1Ti.2:9 (see Tr., Syn., § xx), 1Ti.2:15.† (AS)

G5001.strongs_def: τάγμα, -τος, τό (τάσσω), [in LXX chiefly for דֶּגֶל, also for חַי, רַגְלִי ;] that which has been arranged or placed in order; esp. as military term, a company, troop, division, rank: metaphorically, 1Co.15:23 (see ICC, in l).† (AS)

G5020.strongs_def: ταρταρόω, -ῶ (Τάρταρος, a Greek name for the underworld, esp. the abode of the damned), to cast into hell: 2Pe.2:4 (see Mayor, in l).† (AS)
G5020.derivation: from Tartaros (the deepest abyss of Hell)

G5031.strongs_def: ταχινός, -ή, -όν [in LXX: Pro.1:16, Hab.1:6, Isa.59:7 (מָהַר), Wis.13:2, Sir.11:22 18:26 * ;] poët. and late for ταχύς, swift: of swift approach, 2Pe.1:14 2:1.† (AS)

G5041.strongs_def: τεκνογονέω, -ῶ to beget or bear children: 1Ti.5:14 (Anthol.).† (AS)
G5041.derivation: from a compound of 5043 and the base of 1096

G5044.strongs_def: τεκνο-τροφέω, -ῶ to rear young (of bees, Arist.), to bring up children: 1Ti.5:10.† (AS)

G5049.strongs_def: τελείως (τέλειος), adv., [in LXX: Jdth.11:6, 2Ma.12:42, 3Ma.3:26 3Mac 7:22, R* ;] completely, perfectly: 1Pe.1:13.† (AS)

G5066.strongs_def: τεταρταῖος, -α, -ον (τέταρτος), [in LXX: 2Ki.3:4 A (רְבִיעִי) * ;] of or on the fourth day: τ. εἶναι (Hdt., τ. γενέσθαι), to be four days dead, Jhn.11:39.† (AS)

G5073.derivation: from 5064 and a derivative of the base of 4118

G5077.strongs_def: τεφρόω, -ῶ (τέφρα, ashes; Wis.2:3, al.), to burn to ashes: 2Pe.2:6.† (AS)

G5080.strongs_def: τήκω [in LXX for מָסַס ni., מָקַק ni., מוּג ni., etc. ;] trans., to melt, melt down; pass., to melt, melt away: 2Pe.3:12.† (AS)

G5081.strongs_def: τηλαυγῶς adv. (τῆλε, afar, + αὐγή, radiance), poët. and in late prose, at a distance clearly: Mrk.8:25 (W, mg., δηλαυγῶς).† (AS)
G5081.derivation: from a compound of a derivative of 5056 and 827

G5099.strongs_def: τίνω [in LXX: Pro.27:12 (τ. ζημίαν, for עָנַשׁ ni.), etc. ;] to pay: t. δίκην (cf. Pr, l.with), to pay penalty, 2Th.1:9 (see M, Th., in l).† (AS)
G5099.derivation: strengthened for a primary tio {tee'-o} (which is only used as an alternate in certain tenses)

G5104.strongs_def: 1. enclit. Particle, serving to express belief in an assertion, let me tell you, surely, verily , used to express an inference, then, consequently , (Homer); and in [variant datesTragica Adespota, to introduce a general sentiment. 2. to strengthen other Particles, γάρ τοι, ἤτοι, καίτοι, μέντοι, τοιγάρτοι, etc.: compare τἆρα, τἄν, μεντἄν. (ML)

G5107.strongs_def: antecedent to οἷος, as ἀοιδοῦ τοιοῦδ᾽ οἷος ὅδ᾽ ἐστί of such a minstrel as is this one, (Odyssey by Homer); absolute, ἀλλ᾽ ὅδ᾽ ἐγὼ τοιόσδε here am I such as you see , (Odyssey by Homer):—;also, so great, so noble, so bad , τοιάδε λαίφη such clothes, i. e. so bad , (Odyssey by Homer); τοσόσδε καὶ τοιόσδε (Herdotus Historicus):—;also with a qualifying word, τοιόσδ᾽ ἠμὲν δέμας ἠδὲ καὶ ἔργα such both in form and works, (Odyssey by Homer):—;with the Art., ὁ τ. ἀνήρ (Aeschulus Tragicus), etc.; οἱ τοιοίδε (Sophocles Tragicus); ἐν τῷ τοιῷδε in such circumstances, (Herdotus Historicus):—;the sense is made more indefinite in τοιόσδε τις such a one, (Thucydides):—;neuter plural τοιάδε as follows , τοιαῦτα as aforesaid , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G5110.strongs_def: τόκος, -ου, ὁ (τίκτω), [in LXX for נֶשֶׁךְ, etc. ;] __(a) a bringing forth, birth; __(b) offspring. Metaphorical, of the produce of money lent out, interest, usury (cf. Merch. of Venice, I, iii, "a breed of barren metal "): Mat.25:27, Luk.19:23 (Soph., Plat., al.).† (AS)

G5113.strongs_def: τολμητής, -οῦ, ὁ (τολμάω), a bold, daring man: 2Pe.2:10 (Thuc.).† (AS)

G5157.strongs_def: τροπή, -ῆς, ἡ (τρέπω), [in LXX: Deu.33:14, Job.38:33, Wis.7:18, al. ;] a turning: esp. of the revolution of heavenly bodies, figuratively, Jas.1:17 (see: ἀποσκίασμα).† (AS)
G5157.derivation: from an apparently primary trepo {to turn}

G5162.strongs_def: τροφός, -oῦ, ἡ (τρέφω), [in LXX: Gen.35:8, 4Ki.11:2, 2Ch.22:11 Isa.49:23 (יָנַק) * ;] a nurse: 1Th.2:7.† (AS)

G5181.strongs_def: 1. an absolute sovereign , unlimited by law or constitution, (Herdotus Historicus), etc.: not applied to old hereditary sovereignties βασιλεῖαι); such as those of (Homer) or of Sparta; for the term rather regards the irregular way in which the power was gained , than the way in which it was exercised , being applied to the mild Pisistratus, but not to the despotic kings of Persia. However, the word soon came to imply reproach, like our tyrant , (Plato Philosophus), etc. 2. in a wider sense, the tyrant's son , or any member of his family , (Sophocles Tragicus):—;so, ἡ τύραννος was both the queen herself or a princess , (Euripides) 3. τύραννος, ον, as adjective kingly, royal , [variant datesTragica Adespota 4. imperious, despotic , (Thucydides); τύραννα δρᾶν (Sophocles Tragicus) τύραννος is probably from same Root as κύριος, κοίρανος. (ML)
G5181.derivation: a provincial form of the derivative of the base of 2962

G5187.strongs_def: τυφόω, -ῶ (τῦφος, smoke; metaphorically, conceit), prop., to wrap in smoke; used only metaphorically, to puff up, becloud with pride: pass., 1Ti.3:6 6:4, 2Ti.3:4 (Dem., Arist., al.).† (AS)

G5194.strongs_def: ὕαλος, -ου, ὁ [in LXX: Job.28:17 (זְכוּכִית) * ;] __1. (Hdt.) a clear transparent stone. __2. (from Plat. on) glass: Rev.21:18, 21.† (AS)
G5194.derivation: perhaps from the same as 5205 (as being transparent like rain)

G5202.strongs_def: ὑδροποτίω, -ῶ (ὕδωρ, πίνω), [in LXX: Dan LXX 1:12 שָׁתָה מַיִם) * ;] to drink water, opposite to οἴνῳ χρῆσθαι: 1Ti.5:23 (Hdt., i, 71; Plat., Rep., 561 with, al.).† (AS)
G5202.derivation: from a compound of 5204 and a derivative of 4095

G5203.strongs_def: ὑδρωπικός, -ή, -όν (ὕδρωψ, dropsy), dropsical, suffering from dropsy: Luk.14:2.† (AS)
G5203.derivation: from a compound of 5204 and a derivative of 3700 (as if looking watery)

G5229.strongs_def: ὑπερ-αίρω [in LXX: 2Ch.32:23 (נָשָׂא ni.), etc. ;] to lift or raise over. Mid., to uplift oneself: 2Co.12:7; before ἐπί, with accusative, of person(s), 2Th.2:4 (cf. 2Ma.5:23).† (AS)

G5230.strongs_def: ὑπέρακμος, -ον past the bloom of youth: 1Co.7:36 (Eustath.).† (AS)

G5232.strongs_def: ὑπερ-αυξάνω to increase beyond measure: 2Th.1:3 (see Lft., Notes, 98).† (AS)

G5233.strongs_def: ὑπερ-βαίνω [in LXX for עָבַר, etc. ;] __1. trans., to step over, trans­gress (R, overreach: 1Th.4:6). __2. Intrans., to transgress: metaphorically, 1Th.4:6 (R, txt.; see M, Th., in l).† (AS)

G5234.strongs_def: ὑπερβαλλόντως [in LXX: Job.15:11 א B (†) * ;] above measure: 2Co.11:23.† (AS)

G5238.strongs_def: ὑπερ-έκεινα comp. adv. (see Bl., 28, 2; M, Pr., 99), beyond: as prep. with genitive, τὰ ὑ. ὑμῶν, 2Co.10:16 (Byz. and Ecc.1:1-18.).† (AS)
G5238.derivation: from 5228 and the neuter plural of 1565

G5239.strongs_def: ὑπερ-εκ-τείνω to stretch out overmuch: metaphorically, ἑαυτούς, 2Co.10:14.† (AS)

G5247.strongs_def: ὑπεροχή, -ῆς, ἡ (ὑπερέχω) [in LXX: Jer.52:22 (קוֹמָה), 2Ma.3:11, al. ;] a projection, eminence, as the peak of a mountain. Metaphorical (Arist.), excellence, pre-eminence: λόγου ἢ σοφίας, 1Co.2:1; οἱ ἐν ὑ (for a parallel to this phrase, see Deiss., BS, 255, and cf. 2Mac, l.with), 1Ti.2:2.† (AS)

G5248.strongs_def: ὑπερ-περισσεύω to abound more exceedingly: Rom.5:21. Mid., in same sense (RV, overflow): with dative of thing(s), 2Co.7:4.† (AS)

G5250.strongs_def: ὑπερ-πλεονάζω to abound exceedingly: 1Ti.1:14 (Ps Sol 5:19; Herm., Mand., v, 2, 5).† (AS)

G5261.strongs_def: ὑπογραμμός, -οῦ, ὁ (ὑπογράφω, (a) to write under; (b) to trace letters for copying), [in LXX: 2Ma.2:28 * ;] __1. a writing-copy, hence, __2. an example: 1Pe.2:11 (Philo).† (AS)

G5268.strongs_def: ὑπο-ζύγιος, -α, -ον [in LXX for חֲמוֹר ;] under the yoke; as subst., τ . (Hdt., al.), a beast of burden; colloq., an ass (see Deiss., BS, 160 f.), and so always in LXX and NT: Mat.21:5 (LXX), 2Pe.2:16.† (AS)
G5268.derivation: neuter of a compound of 5259 and 2218

G5277.strongs_def: ὑπο-λιμτάνω collat. form of ὑπολείπω, to leave behind: 1Pe.2:21.† (AS)

G5280.strongs_def: ὑπόμινησις, -εως, ἡ (ὑπομιμνήσκω) [in LXX: Psa.71:6 א (תְּהִלָּה), Wis.16:11, 2Ma.6:17 * ;] a reminding, reminder: ἐν ὑ., 2Pe.1:13 3:1; with genitive, 2Ti.1:5.† (AS)

G5283.strongs_def: ὑπόνοια, -ας, ἡ (ὑπονοέω), [in LXX: Dan LXX 4:16, 32 5:6 (רַעְיוֹן), Sir 3:34* ;] a suspicion: 1Ti.6:4.† (AS)

G5296.strongs_def: ὑπο-τύπωσις, -εως, ἡ (ὑποτυπόω, to delineate), an outline, sketch. Metaphorical, a pattern, example: 1Ti.1:16, 2Ti.1:13.† SYN.: ὁμοίωμα, τύπος, ὑπόδειγμα (see DB, iii, 696b) (AS)
G5296.derivation: from a compound of 5259 and a derivative of 5179

G5297.strongs_def: ὑπο-φέρω [in LXX for נָשָׂא, etc. ;] to bear by being under. Metaphorical, to endure: with accusative of thing(s), 1Co.10:13, 2Ti.3:11, 1Pe.2:19.† (AS)

G5300.strongs_def: ὗς, ὑός, ὁ, ἡ [in LXX for חֲזִיר ;] swine: fem. (sow), 2Pe.2:22,† (AS)

G5306.strongs_def: ὕστερος, -α, -ον [in LXX for אַחֲרוֹן and cogn. forms ;] latter, later: ἐν ὑ. καιροῖς, 1Ti.4:1 (on the reading ὁ ὕ., WH, for ὁ πρῶτος, see WH, App., in l). Neut., τὸ ὕ., used adverbially instead of ὑστέρως, afterwards, later: Mat.4:2 21:29, 32 21:37 25:11 26:60, Mrk.16:14, Luk.20:32, Jhn.13:36, Heb.12:11; with genitive, Mat.22:27.† (AS)
G5306.derivation: comparative from 5259 (in the sense of behind)

G5321.strongs_def: φανέρωσις, -εως, ἡ (φανερόω), [in LXX as seel. for δήλωσις אוּרִים), Lev.8:8, Cod. Ven. (Thayer, see word) * ;] manifestation: 1Co.12:7, 2Co.4:2.† (AS)

G5341.strongs_def: φελόνης (Rec. φαιλ-), -ου, ὁ by metath. for παινόλης (also φενόλης, φαινόλιον; Lat. pænula) a cloak (see DCG, i, 338; on the idea that the meaning here is book-cover, see CGT, in l; Milligan, NTD, 20; Field, Notes, 217 f., where the view that the φ. here is an eccl. vestment is discussed): 2Ti.4:13.† (AS)
G5341.derivation: by transposition for a derivative probably of 5316 (as showing outside the other garments)

G5361.strongs_def: φιλ-άδελφος, -ον [in LXX: 2Ma.15:14, 4Ma.13:21 4Mac 15:10 * ;] loving one's brother, loving like a brother (Soph., Xen., al.): of Christians' love for one another (EV, loving as brethren), 1Pe.3:8.† (AS)

G5365.strongs_def: φιλαργυρία, -ας, ἡ (φιλάργυρος), [in LXX: 4Ma.1:26 4Mac 2:15 א1 * ;] love of money, avarice: 1Ti.6:1.† SYN.: πλεονεξία, covetousness (see Tr., Syn., § xxiv) (AS)

G5367.strongs_def: φίλ-αυτος, -ον loving oneself (Arist.); in bad sense (ib.), selfish: 2Ti.3:2.† SYN.: αὐθάδης (see Tr., Syn., § xciii) (AS)

G5369.strongs_def: φιλήδονος, -ον (φίλος, ἡδονή), loving pleasure: 2Ti.3:4 (Polyb., Plut. al.).† (AS)

G5380.strongs_def: φιλό-νεικος, -ον (νεῖκος, strife) [in LXX: Eze.3:7 (חָזָק ־מֵצַח)* ;] fond of strife, contentious: 1Co.11:16.† (AS)
G5380.derivation: from 5384 and neikos (a quarrel, probably akin to 3534)

G5383.strongs_def: φιλο-πρωτιύω (φιλόπρωτος, Plut., al.) to strive to be first: III Jn 9 (eccl.).† (AS)

G5388.strongs_def: φιλότεκνος, -ον (φίλος, τέκνον), [in LXX: 4Ma.15:4-6 * ;] loving one's children (Hdt., Arist., Plut., al.): of women, joined with φίλανδρος, which see, Tit.2:4.† (AS)

G5390.strongs_def: φιλοφρόνως (φιλόφρων) adv., [in LXX: 2Ma.3:9, 4Ma.8:5 * ;] kindly, with friendliness: Act.28:7.† (AS)

G5396.strongs_def: φλυαρέω, -ῶ (φλύαρος), to talk nonsense: with accusative of person(s), ἡμᾶς (EV, prating against us), III Jn 10.† (AS)

G5397.strongs_def: φλύαρος, -ον (φλύω, to babble), [in LXX: 4Ma.5:10 * ;] babbling, garrulous: 1Ti.5:13 (EV, tattlers; of things, φιλοσοφία, 4Mac, l.with).† (AS)

G5415.strongs_def: φορτούνατος (Rec. Φουρ-, see Mayser, 116 f.), -ου, ὁ (Lat.) Fortunatus: 1Co.16:17 (see Lft., Cl. Ro., 1Co., 59).† (AS)

G5424.strongs_def: φρήν genitive, φρενός, ἡ, [in LXX most frequently in Pr (Pro.6:32, al.) and chiefly for לֵב; also 3Ma.4:16 3Mac 5:47 ;] chiefly in Hom. and Trag., but also in Plat., al., both sing. and pl.; __1. in physical sense, the parts about the heart, midriff. __2. heart, mind, thought: pl., 1Co.14:20 (see Edwards, Eng.-Gr. Lex., App., 1).† (AS)
G5424.derivation: probably from an obsolete phrao (to rein in or curb, cf 5420)

G5425.strongs_def: φρίσσω (Att.. -ττω, and so 4Ma.14:9 4Mac 17:7) [in LXX: Job.4:15 ( pi.), etc. ;] __1. to be rough, bristle. __2. to shiver, shudder, tremble, from fear: Jas.2:19 (see Hort, in l).† (AS)

G5450.strongs_def: φυσίωσις, -εως, ἡ (φυσιόω), a puffing up, swelling with pride: pl., 2Co.12:20.† (AS)

G5459.strongs_def: φωσ-φόρος, -ον (φῶς, φέρω), light-bringing; as subst., ὁ φ., the morning star (Plat., al.; cf. ἐωσφόρος, Isa.14:12, Job.3:9, Psa.110:3): metaphorically, 2Pe.1:19 (see Mayor, in l).† (AS)

G5462.strongs_def: φωτισμός, -οῦ, ὁ (φωτίζω) [in LXX: Job.3:9, Psa.27:1 44:3 78:14 139:11 (אוֹר), Psa.89:8 (מָאוֹר) * ;] illumination, light: metaphorically, 1Co.4:4 4:6.† (AS)

G5471.strongs_def: χαλκεύς, -έως, ὁ (χαλκός), [in LXX for חָרָשׁ, etc. ;] a worker, in metal, esp. a copper-smith: 2Ti.4:14.† (AS)

G5489.strongs_def: χάρτης, -ου, ὁ [in LXX: Isa.8:1 A, Jer.36:2, 6 36:23 (מְגִלָּה) * ;] a sheet of paper, made of papyrus strips (see Kennedy, Sources, 42; Milligan, NTD, 10-12; DB, iv, 945 f.): II Jn 12 (Plat., Inscr.).† (AS)

G5497.strongs_def: χειρ-αγωγός, -όν (χείρ, ἄγω) leading by the hand. As subst., ὁ χ., one to lead by the head, a guide: Act.13:11.† (AS)
G5497.derivation: from 5495 and a reduplicated form of 71

G5516.strongs_def: χξς ́ (on ς, see: Z), in T, Tr., Rec. for ἑξακόσιοι ἑξήκοντα ἕξ, six hundred and sixty-six (L, mg., R, mg., six hundred and sixteen), the mystical number of the Beast: Rev.13:18 (on the interpretation, see Swete, Ap., 172 f.).† (AS)
G5516.derivation: the 22d, 14th and an obsolete letter (4742 as a cross) of the Greek alphabet (intermediate between the 5th and 6th), used as numbers

G5517.strongs_def: χοϊκός, -ή, -όν, (χοῦς) earthy, made of dust: 1Co.15:47-49 (see Field, Notes, 179 f.).† (AS)

G5524.strongs_def: χορηγέω, -ῶ (χορός, ἡγέομαι) [in LXX for כּוּל pilp. ;] __1. to lead a χορός (see LS, see word). __2. to defray the cost of a χορός. __3. In late writers, metaphorically, with accusative (see M, Pr., 65), to supply, furnish abundantly: 2Co.9:10, 1Pe.4:11 (Polyb., al.).† (AS)

G5525.strongs_def: χορός, -οῦ, ὁ [in LXX chiefly for מָחוֹל, מְחֹלָה ;] a dance: pl., Luk.15:25.† (AS)

G5527.strongs_def: χόρτασμα, -τος, τό (χορτάζω), [in LXX: Gen.24:25, 32 42:27 43:24, Jdg.19:19 (מִסְפּוֹא), Deu.11:16 (עֶשֶׂב), (Sir.33:24) Sir.38:26 * ;] fodder (Polyb., Plut., al.): pl., Act.7:11 (RV, sustenance).† (AS)

G5539.strongs_def: χρήσιμος, -η, -ον (χράομαι), [in LXX: Gen.37:26 בֶּצַע etc. ;] useful: 2Ti.2:14.† (AS)

G5545.strongs_def: χρίσμα (T, χρῖσμα, as in cl.; see Tdf., Pr., 102; Bl., § 4, 2), -τος, το (χρίω), later form of χρῖμα (Æsch., al.), [in LXX for מִשְׁחָה and cogn. forms (Exo.29:7, al.) ;] an anointing, unction (the result of the action χρίειν; ICC, in l; but cf. Westc., in l, for the view that the oil, not the act, is meant): 1Jn.2:20 Jn 2:27.† (AS)

G5566.strongs_def: the North-west wind , Lat. Caurus, (New Testament) (ML)

G5573.strongs_def: ψευδο-λόγος, -ον (ψευδής, λέγω), speaking falsely, lying: 1Ti.4:2 (Aristoph., Polyb., al.).† (AS)

G5581.strongs_def: ψευδώνυμος, -ον (ψευδής, ὄνομα) under a false name, falsely called: 1Ti.6:20 (Æsch., Plut., a1.).† (AS)

G5587.strongs_def: ψιθυρισμός, -οῦ, ὁ (ψιθυρίζω, to whisper), [in LXX: Ecc.10:11 (לַחַשׁ) * ;] a whispering; __(a) of secret slander, 2Co.12:20 (Plut.); __(b) of a murmured enchantment, Ec, l.with† (AS)
G5587.derivation: from a derivative of psithos (a whisper; by implication, a slander, probably akin to 5574)

G5588.strongs_def: ψιθυριστής, -οῦ, ὁ (see supr.), a whisperer (as epithet of Hermes, Dem., 1358, 6): in bad sense, Rom.1:30.† Syn.: καταλάλος, q.v (AS)

G5594.strongs_def: ψύχω [in LXX for קוּר, שָׁטַח ;] to breathe, blow; hence, to make cool. Pass., to grow cool: metaphorically, Mat.24:12.† (AS)

G5612.strongs_def: ὠρύομαι depon., [in LXX for שָׁאַג ;] of animals (also of men, Hdt., al.), to roar, howl: λέων, 1Pe.5:8.† (AS)
G5612.derivation: middle voice of an apparently primary verb

G5619.strongs_def: ὡσ-περ-εί adv., as, as it were: 1Co.15:8.† (AS)

G6000.strongs_def: ἀγγέλλω (ἄγγελος), [in LXX for נגד hi. ;] to announce, report: Jhn.4:51 (WHR omit), 20:18 (MM, VGT, see word).† (AS)

G6001.strongs_def: ἄγγος, -εος, τό, [in LXX for כְּלִי, כְּלוּב ;] a vessel: Mat.13:48.† (AS)

G6002.strongs_def: Ἀδμείν (WH, mg., Ἀδάμ), 6, indecl., Admin.: Luk.3:33.† (AS)

G6003.strongs_def: ἀθροίζω (ἀθρόος, assembled in crowds, MM, VGT, see word; θρόος, a noise, tumult), [in LXX chiefly for קבץ ;] to gather, assemble: Luk.24:33.† (AS)

G6005.strongs_def: ἀμφιέζω, see: ἀμφιάζω. ἀμφιάζω (ἀμφί, on both sides: see M, Pr., 100), Hellenistic for ἀμφιέννυμι (cf. MM, VGT, see word), [in LXX for לָבַשׁ, etc. ;] to clothe: Luk.12:28 (T, -έζει).† (AS)

G6006.strongs_def: ἀμφι-βάλλω (see supr.), [in LXX: Hab.1:17 * ;] = περιβάλλω, to throw around, as a garment: absol. (MM, VGT, see word), of casting a net: Mrk.1:16 (Rec. βάλλονταν ἀμφίβληστρον).† SYN.: δίκτυον, σαγήνη. ἀ. is a casting-net, σ. a drag-net, δ. is the more general term - a net of any kind (Tr., Syn., § lxiv). (AS)

G6007.strongs_def: ἄμωμον, -ου, τό, amomum, a fragrant plant of India (RV, spice): Rev.18:13 (AS)

G6008.strongs_def: ἀνα-πηδάω, -ῶ (πηδάω, to leap), [in LXX: 1Ki.20:34 (קוּם) 1Ki.25:10, Est.5:1, To.4 * ;] to leap up: Mrk.10:50 (Rec. ἀναστάς) (AS)

G6011.strongs_def: βελόνη, -ῆς, ἡ (βέλος), __1. a sharp point, as of a spear. __2. a needle: Luk.18:25 (Rec. ῥαφίς, which see).† (AS)

G6013.strongs_def: product, fruit, harvest Variant for γέννημα (G1081)

G6014.strongs_def: δεκα-οκτώ, T for δέκα ὀκτώ, eighteen: Luk.13:4.† (AS)

G6015.strongs_def: δέος, -ους, τό (δείδω), [in LXX: 2Ma.3:17, 30 12:22 13:16 15:23 * ;] fear, awe, reverence: μετὰ εὐλαβείας καὶ δ., Heb.12:28.† SYN.: δειλία, φόβος. (AS)

G6017.strongs_def: δια-χλευάζω, intensive of χλευάζω, to scoff, mock: __(a) with accusative; __(b) absol., Act.2:13.† (AS)

G6018.strongs_def: δι-ενθυμέομαι, -οῦμαι, depon., to consider, reflect: before περί, Act.10:19.† (AS)

G6019.strongs_def: δισ-μυριάς, -άδος, ἡ, [in LXX: 2Ma.6:1-31 * ;] twice ten thousand: Rev.9:16 (LT; δὶς μυριάδες, WH; δύο μ., Rec.).† (AS)

G6020.strongs_def: δοκιμασία, -ας, ἡ (δοκιμάζω), [in LXX: Sir.6:21 * ;] a testing, proving: Heb.3:9 (LXX).† SYN.: πειράζω (see Tr., Syn., LXXiv; Cremer, 494 ff., 699 ff.). (AS)

G6022.strongs_def: δυσφημέω, -ώ (δύσφημος, slanderous), [in LXX: 1Ma.7:41 * ;] __1. intrans., to use evil words (Æsch.). __2. Trans., to speak ill of, defame (Soph.): pass., 1Co.4:13.† (AS)

G6023.strongs_def: ἐγκακέω, see: ἐνκ-. ἐν-κακέω, -ῶ (LTr., ἐγκ-; Rec. ἐκκ-; cf. WH, Notes, 157 f.; κακός, cowardly), [in Sm.: Gen.27:46, Num.21:5, Pro.3:11, Isa.7:16 *;] to lose heart : Luk.18:1, 2Co.4:1,16, Gal.6:9, Eph.3:13, 2Th.3:13 (Cremer, 330).† (AS)

G6025.strongs_def: εἵνεκεν, see: ἕνεκα. ἕνεκα (so Mat.19:5, Luk.6:22, Act.19:32 26:21; elsewhere, prop, only before a vowel, ἕνεκεν; εἵνεκεν, originally Ionic: Luk.4:18 18:29, Act.28:20, 2Co.3:10), prep. with genitive, on account of, because of: Mat.5:10-11 16:25 19:29, Mrk.8:35, Luk.6:22, Act.28:20, Rom.8:36, 2Co.3:10; ἕ. τούτου, Mat.19:5; υούτων, Act.26:21; τίνος ἕ., Act.19:32; before τοῦ, with inf., 2Co.7:12; οὗ ἕν., Luk.4:18 (AS)

G6027.strongs_def: ἐκ-ζήτησις, -εως, ἡ (ἐκζητέω), a questioning (RV), subject for dispute: 1Ti.1:4.† (AS)

G6028.strongs_def: ἐκ-θαυμάζω, [in LXX: Sir.27:23 43:18, 4Ma.17:17 * ;] strengthened form of θαυμ-; to wonder greatly: Mrk.12:17.† (AS)

G6029.strongs_def: εκ-περισσῶς, adv., more exceedingly: Mrk.14:31 (of. ὑπερπερ-).† (AS)

G6030.strongs_def: ἐκ-πηδάω, -ῶ [in LXX: Deu.33:22 (זָנַק), etc. ;] to spring forth: εἰς τ. ὄχλον (cf. Ju 14:17), Act.14:14 (for ex. in π., see MM, Exp., xii).† (AS)

G6031.strongs_def: ἐλεγμός, -οῦ, ὁ (ἐλέγχω), [in LXX: Psa.38:14 39:11 (תּוֹכֵחָה), Sir.20:29 21:6 41:4, al. ;] reproof: 2Ti.3:16.† ἔλεγχος, -ου, ὁ (AS)

G6033.strongs_def: 1. adverb: 2. Demonstr., 3. of Place, Lat. inde, thence, (Homer); ἔνθεν μὲν . ., ἑτέρωθι δέ .., on the one side and the other, (Odyssey by Homer); ἔνθεν καὶ ἔνθεν on this side and on that , Lat. hinc illinc, (Herdotus Historicus), etc.:—; with genitive, ἔνθεν καὶ ἔνθεν τῶν τροχῶν on both sides of the wheels, (Xenophon Historicus) 4. of Time, thereupon, thereafter , (Iliad by Homer) 5. of occasion, thence, from that point , (Odyssey by Homer) 6. Relat., for ὅθεν, 7. of Place, Lat. unde, whence, from which, (Odyssey by Homer) 8. of occasion, whence , like Lat. unde, (Aeschulus Tragicus) Hence (ML)

G6034.strongs_def: ἐν-ορκίζω, [in LXX: Neh.13:25 A (שָׁבַע hi.)* ;] to adjure: with dupl. accusative (like ορκίζω, which see), ὑμᾶς τ. κῦριον, 1Th.5:27.† (AS)

G6035.strongs_def: ἐπ-άρατος, -ον (ἐπαράομαι, to imprecate), accursed: Jhn.7:49 (for exx. from π., see MM, Exp., xiv; cf. Cremer, 108).† (AS)

G6036.strongs_def: ἐπ-εισ-έρχομαι [in LXX: 1Ma.16:16 (with dative) * ;] to come in upon: before ἐπί Luk.21:35.† (AS)

G6037.strongs_def: ἐπι-σπείρω, to sow upon or besides: ἀνὰ μέσον, Mat.13:25.† (AS)

G6041.strongs_def: ζηλεύω, late and rare form of ζηλόω, which see; __1. to envy, be jealous. __2. to be zealous: Rev.3:19.† (AS)

G6045.strongs_def: καθώσπερ (Tr. καθώς περ), adv. (see: καθώς), even as: 2Co.3:8 (WH, mg.), Heb.5:4.† (AS)

G6046.strongs_def: to burden, make heavy, opress Some manuscripts list βαρέω (G0916) in place of G6046 at Mrk.14.40

G6047.strongs_def: 1. to scratch away, lacerate , (Herdotus Historicus) 2. to engrave, inscribe , νόμους (Plutarch) 3. to paint over , (Lucian) 4. to fill tablets with writing (Euripides) 5. to write down, register, record , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G6048.strongs_def: κατα-δίκη, -ης, ἡ, [in LXX: Wis.12:27 * ;] sentence, condemnation: Act.25:15.† (AS)

G6049.strongs_def: to bend down, stoop , (Iliad by Homer):—; bend down and peep into a thing, (Lucian) (ML)

G6050.strongs_def: κατ-ευλογέω, -ῶ, [in LXX: Tob.11:1, 17 * ;] to bless fervently: Mrk.10:16 (see Swete, in l).† (AS)

G6051.strongs_def: κατήγωρ, ὁ (Aram. קָטִיגוֺר; Dalman, Gr., 185; but see Deiss., LAE, 90 f.), = κατήγορος, an accuser: Rev.12:10.† (AS)

G6052.strongs_def: 1. to remove to a place, plant, settle or establish there as colonists , κ. τινὰ εἰς τόπον (Herdotus Historicus); γυναῖκας ἐς φῶς ἡλίου κατ. (Euripides):—;also, κ. τινὰ ἐν τόπῳ to settle or plant one in , (Sophocles Tragicus); ἐλπίδας ἔν τινι κ. to plant them in his mind, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 2. with accusative loci, to colonise, people a place, (Herdotus Historicus), etc. 3. Pass., 4. of persons, to be placed or settled , ἐν τόπῳ (Herdotus Historicus); ἐς τόπον (Thucydides) 5. of places, to have colonies planted there, to be colonised , (Thucydides) 6. to bring home and re-establish there, to restore to one's country , (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

G6053.strongs_def: κατωτέρω, see: κάτω. κάτω adv. (κατά), [in LXX for מַטָּה, תַּחַת and cogn. forms ;] __1. down, downwards (with verbs of motion), Mat.4:6, Luk.4:9, Jhn.8:6, 8, Act.20:9. __2. below, beneath: Mrk.14:66, Act.2:19" (LXX) ; ἕως κ. (Eze.1:27, al.), Mat.27:51, Mrk.15:38. τὰ κ. (opposite to τ. ἄνω), Jhn.8:23. Compar. κατωτέρω: ἀπὸ διετοῦς καὶ κ. (cf. 1Ch.27:21), Mat.2:16.† (AS)

G6055.strongs_def: κλινάριον, -ου, τό, dimin, of κλίνη, a couch: Act.5:15 (cf. κλινίδιον).† (AS)

G6059.strongs_def: κυκλεύω (κύκλος), [in LXX: 4Ki.3:25 B (סָבַב) * ;] __1. to make a circle, go round. __2. to encircle, surround: with accusative of person(s), Jhn.10:24 (Tr., WH, mg.); with accusative of thing(s), Rev.20:9.† (AS)

G6060.strongs_def: to turn around Some manuscripts list μεταστρέφω (G3344) in place of G6060 at Jas.4.9

G6061.strongs_def: μύλινος, -η, -ον (μύλος), __1. made of mill-stone (C.l. 3371) __2. = μυλικός: Rev.18:21 (μύλον, T).† (AS)

G6063.strongs_def: 1. to know , εὖ οἶδα I know well; εὖ ἴσθι be assured : often with accusative rei, νοήματα οἶδε, μήδεα οἶδε he is versed in counsels, (Homer); with neut. Adjs., πεπνυμένα, φίλα, ἀθεμίστια εἰδώς (Homer); also with genitive, τόξων εὖ εἰδώς cunning in the use of the bow; οἰωνῶν σάφα εἰδώς (Odyssey by Homer): —; χάριν εἰδέναι τινί to acknowledge a debt to another, thank him , (Iliad by Homer), etc.:—;the Imperat. in protestations, ἴστω Ζεὺς αὐτός be Zeus my witness , (Iliad by Homer); doric ἴττω Ζεύς, ἴττω (Aristophanes Comicus): —; εἰδώς absolute one who knows , εἰδυίηι πάντ᾽ ἀγορεύω (Iliad by Homer); ἰδυίηισι πραπίδεσσι with knowing mind, (Iliad by Homer) 2. with infinitive to know how to do, (Iliad by Homer), attic 3. with the participle to know that so and so is the case, ἴσθι μοι δώσων know that thou wilt give, (Aeschulus Tragicus); τὸν Μῆδον ἴσμεν ἐλθόντα (Thucydides) 4. οὐκ οἶδα εἰ, I know not whether, expresses disbelief, like Lat. nescio an non, οὐκ οἶδ᾽ ἂν εἰ πείσαιμι (Euripides) 5. οἶδα or ἴσθι are often parenthetic, οἶδ᾽ ἐγώ (Euripides); οἶδ᾽ ὅτι, οἶσθ᾽ ὅτι, ἴσθ᾽ ὅτι, πάρειμι (Sophocles Tragicus); so, εὖ οἶδ᾽ ὅτι (Demosthenes Orator): —;in [variant datesTragica Adespota also, οἶσθ᾽ ὃ δρᾶσο; equivalent to δρᾶσον —; οἶσθ᾽ ; do —; know'st thou what? i. e. make haste and do; οἶσθ᾽ ὡς ποίησον, etc. (ML)

G6064.strongs_def: οἰκετεία, -ας, ἡ (οἰκέτης), a household (of servants): Mat.24:45.† (AS)

G6066.strongs_def: ὀλιγοπιστία, -ας, ἡ, little faith or trust: Mat.17:20.† (AS)

G6067.strongs_def: scarcely, barely Some manuscripts list ὀλίγος (G3641) in place of G6067 at 2Pe.2.18

G6068.strongs_def: 1. a mist, fog , (not so thick as νέφος or νεφέλη); (Iliad by Homer); κονίης ὀμίχλη a cloud of dust, (Iliad by Homer) 2. metaphorically a mist over the eyes, (Aeschulus Tragicus): darkness, gloom , [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

G6069.strongs_def: πανταχῇ (Rec. -χῆ), adv., [in LXX: Isa.24:11 (בַּחוּצוֹת), Wis.2:9, 2Ma.8:7 * ;] everywhere: Act.21:28.† (AS)

G6070.strongs_def: 1. to put in beside, insert, interpolate, interpose , τι (Aristophanes Comicus); π. ὑποψίας to insinuate suspicions, (Aeschines Orator) 2. to put the auxiliaries in line with the legionaries, (Polybius Historicus) 3. intransitive to fall into line, to encamp , (Polybius Historicus) (ML)

G6071.strongs_def: περαιτέρω (πέρα, beyond), compar. adv., beyond: Act.19:39, L, Tr., WH (T, Rec., R, περὶ ἑτέρων).† (AS)

G6072.strongs_def: περι-άπτω, [in LXX: 3Ma.3:7 * ;] __1. to tie about, attach. __2. In late writers, to light a fire around, kindle: πῦρ, Luk.22:55.† SYN.: θιγγάνω, ψηλαφάω. ἅ. is the stronger, θ., to touch, the lighter term. ψ. is to feel, as in search of something (Tr., Syn., § xvii; Lft., Col., 201 f.) (AS)

G6073.strongs_def: gentleness, meekness Some manuscripts list πραότης (G4236) in place of G6073 at 1Ti.6.11

G6074.strongs_def: the first founder of a family, forefather , (Herdotus Historicus):—;in plural ancestors, forefathers , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; ὦ Ζεῦ, προγόνων προπάτωρ (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G6075.strongs_def: προσαίτης, -ου, ὁ, a beggar: Mrk.10:46, Jhn.9:8.† (AS)

G6076.strongs_def: προσ-κλίνω [in LXX: 2Ma.14:24 * ;] __1. to make to lean against. __2. to make the scale incline one way or another; hence, metaphorically, of persons, to incline (sc. ἑαυτόν) towards: pass., Act.5:36.† (AS)

G6077.strongs_def: A man living at the time of the New Testament, only mentioned at Act.20.4; father of: Sopater (G4986) § Pyrrhus (the name of Sopater of Boroeas's father) See also πυρρός (G4450)

G6078.strongs_def: first, originally Some manuscripts list πρῶτον (G4412) in place of G6078 at Act.11.26

G6079.strongs_def: 1. grain, corn: food made from grain, bread , ποιεῖσθαι σιτία ἀπὸ ὀλυρέων to feed off spelt, (Herdotus Historicus) 2. generally, food, victuals, provisions , (Herdotus Historicus); σιτία ἡμερῶν τριῶν three days' provision , of soldiers, (Aristophanes Comicus); σιτία καὶ ποτά meat and drink, (Plato Philosophus) 3. τἀν Πρυτανείῳ σιτία public maintenance in the Prytaneum, (Aristophanes Comicus); compare σίτησις. 4. rarely food for dogs, (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G6080.strongs_def: συγγενίς, -ίδος, ἡ, late fem. form of σνγγενής, which see, a kinswoman: Luk.1:36.† (AS)

G6081.strongs_def: 1. to fall together, meet in battle, come to blows , Lat. concurrere, (Homer): ς. ἐς νείκεα (Herdotus Historicus): to encounter , κλύδωνι (Euripides); νηί (Thucydides) 2. generally, to fall in with, meet with accidents, misfortunes, with dative, (Herdotus Historicus) 3. of ailments, events, to fall upon, happen to , with dative pers., (Aeschulus Tragicus); also ἔς τινα (Herdotus Historicus) 4. absolute to happen or fall out at the same time, concur , (Herdotus Historicus) 5. with part, like τυγχάνω, τόδε συνέπεσε γενόμενον (Herdotus Historicus) 6. impersonal, συνέπεσε, it happened, fell out, came to pass , with infinitive, (Herdotus Historicus); ξυνέπεσεν εἰς τοῦτο ἀνάγκης ὥστε . . matters came to such a pass that . ., (Thucydides); or with accusative et infinitive, (Thucydides) 7. to coincide, agree or be in accordance with , τινί (Herdotus Historicus): absolute to agree exactly , (Herdotus Historicus); ἐμοὶ σὺ συμπέπτωκας ἐς ταὐτὸν λόγου have come to exactly the same point with me, (Euripides) 8. to fall together , i. e. fall in, collapse , of a house, Lat. concidere, (Euripides); σῶμα συμπεσόν a frame having collapsed from disease, (Plato Philosophus) 9. συμπίτνω poetry for συμπίπτω, when the penultimate is to be short 10. to fall or dash together , of waves, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 11. to concur , (Aeschulus Tragicus); with dative, (Euripides) (ML)

G6083.strongs_def: ύν-οιδα , pf. with Pres. meaning (see: οἶδα), [in LXX: Lev.5:1 (יָדַע), Job.27:6; ptcp., 1Ma.4:21 A, 2Ma.4:41 A, 3Ma.2:8 R * ;] __1. to share the knowledge of, be privy to (Hdt., Thuc., al.): ptcp., Act.5:2. __2. C. prop. reflex., to be conscious of (Eur., Plat., al.), esp. of guilty consciousness: οὐδὲν γὰρ ἐμαυτῷ σ., for I know nothing against myself, 1Co.4:4.† (AS)

G6084.strongs_def: Τίτιος, -ου, ὁ, Titius, surnamed Justus: Act.18:7, T, WH (RV., Τίτος).† (AS)

G6085.strongs_def: τρῆμα, -τος, τό, a perforation, hole: ῥαφίδος, Mat.19:24, WH, txt. βελόνης, Luk.18:25 (Aristoph., Plat., al.).† SYN.: τρυμαλιά, τρύπημα (AS)

G6087.strongs_def: εκ-περισσῶς, adv., more exceedingly: Mrk.14:31 (of. ὑπερπερ-).† (AS)

G6088.strongs_def: ὑπερλίαν (Rec. ὑπὲρ λίαν, see WM, § 50, 7n; B1., § 4, 1), adv., exceedingly, pre-eminently: 2Co.11:5 12:11.† (AS)

G6090.strongs_def: ὠτάριον, -ου, τό = ὠτίον (which see), the ear: Mrk.14:47, Jhn.18:10.† (AS)

G6091.strongs_def: δύσις, -εως, ἡ (δύνω), [in LXX: Psa.104:19 (מָבוֹא) * ;] __1. a sinking, setting, as of the sun (Æsch.): Mrk.16:1-20 [alt. ending]. __2. the sun-setting, the west (Thuc.).† (AS)

G6092.strongs_def: ἐκ-βαίνω, [in LXX for עָלֶה ;] to go out: Heb.11:15.† (AS)

G6093.strongs_def: σιρός, see: σειρός.σειρός (σιρός, T), -οῦ, ὁ (Rec., R, mg., σειρά, which see), = cl. σιρός, a pit for the storage of grain: σειροὶ ζόφου, 2Pe.2:4, WH, R., txt. (but see Mayor, in l; Field, Notes, 241).† (AS)

G6094.strongs_def: αὐχέω, -ῶ, (αὔχη, boasting), to boast: with accusative (MM, see word), μεγάλα αὐχεῖ (Rec. μεγαλαυχεῖ, which see), Jas.3:5.† (AS)

G6095.strongs_def: A man of the tribe of Judah living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at Rut.4.19; son of: Hezron (H2696H); brother of: Jerahmeel (H3396), Caleb (H3612H), Segub (H7687H) and Ashhur (H0806); father of: Amminadab (H5992); also called Admin (KJV: Aram) at Luk.3.33; § Arni (Proper name)

G6098.strongs_def: burn to ashes, destroy by fire (2PE.2:6 - variant P72*)

G6099.strongs_def: comb, clean (of wool; MAT.6:28 - variant א*)

G6101.strongs_def: 1. untrodden, impassable, inaccessible , of mountains, (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; of a river, not fordable , (Xenophon Historicus) 2. of holy places, not to be trodden , like ἄθικτος, (Sophocles Tragicus): metaphorically pure, chaste , ψυχή (Plato Philosophus) 3. of horses, not ridden , (Lucian) 4. active, ἄβ. πόνος a plague that hinders walking , i.e. gout, (Lucian) (ML)

G6104.strongs_def: want of counsel, thoughtlessness , (Herdotus Historicus), etc. (ML)

G6111.strongs_def: 1. a glory, delight, honour , (Iliad by Homer), attic; ἀγάλματ᾽ ἀγορᾶς mere ornaments of the agora, (Euripides) 2. a pleasing gift , especially for the gods, (Odyssey by Homer) 3. a statue in honour of a god , (Herdotus Historicus), attic; an image , as an object of worship, etc., (Aeschulus Tragicus); then generally,= ἀνδριάς, any statue , (Plato Philosophus): also a portrait, picture , ἐξαλειφθεῖς᾽ ὡς ἄγαλμα (Euripides) (ML)

G6117.strongs_def: 1. a loop or noose in a cord,Eur., (Xenophon Historicus) 2. the thong of a javelin , by which it was hurled: the javelin itself, (Euripides) 3. a bow-string , (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G6118.strongs_def: 1. the bend of the arm, the elbow , (Homer) 2. generally the arm , like ἀγκάλη, (Pindar) 3. any bend , as the jutting angle of a wall, (Iliad by Homer): the bend or reach of a river, (Herdotus Historicus); ἕσπεροι ἄγκωνες, in (Sophocles Tragicus), seem to be the angle of the bay of Rhoeteium. (ML)

G6122.strongs_def: 1. passive unborn , (Iliad by Homer): not yet born , (Euripides) 2. active not producing, unfruitful, barren ; τόκοισιν ἀγόνοις travail without issue, bringing no children to the birth , (Sophocles Tragicus), etc. 3. with genitive not productive of, barren in a thing, (Plato Philosophus) 4. childless , (Euripides) (ML)

G6124.strongs_def: 1. intransitive to be angered, provoked, chafed , (Plato Philosophus); τινί with one, (Plato Philosophus); metaphorically of rivers, (Plutarch) 2. Causal, to make angry : Pass. to be angered , (Plutarch) (ML)

G6127.strongs_def: 1. of or in the country , (Aristophanes Comicus), etc. 2. of men, dwelling in the country, a countryman, rustic , (Aristophanes Comicus); then, opposite to ἀστεῖος, clownish, boorish, rude , (Aristophanes Comicus); the character of the ἄγροικος is described by (Theophrastus Philosophus) 3. adverb -κως, (Aristophanes Comicus); comparative -οτέρως, (Plato Philosophus); but -ότερον, (Plato Philosophus) 4. of land, rough, uncultivated , (Thucydides) (ML)

G6128.strongs_def: Substantive and adjective, (Sophocles Tragicus), a grass that mules fed on . (ML)

G6129.strongs_def: 1. nearness of kin , (Plato Philosophus) 2. rights of kin, right of inheritance , (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G6130.strongs_def: mostly in plural ἀγχιστεῖς, closely akin , of nations, (Herdotus Historicus): next of kin , (Lucian) (ML)

G6131.strongs_def: 1. to be next or near , with dative, (Euripides) 2. to be next of kin , (Isaeus Orator) (ML)

G6132.strongs_def: to compress, press tight , especially the throat, to strangle, throttle, choke , ἄγχε μιν ἱμὰς ὑπὸ δειρήν (Iliad by Homer); τὸν Κέρβερον ἀπῇξας ἄγχων (Aristophanes Comicus): metaphorically of creditors, (Aristophanes Comicus); of a guilty conscience, τοῦτο ἄγχει (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

G6133.strongs_def: adamantine , (Aeschulus Tragicus), etc.: —;metaphorically hard as adamant , σιδηροῖς καὶ ἀδαμαντίνοις λόγοις (Plato Philosophus); οὐκ ἀδ. ἐντί, of a girl, (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus):—;adverb -νως, (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G6134.strongs_def: 1. properly the untamed, unconquerable : 2. as Substantive adamant , i. e. the hardest metal, probably steel : metaphorically of any thing unalterable , ἔπος ἐρέω ἀδάμαντι πελάσσας having fixed it firm as adamant , (Oracle quoted in Herdotus Historicus) 3. the diamond , (Theophrastus Philosophus) 4. as adjective, metaphorically, the inflexible , of Hades, (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) (ML)

G6135.strongs_def: Adar, 6th month of the civil calendar, 12 month of the religious calendar

G6140.strongs_def: garrulity, idle talk , (Aristophanes Comicus), etc.; (Theophrastus Philosophus) wrote περὶ ἀδολεσχίας. (ML)

G6141.strongs_def: 1. to be held in no esteem, to stand in ill repute , (Euripides) 2. transitive to hold in no esteem , τινα (Plutarch) (ML)

G6142.strongs_def: 1. in the primary sense it seems to mean thick : (akin to ἀδ-ινός, as κυδρός to κυδνός): 2. of things, χιόνα ἁδρὴν πίπτουσαν falling thick , (Herdotus Historicus):—; strong , great in any way, ἁδρὸς πόλεμος (Aristophanes Comicus) 3. of persons, large, fine, well-grown , (Herdotus Historicus); of animals, (Xenophon Historicus); of fruit or corn, full-grown, ripe , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G6143.strongs_def: 1. to make ripe, ripen , (Xenophon Historicus) 2. Pass. to grow ripe, ripen , of fruit or corn, (Herdotus Historicus), etc. (ML)

G6144.strongs_def: 1. want of strength or power, inability, incapacity , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; with genitive, ἀδ. τοῦ ἀδικεῖν for wrong-doing, (Plato Philosophus) 2. poverty , (Xenophon Historicus), etc. (ML)

G6146.strongs_def: not-working, idle , (Homer), etc.;—; ἀεργοὶ δόμοι idle houses, i. e. where people are idle , (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus)—;Cf. attic ἀργός. (ML)

G6147.strongs_def: ἀηδία, -ας, ἡ (ἀ- neg., ἦδος, pleasure), [in LXX: Pr 2329 (שִׂיחַ)* ;] __1. of things or persons, unpleasantness, odiousness (Hipp., Dem., al.); __2. dislike (Plat.), disagreement (MM, VGT, see word): Luk.23:12 D. † (AS)

G6148.strongs_def: Athanim or Ethanim, or Tishri; the first month of the civil calendar and seventh month of the religious calendar

G6152.strongs_def: want of heart, faintheartedness , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; εἰς ἀθυμίαν καθιστάναι τινά (Plato Philosophus); ἀθυμίαν παρέχειν τινί (Xenophon Historicus); ἐν ἀθυμίαι εἶναι (Xenophon Historicus); ἀθυμία ἐμπίπτει τινί (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G6153.strongs_def: 1. not offered , i. e. neglected , ἱερὰ ἄθ., Lat. sacra inauspicata, (Aeschines Orator) 2. active without sacrificing , ἄθυτος ἀπελθεῖν (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G6156.strongs_def: 1. to be ashamed to do a thing, with infinitive, (Homer), etc.; rarely with participle, αἴδεσαι μὲν πατέρα προλείπων feel ashamed of deserting him, (Sophocles Tragicus):—;absolute, αἰδεσθείς from a sense of shame , (Iliad by Homer) 2. with accusative pers. to stand in awe of, fear, respect , αἰδεῖο θεούς (Iliad by Homer), etc.; and of things, αἴδεσσαι μέλαθρον respect the house, (Iliad by Homer); ὅρκον αἰδεσθείς (Sophocles Tragicus) 3. to feel regard for a person, μήδε τί μ᾽ αἰδόμενος μήδ᾽ ἐλεαίρων (Odyssey by Homer) (ML)

G6157.strongs_def: 1. of persons, regarded with reverence, august, venerable , and of women, deserving respect, tender , (Homer) 2. active shamefaced, reverent , (Odyssey by Homer):—;adverb -ως, reverently , (Odyssey by Homer) 3. comparative αἰδοιότερος, (Odyssey by Homer); Sup. αἰδοιέστατος, (Pindar) (ML)

G6159.strongs_def: clear, bright, fair , of weather, (Homeric Hymns); epithet of Ζεύς, (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) (ML)

G6165.strongs_def: praise, fame , ἐν αἴνηι ἐών (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G6167.strongs_def: 1. a goat , Lat. caper, capra, (Homer) 2. αἲξ ἄγριος the wild goat, the ibex , (Homer) 3. αἶγες, old name for waves . Prob. not from ἀί̈σσω, of which the root is αικ. (ML)

G6168.strongs_def: 1. a herd of goats , (Iliad by Homer), etc. 2. a goat-pasture , [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

G6170.strongs_def: 1. that may be taken or conquered , (Herdotus Historicus); that may be understood , (Plato Philosophus) 2. ( αἱρέομαι) to be chosen, eligible , (Plato Philosophus), etc.; ζοῆς πονηρᾶς θάνατος αἱρετώτερος (Menander Comicus) 3. chosen, elected , (Plato Philosophus), etc. (ML)

G6171.strongs_def: 1. of or for perception by the senses, perceptive , (Plato Philosophus), etc.:—;adverb αἰσθητικῶς ἔχειν to be quick of perception , (Aristotle Philosopher) 2. of things, perceptible , (Plutarch) (ML)

G6174.strongs_def: 1. to charge, accuse, censure, blame , with accusative pers., τάχα κεν καὶ ἀναίτιον αἰτιόωιτο (Iliad by Homer); αἰτ. τινά τινος to accuse of a thing, (Herdotus Historicus), etc.;—;with infinitive, αἰτ. τινα ποιεῖν τι to accuse one of doing, (Herdotus Historicus):—;in this signification, certain tenses are used in passive sense, to be accused , aor1 ἠιτιάθην (Thucydides); perfect ἠιτίαμαι (Thucydides) 2. with accusative rei, to lay to one's charge, impute , τοῦτο αἰτ. (Xenophon Historicus); ταῦτα (Demosthenes Orator); with double accusative, τί ταῦτα τοὺς Λάκωνας αἰτιώμεθαa (Aristophanes Comicus) 3. to allege as the cause , αἰτ. τινα αἴτιον (Plato Philosophus); φωνάς τε καὶ ἄλλα μυρία αἰτ. (Plato Philosophus); τῆς ἱερᾶς χώρας ἠιτιᾶτο εἶναι he alleged that it was part of the sacred territory, (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

G6187.strongs_def: 1. unmoved, motionless , of Delos, (Oracle quoted in Herdotus Historicus); ἐξ ἀκινήτου ποδός without stirring a step, (Sophocles Tragicus) 2. idle, sluggish , (Aristophanes Comicus) 3. unmoved, unaltered , of laws, (Thucydides), etc. 4. immovable, hard to move , (Plato Philosophus):—;adverb, ἀκινήτως ἔχειν to be immovable , (Plato Philosophus), etc. 5. not to be stirred or touched, inviolate , Lat. non movendus, τάφος (Herdotus Historicus): proverbial of sacred things, κινεῖν τὰ ἀκίνητα (Herdotus Historicus); also τἀκίνητα φράσαι (Sophocles Tragicus) 6. of persons, not to be shaken, steadfast, stubborn , (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G6188.strongs_def: 1. a point, the barb of an arrow or hook, (Plutarch) 2. metaphorically, πόθων ἀκίδες the stings of desire, [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

G6190.strongs_def: 1. a point, edge : proverbial, ἐπὶ ξυροῦ ἀκμῆς on the rasor's edge (see. ξυρόν); ἀμφιδέξιοι ἀκμαί the fingers of both hands, (Sophocles Tragicus); ποδοῖν ἀκμαί the toes, (Sophocles Tragicus) 2. the highest point of anything, the bloom, flower, prime , of man's age, Lat. flos aetatis, ἀκμὴ ἥβης (Sophocles Tragicus); ἀκμὴ βίου (Xenophon Historicus); ἐν ἀκμῆι εἶναι = ἀκμάζειν, (Plato Philosophus); ἀκμὴν ἔχειν, of corn, to be ripe, (Thucydides); also of time, ἀ. ἦρος the spring- prime , (Pindar); ἀ. θέρους mid -summer, (Xenophon Historicus); ἀ. τῆς δόξης (Thucydides); periphrastic like βία, ἀκμὴ Θησειδᾶν (Sophocles Tragicus) 3. like καιρός, the best, most fitting time , [variant datesTragica Adespota; ἔργων, λόγων ἀκμή the time for doing, speaking, (Sophocles Tragicus); ἀκμή ἐστι, with infinitive, 'tis high time to do, (Aeschulus Tragicus); ἐπ᾽ ἀκμῆς εἶναι, with infinitive, to be on the point of doing, (Euripides); ἐπ᾽ αὐτὴν ἥκει τὴν ἀκμήν 'tis come to the critical time , (Demosthenes Orator) 4. ἀκμήν, accusative of ἀκμή, used as adverb, just , (Xenophon Historicus) 5. yet, still , (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) (ML)

G6191.strongs_def: 1. originally probably a thunderbolt , ἄκμων οὐρανόθεν κατιών (Hesiod) 2. an anvil , (Homer), etc.: metaphorically, λόγχης ἄκμονες very anvils to bear blows, (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

G6192.strongs_def: 1. Lat. non castigatus, unchastised, undisciplined, unbridled, (Herdotus Historicus), attic, etc. 2. licentious, intemperate , opposite to σώφρων, (Sophocles Tragicus), etc.:—; so in adverb, ἀκολάστως ἔχειν (Plato Philosophus); comparative, ἀκολαστοτέρως ἔχειν πρός τι to be too intemperate in a thing, (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G6193.strongs_def: to sharpen, whet , μαχαίρας (Aristophanes Comicus); λόγχην (Xenophon Historicus):—;Mid., ἀκονᾶσθαι μαχαίρας to sharpen their swords, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G6194.strongs_def: 1. to hurl a javelin , τινός at one, (Iliad by Homer); ἐπί τινι (Iliad by Homer):—;the weapon is put in dative, ἀκόντισε δουρί darted with his spear, (Iliad by Homer); also in accusative, ἀκόντισαν ὀξέα δοῦρα darted their spears, (Odyssey by Homer) 2. with accusative pers. to hit with a javelin , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; Pass. to be so hit or wounded , (Euripides) 3. to shoot forth rays , of the moon, (Euripides) 4. intransitive to pierce , εἴσω γῆς (Euripides) (ML)

G6196.strongs_def: 1. without order, disorderly , (Aeschulus Tragicus):—;in (Homer) of Thersites' words, disorderly :—; adverb -μως, (Herdotus Historicus), etc. 2. κόσμος ἄκοσμος, a world that is no world , [variant datesAnthology Palantina; also of an inappropriate ornament, [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

G6200.strongs_def: 1. heard, audible , (Homeric Hymns), etc. 2. that should be heard , (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G6202.strongs_def: 1. a headland, foreland, cape , (Homer), etc. 2. a mountain-top, summit : used by (Homer) only in the phrase κατ᾽ ἄκρης from top to bottom , i. e. utterly , πόλιν αἱρέειν κατ᾽ ἄκρης (Herdotus Historicus); so in attic, κατ᾽ ἄκρας utterly , [variant datesTragica Adespota, (Plato Philosophus) 3. the citadel of a city, Lat. arx, (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G6204.strongs_def: 1. to hearken to, listen to , with genitive pers., accusative rei, (Thucydides), etc.; with genitive rei, (Thucydides) 2. absolute to listen , ὁ ἀκροώμενος a hearer, disciple , (Plato Philosophus) 3. to attend to, obey , τινός (Thucydides), etc. (ML)

G6205.strongs_def: 1. a hearing or listening , (Thucydides), etc. 2. obedience to another, with genitive, (Thucydides) (ML)

G6208.strongs_def: 1. at the furthest point , and so either topmost = Lat. summus, or outermost = Lat. extremus: 2. highest, topmost , ἐν ἄκρηι πόλει = ἐν ἀκροπόλει, (Iliad by Homer); μέλαν ὕδωρ ἄκρον at its surface , (Iliad by Homer), etc. 3. outermost , ἄκρη χείρ, ἄκροι πόδες, ἄκρος ὦμος the end of the hand, ends of the feet, tip of the shoulder, (Iliad by Homer); ἐπ᾽ ἄκρων [ δακτύλων] on tiptoe , (Sophocles Tragicus); ἄκροισι λαίφους κρασπέδοις with the outermost edges of the sail, i. e. under close-reefed sails, (Euripides) 4. of Time, it denotes completeness , ἄκραι σὺν ἑσπέραι when eve was fully come , (Pindar); ἄκρας νυκτός at dead of night, (Sophocles Tragicus) 5. of Degree, the highest in its kind, exceeding good, consummate, excellent : of persons, (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; ἄκρος μάντις (Sophocles Tragicus):—;often with an accusative modi added, ψυχὴν οὐκ ἄκρος not strong in mind, (Herdotus Historicus); ἄκροι τὰ πολέμια, skilful in war, (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; also with genitive modi, οἱ ἄκροι τῆς ποιήσεως (Plato Philosophus); also, ἄκρος εἰς or περί τι (Plato Philosophus) 6. as Substantive, see. ἄκρα, ἄκρον. 7. neuter as adverb on the top or surface , just , ἄκρον ἐπὶ ῥηγμῖνος on the very edge of the surf, il. 8. exceedingly , (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) 9. utterly, completely , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G6210.strongs_def: 1. any prominent part , ἀκρ. τοῦ οὔρεος a mountain- peak , (Herdotus Historicus) 2. a cape, promontory , (Herdotus Historicus) 3. the extremity of anything, ἀκρ. νηός a ship's beak , (Herdotus Historicus) 4. in plural the extremities of the body, hands and feet, fingers and toes , (Thucydides), etc.; τὰ ἀκρ. τῆς Νίκης her wings , (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

G6211.strongs_def: 1. without authority : 2. of laws and contracts, invalid , ἄκυρον ποιεῖν, Lat. irritum facere, to set aside, and ἄκυρον γίγνεσθαι, to become of no force , to be set aside, (Plato Philosophus); νόμοις ἀκύροις χρωμένη, i. e. having laws, but not enforcing them, (Thucydides) 3. of persons, having no right or power , ἄκ. ποιεῖν τινά (Xenophon Historicus); with genitive, ἄκυροι πάντων γενήσεσθε (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

G6212.strongs_def: to make false pretensions , of the Sophists, (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G6213.strongs_def: 1. = ἀλαλαγή, a shouting . 2. a loud noise , τυμπάνων, αὐλοῦ (Euripides) (ML)

G6215.strongs_def: 1. to wander, stray or roam about , (Homer), etc.: to wander from home, be banished , (Sophocles Tragicus); with accusative loci, ἀλ. γῆν to wander over the land, (Sophocles Tragicus) 2. with genitive to wander away from, cease to enjoy , εὐφροσύνας (Pindar); τῆς πάροιθ᾽ εὐπραξίας (Euripides) 3. metaphorically to wander in mind, be distraught , (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G6216.strongs_def: 1. to feel bodily pain, suffer , (Iliad by Homer), etc.; the suffering part in accusative, ἀλγ. ἧπαρ (Aeschulus Tragicus); τὸν δάκτυλον, τὰ ὄμματα (Plato Philosophus) 2. to suffer hardship , (Odyssey by Homer) 3. to feel pain of mind, to grieve, be troubled or distressed , ἀλγεῖν ψυχήν, φρένα (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; ἀλγ. τινί to be pained at a thing, (Herdotus Historicus); ἐπί τινι (Sophocles Tragicus); διά τι (Herdotus Historicus); περί τι or τινος (Thucydides); with genitive, (Aeschulus Tragicus); with accusative, ἀλγῶ μὲν ἔργα (Aeschulus Tragicus); with participle, ἤλγης᾽ ἀκούσας (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G6217.strongs_def: 1. a sense of pain, pain, suffering , (Herdotus Historicus), etc. 2. of mind, pain, grief , (Sophocles Tragicus), etc. (ML)

G6220.strongs_def: 1. pain of body, (Iliad by Homer) 2. pain of mind, grief, distress , (Homer) 3. anything that causes pain , [Refs 2nd c.BC, variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

G6221.strongs_def: anything used for anointing, unguent, fat, oil , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G6222.strongs_def: to grind, bruise, pound , (Odyssey by Homer) (ML)

G6226.strongs_def: 1. to be taken, conquered , of persons and places, (Homer), etc.; ἁλίσκεσθαι εἰς πολεμίους to fall into the hands of the enemy, (Plato Philosophus) 2. to be caught, seized , θανάτῳ ἁλῶναι or without θανάτῳ, to die , (Homer); ἑάλωσαν εἰς Ἀθήνας γράμματα letters were seized and taken to Athens, (Xenophon Historicus) 3. in good sense, to be won, achieved, attained , (Sophocles Tragicus), etc. 4. with participle to be caught or detected doing a thing, (Herdotus Historicus); ἐὰν ἁλῷς τοῦτο πράττων (Plato Philosophus); also with a Substantive or adjective, the participle ὤν being omitted, οὐ γὰρ δὴ φονεὺς ἁλώσομαι (Sophocles Tragicus) 5. as attic law-term, to be convicted and condemned , (Plato Philosophus):—;with genitive criminis, to be convicted of , ἁλῶναι ψευδομαρτυριῶν, etc. (ML)

G6228.strongs_def: that which is given or taken in exchange: the price of a thing, [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

G6230.strongs_def: 1. to make different, to change, alter , (Plato Philosophus), etc. 2. Pass. with future middle ἀλλοιώσομαι and passive ἀλλοιωθήσομαι:—; to become different, be changed , (Thucydides) 3. to be changed for the worse , (Xenophon Historicus) Hence (ML)

G6232.strongs_def: 1. with genitive pers. to estrange from , τῶν σωμάτων τὴν πόλιν (Thucydides) 2. with dative pers. to make hostile to another, τὴν χώραν τοῖς πολεμίοις (Xenophon Historicus):—;Pass. to be made an enemy , τινι (Thucydides) 3. in Pass. of things, to be alienated, fall into other hands , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G6234.strongs_def: estrangement , τῆς ξυμμαχίας οὐχ ὁμοία ἡ ἀλλ. its estrangement , its loss , (Thucydides) (ML)

G6236.strongs_def: a spring, leap, bound , (Odyssey by Homer); ἅλμα πέτρας a leap or fall from the rock, (Euripides); κυνῆς ἅλμα the leap of the lot from the helmet, (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G6237.strongs_def: 1. sea-water, brine , (Odyssey by Homer), etc.: spray that has dried on the skin , (Odyssey by Homer): a salt incrustation on soil, (Herdotus Historicus) 2. the brine, i. e. the sea , (Pindar) (ML)

G6239.strongs_def: 1. salt, briny , (Odyssey by Homer) 2. of taste, salt, brackish , (Thucydides) 3. metaphorically bitter, distasteful , Lat. amarus, (Plato Philosophus), etc.; ἁλμυρὰ κλαίειν to weep bitterly , (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) (ML)

G6241.strongs_def: 1. anything used for anointing, hog's-lard, grease, unguent , (Homer) 2. laying on of unguents or paint, ἀλ. μύρων (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G6242.strongs_def: a glade or grove , Lat. saltus, (Homer); grove , (Odyssey by Homer), etc. (ML)

G6245.strongs_def: 1. peeled or pearl-barley ; singular only in phrase ἀλφίτου ἀκτή, barley- meal, Lat. polenta, (Homer): in plural ἄλφιτα, barley-groats, barley-meal , opposite to ἄλευρα, (Homer), attic 2. metaphorically one's daily bread , (Aristophanes Comicus); πατρῶια ἄλφ. one's patrimony , (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G6248.strongs_def: 1. a wagon, wain , opposite to the war-chariot ( ἅρμα), Lat. plaustrum, (Homer) 2. with genitive a wagon-load of , πετρῶν, σίτου (Xenophon Historicus) 3. the carriage of the plough , Lat. currus, (Hesiod):—; Charles' wain in the heavens, the Great Bear ( ἄρκτος), (Homer) 4. = ἁμαξιτός, [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

G6252.strongs_def: 1. dimly seen, dim, faint, baffling sight , εἴδωλον ἀμ. a shadowy spectre, (Odyssey by Homer) 2. having no light, darksome , νύξ (Lucian):—; blind, sightless , (Sophocles Tragicus); so, ἀμαυρῶι κώλωι with blind foot, said of a blind man, (Sophocles Tragicus) 3. metaphorically, 4. dim, obscure, uncertain , κληδών (Aeschulus Tragicus); ἐλπίς (Plutarch) 5. obscure, unknown , (Hesiod) 6. gloomy, troubled , φρήν (Aeschulus Tragicus) 7. active enfeebling , νοῦσος [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

G6253.strongs_def: to make dim, faint , or obscure , (Xenophon Historicus); metaphorically to impair , (Euripides), etc.:—;Pass. to become dim, suffer eclipse , of the sun, (Herdotus Historicus); to disappear , (Hesiod) (ML)

G6254.strongs_def: to blunt, take the edge off a sharp instrument, and metaphorically to make dull , ὄμματος αὐγήν [variant datesAnthology Palantina:—;Pass. to become dull, lose its edge or force , (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

G6255.strongs_def: 1. to milk sheep and goats; βόας (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus): —;Mid., in metaphorically sense, ἀμέλγεσθαι τοὺς ξένους to milk them dry, (Aristophanes Comicus) 2. to draw milk from the animals, ἀμ. γάλα (Herdotus Historicus); Pass., ὄϊες ἀμελγόμεναι γάλα having milk drawn from them, milch- ewes, (Iliad by Homer) 3. metaphorically to squeeze out like milk, to press out , ἐκ βοτρύων ξανθὸν ἄμελξε γάνος [variant datesAnthology Palantina 4. to drink , (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) (ML)

G6258.strongs_def: 1. unmeasured, immeasurable, immense , (Odyssey by Homer), etc. 2. unnumbered, countless , (Euripides) (ML)

G6259.strongs_def: 1. a reaping, harvesting , (Iliad by Homer) (metaphorically of slaughter ). 2. harvest, harvest time , (Hesiod) 3. the crop or harvest reaped , Lat. seges, [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

G6260.strongs_def: (Euripides), χρημάτων ἀμ. without reward of money, (Plutarch) (ML)

G6264.strongs_def: an error, fault, offence , (Aeschulus Tragicus), etc.:—;also, metri grat., ἀπλάκημα, (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

G6266.strongs_def: unspeakable, unspeakably many or great , (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

G6271.strongs_def: in the midland or interior , Lat. mediterraneus, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G6273.strongs_def: 1. a going up, mounting on horseback, (Xenophon Historicus):—; πᾶσα ἄμβασις = πάντες ἀναβάται, all the horsemen , (Sophocles Tragicus) 2. an expedition up from the coast into Central Asia, as that of the younger Cyrus, (Xenophon Historicus) 3. a way up, ascent of a tower or mountain, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G6274.strongs_def: to raise or lift up, carry , (Lucian) (ML)

G6275.strongs_def: one mounted , of Pentheus in the tree, (Euripides): a horseman, rider , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G6276.strongs_def: to shoot up, grow up again , of Plants, (Plato Philosophus); of a city, (Herdotus Historicus); of misfortunes, to spring up, be rank , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G6277.strongs_def: to boil well, seethe , with accusative, (Aristophanes Comicus); absolute, ἀναβράττετ᾽, ἐξοπτᾶτε (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G6279.strongs_def: 1. to yoke again , ἀναζευγνύναι τὸν στρατόν to move off the army, (Herdotus Historicus); ἀν. τὸ στρατόπεδον to break up the camp, (Herdotus Historicus); ἀν. τὰς νῆας to move Them back, (Herdotus Historicus) 2. absolute to break up, shift one's quarters , (Thucydides) (ML)

G6280.strongs_def: 1. to boil up or bubble up , (Sophocles Tragicus) 2. ἀναζ. εὐλάς to swarm with worms, a kind of disease, (Plutarch); also, εὐλαὶ ἀναζέουσιν (Plutarch) (ML)

G6282.strongs_def: 1. shameless , (Homer) 2. with genitive, ἀναιδέα δηϊοτῆτος insatiate of strife, (Iliad by Homer) 3. of things, λᾶας ἀναιδής the reckless stone, of Sisyphus, (Odyssey by Homer); ἔργ᾽ ἀναιδῆ (Sophocles Tragicus): —; τὸ ἀναιδές, contracted τἀνειδές, = ἀναίδεια, (Euripides); ἐπὶ τὸ ἀναιδέστερον τραπέσθαι (Herdotus Historicus) 4. adverb -δῶς, (Sophocles Tragicus), etc. (ML)

G6284.strongs_def: 1. to light up , (Odyssey by Homer), etc.:—;Mid. to light oneself a fire, (Herdotus Historicus) 2. Pass., metaphorically to fire up , with anger, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G6285.strongs_def: 1. to call up the dead , (Aeschulus Tragicus); so in Mid., (Euripides) 2. to call again and again : 3. to invoke, appeal to , θεούς (Herdotus Historicus), etc.;—;so in Mid., (Sophocles Tragicus) 4. to summon, cite , (Herdotus Historicus):—;Mid. to call to oneself, send for, summon , (Euripides) 5. to call by a name, ἀν. κακούς (Euripides); Δαναούς (Thucydides):—;Pass., Ἀργεῖος ἀνακαλούμενος (Sophocles Tragicus) 6. to call on , so as to encourage, (Thucydides); Mid., ἀνακαλεῖσθαι τὰς κύνας to cheer on the hounds, (Xenophon Historicus) 7. to call back, recall , mostly in Mid., (Aeschulus Tragicus); especially from exile, (Plato Philosophus); ἀνακαλεῖσθαι τῆι σάλπιγγι to sound a retreat, (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G6287.strongs_def: leaning back : ἀν. θρόνος a seat with a back , (Plutarch) (ML)

G6288.strongs_def: 1. to push back, stop short, check , ἵππον χαλινῶι (Xenophon Historicus) 2. Mid., ἀνακρούεσθαι πρύμνην to put one's ship astern, by backing water, (Aristophanes Comicus); so ἀνακρούεσθαι alone, (Thucydides); also, ἐπὶ πρύμνην ἀν., (Herdotus Historicus):—;metaphorically to put back , (Plato Philosophus) 3. in Music, to strike up , (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) (ML)

G6289.strongs_def: 1. to flame up, take fire , (Xenophon Historicus) 2. metaphorically to break out anew , as war, (Plutarch) 3. to come to oneself again, revive , (Plutarch) (ML)

G6290.strongs_def: 1. without pain , and so: 2. of persons, insensible to pain , (Aristotle Philosopher) 3. unfeeling, hard-hearted, ruthless , (Sophocles Tragicus); ἀναλγητότερος εἶναι to feel less grieved , (Thucydides): with genitive, ἀν. εἶναί τινος to be insensible to , (Plutarch):—;adverb -τως, unfeelingly , (Sophocles Tragicus) 4. of things, not painful , (Sophocles Tragicus) 5. cruel , πάθος (Euripides) (ML)

G6291.strongs_def: 1. to pick up, gather up , ὀστέα (Iliad by Homer):—;Mid. to pick up for oneself , (Herdotus Historicus); ἀν. πνεῦμα to collect one's breath, [variant datesAnthology Palantina 2. to reckon up , τὸν χρόνον (Plutarch): —;Pass., ἀναλεγόμενον being recounted , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G6294.strongs_def: 1. to mix up, mix together , (Odyssey by Homer), etc.:—;Pass. to be mixed with others, (Herdotus Historicus), attic: to have intercourse , (Plutarch) 2. ἀναμίσγω, poetry and ionic for ἀναμίγνυμι, only in present and imperfect 3. to mix one thing with another, τί τινι (Odyssey by Homer): —;Pass. to have intercourse , τινι (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G6296.strongs_def: 1. to throw the head back , in token of denial (which we express by shaking the head) , (Homer), etc. 2. with accusative rei, to deny, refuse , (Iliad by Homer) (ML)

G6298.strongs_def: to dry up things, of the wind, (Iliad by Homer); to dry up a stream, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G6299.strongs_def: 1. a repose, rest , (Hesiod); μεριμνῶν from cares, (Theognis Elegiacus) 2. a resting-place , [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

G6300.strongs_def: be effronted; to have a look of effrontery

G6302.strongs_def: 1. to breathe again, take breath , (Iliad by Homer), etc.: to recover from a thing, with genitive, (Iliad by Homer), etc.; so, ἔκ τινος (Herdotus Historicus):—; absolute to revive , (Xenophon Historicus); and in this sense (Homer) uses ἄμπνυτο, ἀμπνύνθη. 2. to draw breath, breathe , (Pindar) 3. to breathe forth, send forth , καπνόν (Pindar) (ML)

G6303.strongs_def: 1. recovery of breath, revival , (Pindar); μόχθων ἀμπνοά rest from toils, (Pindar) 2. a drawing breath, respiration , (Aristophanes Comicus); ἀμπνοὰς ἔχειν = ἀναπνέειν, to breathe , (Sophocles Tragicus); τὴν ἀν. ἀπολαβεῖν τινος to strangle him. 3. a breathing organ , of the mouth, (Lucian); an air-hole , (Plutarch) (ML)

G6304.strongs_def: to die in a place, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G6307.strongs_def: 1. properly of a bird, to raise its feathers : hence, ἀν. ἐθείρας (Euripides) 2. metaphorically to set on the wing, excite vehemently , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.:—; Pass. to be in a state of excitement , (Aeschulus Tragicus), etc. (ML)
