G6308.strongs_def: 1. to snatch up , (Iliad by Homer) 2. to snatch away, carry off , (Homer), etc.; of slave-dealers, to kidnap , (Odyssey by Homer):—;Pass., (Sophocles Tragicus): in Prose also, to be dragged before a magistrate, carried off to prison , Lat. rapi in jus, (Demosthenes Orator) 3. in good sense, to rescue , (Plutarch) 4. to take by storm, plunder , (Euripides); of persons, ἀναρπασόμενος τοὺς Φωκέας to take them by storm or at once , (Herdotus Historicus) 5. to carry off, steal , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

(Plato Philosophus); ὡς or ὅτι μ., Lat. quam maxime, (Plato Philosophus); ὅσον μ. (Aeschulus Tragicus); ὡς μ. certainly , in answers, (Plato Philosophus); ὡς δύναμαι μ. (Plato Philosophus); μακρῷ μ. (ML)

Dep., used in present and imperfect : 2. intransitive to work for one's daily bread ; generally, to toil, work, labour , (Homer) 3. to be poor or needy , Solon , (Euripides), etc. 4. with genitive to be poor in, have need of , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 5. transitive to work at, prepare, get ready , δαῖτα πένοντο (Odyssey by Homer); τί σε χρὴ ταῦτα πένεσθα; (Odyssey by Homer) (ML)

(i.e. ἡμέρα); the fiftieth day (after the Passover), Pentecost , (New Testament) (ML)

G8717.strongs_def: looked at from all sides, admired of all observers , (Euripides) (ML)

[ ξίφεος] a scabbard, (Euripides): absolute of walls round a town, ἑπτάπυργοι π. (Euripides) 2. a space enclosed, compass , οἰκίης μεγάλης περιβολή a house of large compass , (Herdotus Historicus) 3. a circumference, circuit , (Thucydides); π. ποιεῖσθαι to make a circuit , (Xenophon Historicus) 4. metaphorically, 5. a compassing, endeavouring after , τῆς ἀρχῆς, Lat. affectatio imperii, (Xenophon Historicus) 6. ἡ π. τοῦ λόγου the whole compass of the matter, long and short of it, (Isocrates Orator) (ML)

G8723.strongs_def: 1. with two right hands , i.e. using both hands alike , (Iliad by Homer) 2. very dexterous , (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G8725.strongs_def: 1. to be around a place, with dative, (Thucydides); τὰ περιόντα circumstances , (Demosthenes Orator) 2. to be better than, superior to another, surpass, excel , with genitive, (Iliad by Homer); περίεσσι γυναικῶν εἶδός τε μέγεθός τε (Odyssey by Homer); οἳ περὶ μὲν βουλὴν Δαναῶν περὶ δd ἐστὲ μάχεσθαι λπαρr εθυαλσs μάχην)) (Iliad by Homer); with dative rei, σοφίᾳ π. τῶν Ἑλλήνων (Plato Philosophus): absolute to be superior , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; ἐκ περιόντος at an advantage , (Thucydides) 3. to overlive, outlive , τινι (Herdotus Historicus): absolute to survive, remain alive , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.:—;of things, to be extant, to be in existence , (Herdotus Historicus) 4. to be over and above, to remain in hand , of property, money, etc., (Thucydides); οἰόμενοι περιεῖναι χρήματά τῳ imagining that any one has a balance in his hands, (Demosthenes Orator) 5. to be a result or consequence , περίεστιν ὑμῖν ἐκ τούτων what you have got by all this is . ., (Demosthenes Orator); τοσοῦτον ὑμῖν περίεστιν τοῦ πρὸς ἐμὲ μίσους you have so much hatred against me left , Philipp. quoted in (Demosthenes Orator); with infinitive, περίεστι ὑμῖν αὐτοῖς ἐρίζειν it remains for you to quarrel with them, (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

G8726.strongs_def: a girdle round the loins, apron , (Plutarch) (ML)

G8801.strongs_def: a making to wander, a dispersing , τῶν νεῶν (Thucydides) (ML)

G8802.strongs_def: the oriental plane , Lat. platanus, (Aristophanes Comicus) From πλατύς, because of its broad leaves. (ML)

G8804.strongs_def: mostly, most often, very often , (Xenophon Historicus), etc. (ML)

G8805.strongs_def: more frequently, oftener , (Plato Philosophus): several times, frequently , (Aristotle Philosopher) (ML)

G8809.strongs_def: 1. an advantage, gain, privilege , (Plato Philosophus): in plural gains, successes , (Xenophon Historicus) 2. an act of overreaching, selfish trick , (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

G8810.strongs_def: 1. a rib : mostly in plural the ribs, the side , (Iliad by Homer), etc.;—;also in singular, (Sophocles Tragicus) 2. of places, πλευρὸν νεῶν the side of the bay where the ships lay, (Sophocles Tragicus); τὸ δεξιὸν πλ. the right flank (of an army), (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G8811.strongs_def: a mistake in music, false note : metaphorically a fault, offence, error , (Plato Philosophus) from πλημμελέω (ML)

G8812.strongs_def: to make a false note in music : metaphorically to go wrong, offend, err , τι in a thing, (Euripides), etc.; εἴς τινα (Aeschines Orator):—;Pass., πλημμελεῖσθαι ὑπό τινος to be ill-treated by one, (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G8815.strongs_def: 1. a filling up, filling , (Plato Philosophus): often of eating and drinking, satiety , (Plato Philosophus) 2. the completion of a number , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G8816.strongs_def: 1. near, close to , with genitive or dative, πλησίοι ἀλλήλων or ἀλλήλοισι (Homer):—;absolute near, neighbouring , (Iliad by Homer), etc.:—;as Substantive a neighbour , ἰδὼν ἐς πλ. ἄλλον (Iliad by Homer), etc. 2. adverb πλησίον, doric πλα_τίον, = πέλας, near, nigh, hard by , with genitive, (Homer), etc.; with dative, (Euripides) 3. with the Art., ὁ πλησίον (i.e. ὤν); one's neighbour , (Theognis Elegiacus), etc.; so in doric, ὁ πλα_τίον (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus):—;also, with Substantives, ὁ πλ. παράδεισος (Xenophon Historicus) 4. comparative πλησιαίτερος, Sup. -αίτατος, (Xenophon Historicus)—;comparative adverb πλησιαιτέρω, (Herdotus Historicus); -αίτερον, (Xenophon Historicus); Sup. -αίτατα, (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G8818.strongs_def: 1. to make into bricks , τὴν γῆν (Herdotus Historicus):—;absolute to make bricks , (Aristophanes Comicus);—;so in Mid., thuc. 2. to build of brick , τείχη (Aristophanes Comicus) 3. to make in the form of a plinth or brick , (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G8819.strongs_def: 1. a small brick , (Thucydides) 2. = πλαίσιον, a rectangle or square , (Plutarch) (ML)

G8820.strongs_def: a brick , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; πλίνθους ἑλκύσαι, εἰρύσαι, Lat. ducere lateres, to make bricks , (Herdotus Historicus); ὀπτᾶν to bake them, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G8822.strongs_def: 1. a twining: anything woven, a web , (Euripides) 2. metaphorically the complication of a plot, opposite to λύσις, (Aristotle Philosopher) (ML)

G8824.strongs_def: 1. floating , (Odyssey by Homer); πλωτοί swimmers , i. e. fish, [variant datesAnthology Palantina 2. navigable , (Herdotus Historicus) 3. of seasons, fit for navigation , (Polybius Historicus) (ML)

G8827.strongs_def: the organ of breathing, the lungs , Lat. pulmo, (Iliad by Homer): mostly in plural, [variant datesTragica Adespota; πνεῦμ᾽ ἀνεὶς ἐκ πλευμόνων (Euripides) (ML)

G8828.strongs_def: 1. grass, herb , (Homer), etc.; ποία Μηδική, Lat. herba Medica, sainfoin or lucerne , (Aristophanes Comicus) 2. the grass , i. e. a grassy place , plat., (Xenophon Historicus) 3. in Poets, of Time, τέσσαρας πόας four grasses , i. e. summers , [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

G8829.strongs_def: 1. to long for, yearn after what is absent, to miss or regret what is lost, Lat. desiderare, (Homer), etc.; ποθεῖς τὸν οὐ παρόντα (Aristophanes Comicus); π. τὰς ἐν τῆι νεότητι ἡδονάς (Plato Philosophus):—;Pass., ὦ ποθουμένη (i.e. Εἰρήνη) (Aristophanes Comicus) 2. of things, to require , ποθεῖ ἡ ἀπόκρισις ἐρώτησιν τοιάνδε (Plato Philosophus) 3. with infinitive to be anxious to do, (Euripides); τὸ νοσοῦν ποθεῖ σε ξυμπαραστάτην λαβεῖν my sickness needs to take thee as an assistant, (Sophocles Tragicus) 4. absolute, τὸ ποθοῦν one's desiring, one's longing , (Sophocles Tragicus) 5. as Dep., ποθουμένη φρήν the longing soul, (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G8830.strongs_def: 1. a marking with various colours, embroidering, embroidery , (Plato Philosophus): in plural pieces of broidery , (Xenophon Historicus) 2. varied aspect, diversity , (Plato Philosophus) 3. versatility, subtlety, craft , (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

G8831.strongs_def: 1. to work in various colours, to broider, work in embroidery , (Euripides); χορὸν ποίκιλλε he wrought a χορός of cunning workmanship , (Iliad by Homer) 2. to embroider a robe, (Pindar), etc. 3. generally, to diversify, vary , (Euripides):—;of style, to embellish , (Pindar):—; to speak as in riddles , (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G8832.strongs_def: 1. a broidered stuff, brocade , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 2. broidered work, broidery , (Homer) 3. generally, a variety, diversity , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G8837.strongs_def: of or for a shepherd , (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus): —; ἡ -κή (i.e. τέχνη); (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G8838.strongs_def: 1. wool in its raw state, a fleece , (Iliad by Homer), etc.: a lock or tuft of wool , (Sophocles Tragicus) 2. proverbial in heterocl. accusative of 3rd declension, εἰς ὄνου πόκας to an ass shearing , i. e. to no-place, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G8839.strongs_def: 1. of or for war , (Thucydides); ἀσπὶς πολεμικωτάτη most fit for service , (Xenophon Historicus) 2. ἡ -κή (i.e. τέχνη); the art of war, war , (Plato Philosophus): —; τὰ πολεμικά warlike exercises , (Thucydides) 3. τὸ πολεμικόν the signal for battle , (Xenophon Historicus) 4. the military class , opposite to the civilian, (Aristotle Philosopher) 5. of persons, skilled in war, warlike , (Thucydides), etc. 6. like an enemy, stirring up hostility , (Xenophon Historicus):—;adverb, πολεμικῶς ἔχειν to be hostile , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G8840.strongs_def: 1. of or belonging to war , (Pindar), etc.: —; τὰ πολέμια whatever belongs to war, war and its business , (Herdotus Historicus), etc. 2. of or like an enemy, hostile , (Pindar), etc.:—;as Substantive an enemy , (Herdotus Historicus), attic; οἱ π. the enemy , (Thucydides): —; τὸ π. hostility , (Thucydides) 3. generally, opposed, adverse , (Herdotus Historicus) 4. of or from the enemy , (Aeschulus Tragicus); πολέμια, ων, τά, enemy's wares, contraband , (Aristophanes Comicus): —; ἡ πολεμία (i.e. γῆ, χώρα); the enemy's country , (Xenophon Historicus) 5. adverb -ίως, in hostile manner , (Thucydides) (ML)

G8841.strongs_def: 1. a warrior, combatant , (Iliad by Homer), etc. 2. π. ἵππος a war-horse, charger , (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) (ML)

G8843.strongs_def: 1. to hem in a city, blockade, beleaguer, besiege , (Herdotus Historicus), attic:—;Pass. to be besieged, in a state of siege , (Herdotus Historicus); of Scamander, to be dammed back , (Plato Philosophus) 2. metaphorically to be besieged, pestered , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G8844.strongs_def: 1. a besieging, siege , (Herdotus Historicus), etc. 2. metaphorically a besieging, pestering , (Plutarch) (ML)

G8845.strongs_def: 1. gray, grizzled, grisly , of wolves, of iron, of the sea, (Iliad by Homer) 2. mostly of hair, gray or hoary from age, (Homer); πολιοί gray-haired men , (Odyssey by Homer), etc.:—;absolute, αἱ πολιαί (i.e. τρίχες); (Pindar); ἅμα ταῖς πολιαῖς κατιούσαις as the gray hairs come down (i.e. from the temples to the beard), (Aristophanes Comicus); π. δάκρυον ἐμβαλών an old man's tear, (Euripides) 3. metaphorically hoary, venerable , (Euripides) 4. like λευκός, bright, clear, serene , (Hesiod) (ML)

G8847.strongs_def: 1. one of many , Lat. unus e multis, i.e. the smallest, least , (Thucydides), etc.:—; adverb, δευτέρως καὶ πολλοστῶς in a very small degree , (Aristotle Philosopher) 2. of Time, πολλοστῷ χρόνῳ after a very long time , (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G8856.strongs_def: 1. much-tangled, thick-wreathed , of a serpent's coils, (Euripides); of the polypus, with tangled, twisting arms , (Theognis Elegiacus) 2. metaphorically much-twisting, complex, intricate , [Refs 5th c.BC, 5th/4th c.BC, variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

G8860.strongs_def: 1. long-existing, of olden time, ancient , (Homeric Hymns) 2. lasting for long , (Aristotle Philosopher):—;comparative -ώτερος, (Plato Philosophus); Sup. -ώτατος, (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G8861.strongs_def: to be very careful , opposite to ὀλιγωρέω, (Aeschines Orator) (ML)

G8862.strongs_def: 1. in early Greek only as Dep. 2. absolute to work hard, do work, suffer toil , (Homer); περὶ δόρπα πονέοντο were busied about their supper, (Iliad by Homer); so, πεπόνητο καθ᾽ ἵππους was busy with the horses, of a charioteer, (Iliad by Homer) 3. metaphorically to be in distress, to distress oneself , (Iliad by Homer):—; to suffer, be sick , (Thucydides) 4. with accusative to work hard at, to make or do with pains or care , (Homer) 5. after (Homer), the active form prevails 6. intransitive to toil, labour , (Theognis Elegiacus), attic; μάτην π. to labour in vain, (Sophocles Tragicus); with accusative, τὰ μηδὲν ὠφελοῦντα μὴ πόνει do not labour at things that profit not, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 7. with accusative cognate, π. πόνον, μόχθους to go through, suffer them, [variant datesTragica Adespota; also with accusative partis, πονεῖν τὰ σκέλη (Aristophanes Comicus) 8. absolute to labour, be hard-pressed, suffer , (Thucydides): to be worn out, spoilt , (Demosthenes Orator) 9. Pass., impersonal, οὐκ ἄλλως αὐτοῖς πεπόνηται = πεπονήκασι, (Plato Philosophus) 10. transitive, 11. with accusative pers. to afflict, distress , (Pindar):—;Pass. to be worn out, to suffer greatly , (Sophocles Tragicus) 12. Pass., also, to be trained or educated , (Aristotle Philosopher) 13. with accusative rei, like ἐκπονεῖν, to gain by toil or labour , χρήματα (Xenophon Historicus): Pass. to be won or achieved by toil , (Pindar) (ML)

G8863.strongs_def: Dep. to be evil, act wickedly, play the rogue , (Aristotle Philosopher); οἱ πεπονηρευμένοι (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

G8864.strongs_def: to pass the sea , νῆυς ποντοποροῦσα sea-sailing , (Odyssey by Homer) from ποντοπόρος (ML)

G8866.strongs_def: a house of ill-fame, brothel , (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G8867.strongs_def: of or for harlots , π. τέλος the tax paid by brothel-keepers , (Aeschines Orator) (ML)

G8869.strongs_def: 1. a purple garment or covering , (Xenophon Historicus) 2. a red-coloured bird , (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G8874.strongs_def: drinking, a drinking-bout, carousal , (Xenophon Historicus); παρὰ πότον, Lat. inter pocula, (Xenophon Historicus); ἐν τοῖς πότοις (Aeschines Orator) (ML)

G8876.strongs_def: a selling, sale , ὠνῇ τε καὶ πρήσι (ionic dative) χρέονται (Herdotus Historicus); ἐπὶ πρήσι for sale , (Herdotus Historicus); πρᾶσιν ποιεῖσθαι (Aeschines Orator) (ML)

G8879.strongs_def: 1. to make soft, mild or gentle, to soften, soothe, calm , (Hesiod), etc.; πρ. ἕλκος to soothe a raging sore, (Sophocles Tragicus); πρ. τινὰ λόγοις (Aeschulus Tragicus):—;Pass. to become soft or gentle, grow milder , (Herdotus Historicus); of passion, to abate , (Herdotus Historicus) 2. to tame wild animals, (Hesiod) (ML)

G8880.strongs_def: 1. a gift of honour , such as was offered to elders, (Iliad by Homer) 2. the privilege of age , and generally, a privilege , (Plato Philosophus), etc. 3. the right of the eldest, his share of the inheritance , (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

G8881.strongs_def: 1. an old man , Lat. senex, (the prose form is πρεσβύτης); (Sophocles Tragicus):—; ὁ πρέσβυς is used much like ὁ πρεσβύτερος, the elder , (Aeschulus Tragicus):—;plural πρέσβεις, elders , always implying dignity, chiefs, princes , (Aeschulus Tragicus); epic πρέσβηες (Hesiod) 2. (Homer) uses only the comparative and Sup., comparative πρεσβύτερος, α, ον, elder, older , (Iliad by Homer), attic; ἐνιαυτῷ by a year, (Aristophanes Comicus); βουλαὶ πρεσβύτεραι the wise councils of age , (Pindar);—;Sup. πρεσβύτατος, η, ον, eldest , (Iliad by Homer), etc.: —;the comparative and Sup. were used of things, πρεσβύτερόν τι (or οὐδὲν); ἔχειν = Lat. aliquid (or nihil) antiquius habere, to deem higher, more important , τὰ τοῦ θεοῦ πρεσβύτερα ποιεῖσθαι ἢ τὰ τῶν ἀνδρῶν (Herdotus Historicus); πρεσβύτατον κρίνειν τι (Thucydides); πρεσβυτέρως γυμναστικὴν μουσικῆς τετιμηκέναι more highly than . . , (Plato Philosophus): —;hence, merely of magnitude, πρεσβύτερον κακὸν κακοῦ one evil greater than another, (Sophocles Tragicus) 3. like πρεσβευτής, an ambassador , (Aeschulus Tragicus);—;plural πρέσβεις is more used than πρεσβευταί, (Aristophanes Comicus), etc. 4. a chief, president : comparative πρεσβύτερος, an elder of the Jewish Council , (New Testament), etc.: an elder of the Church, presbyter , (New Testament) (ML)

G8882.strongs_def: 1. to blow up, swell out by blowing , ἔπρησεν δ᾽ ἄνεμος μέσον ἱστίον (Odyssey by Homer) 2. to blow out, drive out by blowing , τὸ δ᾽ [ αἷμα] ἀνὰ στόμα πρῆσε he blew a shower of blood through his mouth, (Iliad by Homer) (ML)

G8883.strongs_def: 1. to have a thing sold to one, to buy, purchase , (Homer), attic; with dative pretii, πρ. κτεάτεσσιν ἑοῖσιν to buy with one's money, (Odyssey by Homer); with genitive, πρ. θανάτοιο to purchase by his death, (Pindar); πρ. τι ταλάντου (Xenophon Historicus); π. πολλοῦ (Xenophon Historicus); metaphorically, οὐδενὸς λόγου πρίασθαι to buy at no price, (Sophocles Tragicus); πρ. τι παρά τινος (Herdotus Historicus):—; πρ. τίμιον τοὔλαιον to buy it dear, (Aristophanes Comicus) 2. to farm a tax, (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G8886.strongs_def: 1. a choosing one thing before another, an act of deliberate choice, a purpose, resolution , (Plato Philosophus), etc.:—; κατὰ προαίρεσιν on purpose, as one will , (Aristotle Philosopher) 2. a purpose, plan , or scope of action, a course of life, principle of action, (Demosthenes Orator) 3. in political language, a deliberate course of action, a policy , (Demosthenes Orator):—;also, a mode of government, such as an oligarchy, (Demosthenes Orator); in plural, τὰς κοινὰς πρ. your public principles, your general policy , (Demosthenes Orator) 4. a department of government , (Demosthenes Orator) 5. a political party , (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

G8890.strongs_def: the space immediately in front of or round a town, a suburb , (Herdotus Historicus), etc. (ML)

G8891.strongs_def: property in cattle πρόβατα); cattle , (Odyssey by Homer) (ML)

G8892.strongs_def: 1. anything projecting, a headland, promontory , (Sophocles Tragicus) 2. anything put before one, a fence, barrier, screen , (Herdotus Historicus), attic; πρ. σώματος, of a shield, (Aeschulus Tragicus); προβλήματα ἵππων χαλκᾶ the brasen armour of horses, (Xenophon Historicus) 3. with genitive a defence against a thing, πέτρων (Aeschulus Tragicus); χείματος (Euripides); κακῶν (Aristophanes Comicus) 4. πρ. φόβου ἢ αἰδοῦς ἔχειν to have fear or shame as a defence , (Sophocles Tragicus) 5. anything put forward as an excuse or screen , (Demosthenes Orator); so, πρ. λαβεῖν τινά (as we say) to make a stalking horse of him, (Sophocles Tragicus) 6. that which is proposed, a task, business , (Euripides) 7. a problem in Geometry, (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G8894.strongs_def: 1. to be ready, willing, eager, zealous to do a thing, with infinitive, (Herdotus Historicus), attic; also πρ. ὅπως (Herdotus Historicus), attic 2. absolute to shew zeal, exert oneself , (Herdotus Historicus):—; to be of good cheer , (Xenophon Historicus) 3. with accusative rei, to be eager or zealous for, promote eagerly, desire ardently , (Thucydides), etc. (ML)

G8895.strongs_def: 1. the front-door, the door leading from the αὐλή, (Homer); also in plural, (Homer) 2. the space before a door , a kind of porch or verandah , Lat. vestibulum, (Odyssey by Homer), attic 3. metaphorically, Κόρινθος πρόθυρον Ποτειδᾶνος (Pindar); πρόθυρα ἀρετῆς (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G8896.strongs_def: 1. to send before, send on or forward , (Homer): also, to send something to another, ἀγγελίας, φήμην (Odyssey by Homer):—; (Homer) often with an infinitive added; αἰετὼ προέηκα πέτεσθαι, οὖρον προέηκεν ἀῆναι (Odyssey by Homer) 2. to send away, dismiss, let go , (Iliad by Homer); τήνδε θεῷ πρόες let her go to the god, i. e. in reverence to him, (Iliad by Homer) 3. to let loose, let fall , especially thoughtlessly, ἔπος προέηκε let drop a word, (Odyssey by Homer); πηδάλιον ἐκ χειρῶν προέηκε he let the helm slip from his hands, (Odyssey by Homer); δάκρυα προῆκεν (Euripides) 4. of missiles, to send forth, shoot or dart forth , (Homer) 5. of a river, ὕδωρ προί̈ει ἐς Πηνειόν it pours its water into the Peneius, (Iliad by Homer) 6. πρ. τινί ποιεῖν τι to allow one to do, (Pindar) 7. to give up, deliver over, betray one to his enemy, (Herdotus Historicus): —;Pass. to be given or thrown away , εἰ προεῖτο ταῦτα (Demosthenes Orator) 8. ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτίκα ἡδὺ πρ. αὑτόν to give up or devote oneself to present delights, (Xenophon Historicus) 9. Mid. to send forward from oneself, drive forward , (Xenophon Historicus):—;of sounds, to utter , (Aeschines Orator), etc. 10. to give up, let go: to give up to the enemy, (Thucydides), etc.; πρ. σφᾶς αὑτούς gave themselves up as lost , (Thucydides) 11. to desert, abandon , (Thucydides); οὐδαμῆ προί̈εντο ἑαυτούς did not lose themselves (i. e. take bribes), (Demosthenes Orator) 12. to give away, give freely , (Thucydides), etc.; προέσθαι ἀπὸ τῶν ἰδίων (Demosthenes Orator) 13. to throw off one's clothes, (Demosthenes Orator): and, in bad sense, to throw away , τὸν καιρόν (Demosthenes Orator); τὰ πατρῷα (Aeschines Orator): absolute to be lavish , (Aristotle Philosopher) 14. a second predicate is sometimes added, ἡμᾶς προέσθαι ἀδικουμένους to suffer us to be wronged, (Thucydides); προέμενοι αὐτοὺς ἀπολέσθαι (Xenophon Historicus); πρ. τινὶ ὑμᾶς ἐξαπατῆσαι (Demosthenes Orator) 15. to suffer to escape , (Polybius Historicus) 16. rarely in good sense, to give over to one, confide to one's care , (Xenophon Historicus) 17. to neglect, disregard , (Aristotle Philosopher):—; absolute to neglect all advice, to be reckless , (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

G8897.strongs_def: 1. to set before; so in Mid., (Xenophon Historicus) 2. Pass., with aorist2 and perfect active, φυλακῆς μὴ προκαθεστηκυίας no guard having been set beforehand , (Thucydides) (ML)

G8898.strongs_def: 1. to seize beforehand, preoccupy , (Thucydides), etc.:—;Pass. to be preoccupied , (Thucydides) 2. metaphorically to anticipate, frustrate , (Thucydides):—;of persons, to anticipate or surprise them, (Thucydides) 3. to overpower before , (Thucydides) (ML)

G8902.strongs_def: to go out for foraging , (Polybius Historicus) (ML)

G8903.strongs_def: 1. a foraging, a foraging expedition, foray , (Xenophon Historicus): in plural, foraging parties , (Xenophon Historicus) 2. an elephant's trunk , (Polybius Historicus) 3. = προ-νομία, (Lucian) (ML)

G8904.strongs_def: 1. an opening or introduction to a thing; in Music, a prelude, overture , (Pindar); in poems and speeches, a proem, preface, preamble, introduction , Lat. exordium, (Pindar) 2. metaphorically of any prelude or beginning , φροίμιον χορεύσομαι (Aeschulus Tragicus); μηδέπω ' ν προοιμίοις only just beginning , (Aeschulus Tragicus); εἴ τι τοῦδε φρ. ματᾷ if any part of this presage be vain, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 3. generally, a hymn , (Thucydides) (ML)

G8906.strongs_def: reckless haste, vehemence, rashness, indiscretion , (Demosthenes Orator), etc. from προπετής (ML)

G8907.strongs_def: 1. to fall or throw oneself forward , as in rowing, προπεσόντες ἔρεσσον, like Lat. incumbere remis, (Odyssey by Homer):—;of suppliants, to fall prostrate , (Euripides) 2. to rush forward, rush headlong , (Sophocles Tragicus) 3. to move forwards, advance before the rest, (Polybius Historicus): to project , (Polybius Historicus) 4. προπίτνω poetry for προπίπτω 5. to fall prostate , ἐς γᾶν (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

G8908.strongs_def: in plural, like προπύλαια, (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; in singular, [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

G8909.strongs_def: a going up, ascent , κλίμακος προσαμβάσεις ascent by means of ladders, i. e. scaling ladders, (Aeschulus Tragicus); πρ. (Euripides); τειχέων πρ. a place where they may be approached , (Euripides); δωμάτων πρ. i. e. the steps leading to the house, (Euripides) (ML)

G8911.strongs_def: 1. to strike or dash against , τί τινι (Iliad by Homer); ἀψῖδα πέτρῳ πρ. letting it dash against , (Euripides); τὸν πρὶν ὄλβον ἕρματι πρ. to wreck his happiness on a rock, (Aeschulus Tragicus); πρ. θηρία τινί to set them on him, (Demosthenes Orator); πρ. δόρυ τινί (Euripides):—;without any notion of violence, to put to, apply , μαλακὰν χέρα πρ. [ ἕλκει] of a surgeon, (Pindar); πρ. παρειὰν παρηίδι (Euripides); ὄμματα τέκνοις (Euripides) 2. to assign to, procure for , κέρδος τινί (Herdotus Historicus); πρ. (Euripides) (ML)

G9043.strongs_def: to keep the Sabbath , (Septuagint Greek Bible) (ML)

G9050.strongs_def: 1. rotten, decayed, unsound, cracked , (Plato Philosophus)—;adverb, σαθρῶς ἱδρυμένος built on unsound foundations, (Aristotle Philosopher) 2. metaphorically, πρίν τι καὶ σαθρὸν ἐγγίνεσθαί σφι before any unsound thought comes into their heads, i. e. before they prove traitors, (Herdotus Historicus); ς. λόγοι (Euripides) derivation uncertain (ML)

G9059.strongs_def: a satrap, viceroy , Lat. satrapa, (Xenophon Historicus) Persian word. (ML)

G9063.strongs_def: 1. a Siren : in plural Σειρῆνες, αἱ, the Sirens , mythical sisters on the south coast of Italy, who enticed seamen by their songs, and then slew them, (Odyssey by Homer) (Homer) only knows of two , whence epic dual. genitive Σειρήνοιιν. 2. metaphorically a Siren, deceitful woman , (Euripides): the Siren charm of eloquence, (Aeschines Orator) derivation uncertain (ML)

G9065.strongs_def: a plank : metaphorically a leaf of papyrus: —; generally, the page of a book , [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

G9069.strongs_def: a standard , (Polybius Historicus):—; a band under one standard , the Roman manipulus , (Polybius Historicus) (ML)

G9073.strongs_def: 1. strength, might , (Iliad by Homer):—;with infinitive, σθ. πολεμίζειν strength to war, (Iliad by Homer); σθ. ὥστε καθελεῖν (Euripides); σθένει by force , (Sophocles Tragicus); λόγῳ τε καὶ σθένει both by right and might , (Sophocles Tragicus); so, ὑπὸ σθένους (Euripides); παντὶ σθένει with all one's might , (Thucydides) 2. strength, might , of all kinds moral as well as physical, σθένος τῆς ἀληθείας (Sophocles Tragicus); ἀγγέλων σθ. their might or authority , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 3. a force of men, like δύναμις, (Iliad by Homer) 4. metaphorically, like Lat. vis for copia, a quantity, profusion , (Pindar) 5. periphrastic, like βίη, ἴς, μένος, as σθένος Ἰδομενῆος, Ὠρίωνος, for Idomeneus, Orion, themselves, (Iliad by Homer) (ML)

G9075.strongs_def: 1. silently , σῖγα ἔχειν to be silent , (Sophocles Tragicus); κάθησο σῖγα (Aristophanes Comicus); alone, σῖγα hush! be still! (Aeschulus Tragicus):—;the public crier proclaiming silence said σῖγα πᾶς (i.e. ἔστω); (Aristophanes Comicus) 2. under one's breath, in a whisper, secretly , (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

G9076.strongs_def: an implement or tool of iron , σιδηρίων ἐπαί̈ειν to feel iron , not to be proof against it, (Herdotus Historicus); θερμὰ σιδήρια hot irons , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G9086.strongs_def: want of corn or food , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G9089.strongs_def: 1. ς. ἀνάγκη the task of grinding and baking , (Euripides) 2. as Substantive one that ground the corn in the handmill , (Thucydides); mostly feminine a baking-woman , (Herdotus Historicus); γυναῖκες ς. (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G9090.strongs_def: 1. silence , (Sophocles Tragicus), etc.; σιωπὴν ποιεῖν (Xenophon Historicus); ἦν ς. there was a hush or calm , (Sophocles Tragicus) 2. the habit of silence , (Demosthenes Orator) 3. dative σιωπῇ as adverb, in silence , (Homer), attic derivation uncertain (ML)

G9096.strongs_def: a carpenter's axe or adze , used for smoothing the trunks of trees, different from the πέλεκυς, (Odyssey by Homer) derivation uncertain (ML)

G9098.strongs_def: a covering, shelter, protection , (Xenophon Historicus):—;with genitive, ἐν σκέπῃ τοῦ πολέμου under shelter from war, (Herdotus Historicus); ὑπὸ τὴν Ῥωμαίων σκέπην under their protection , (Polybius Historicus) (ML)

G9100.strongs_def: 1. to look about, look carefully , followed by preposition εἰς, (Odyssey by Homer):—;with accusative to look after, watch , (Iliad by Homer), attic:—;absolute to look out, reconnoitre , (Herdotus Historicus); σκέψαι look , (Aeschulus Tragicus); σκέψασθε look out , (Aristophanes Comicus) 2. of the mind, to look to, view, examine, consider, think on , (Sophocles Tragicus), etc.:—; σκέψασθε δέ: only consider , (Thucydides) 3. to think of beforehand, premeditate , (Demosthenes Orator) 4. perfect also in passive sense, ἐσκεμμένα things well-considered , (Thucydides); σκοπεῖτε οὖν. Answ. ἔσκεπται (Plato Philosophus); so 3 future passive ἐσκέψεται (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G9104.strongs_def: 1. a staff or stick to lean upon, a walking-stick , (Homer): metaphorically of the daughters of Oedipus, σκῆπτρα φωτός his staffs or supports , (Sophocles Tragicus) 2. a staff , as the badge of command, a sceptre : in (Homer) borne by chiefs, and transmitted from father to son, whence the passage in (Iliad by Homer) 2 is called ἡ τοῦ σκήπτρου παράδοσις, (Thucydides):—;also borne by judges, by heralds, by speakers, who on rising to speak received it from the herald, (Homer) 3. the sceptre , i. e. royalty, kingly power, rule , [8th/7th c.BC, variant datesTragica Adespota (ML)

G9106.strongs_def: 1. to overshadow, shade , (Iliad by Homer) 2. generally, to overshadow, cover , (Hesiod):—;Pass., (Euripides) 3. to shade in painting , (Lucian) (ML)

G9112.strongs_def: crookedness , (Plutarch): in plural the windings of a stream, etc., (Strabo Geographus) (ML)

G9115.strongs_def: 1. a lookout-place, a mountain-peak , (Homer): of the Trojan acropolis, (Euripides): compare σκόπελος. 2. metaphorically the height or highest point of anything, (Pindar) 3. a watchtower , Lat. specula, (Herdotus Historicus) 4. a look-out, watch , σκοπιὴν ἔχειν to keep watch , (Odyssey by Homer) (ML)

G9119.strongs_def: to look angry or sullen, be of a sad countenance , (Aristophanes Comicus), etc. from σκυθρωπός (ML)

G9120.strongs_def: 1. to strip or despoil a slain enemy of his arms, (Hesiod); with accusative of persons or things, Κύκνον σκυλεύσαντες ἀπp ὤμων τεύχεα having stript the arms of Cycnus from his shoulders, (Hesiod) 2. with accusative rei et genitive pers. to strip the arms off an enemy, (Xenophon Historicus); so, ἀπὸ τῶν νεκρῶν σκ. ψέλια (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G9121.strongs_def: a cub, whelp , especially a lion's whelp , (Iliad by Homer), attic; of other animals, (Euripides); in poets also of men, Ἀχίλλειος σκ. (Euripides) (ML)

G9122.strongs_def: 1. a staff, cudgel, club , [variant datesAnthology Palantina 2. at Sparta, a staff or baton , used as a cypher for writing dispatches:—;a strip of leather was rolled slantwise round it, on which the dispatches were written lengthwise, so that when unrolled they were unintelligible: commanders abroad had a staff of like thickness, round which they rolled these papers, and so were able to read the dispatches:—;hence σκυτάλη came to mean a Spartan dispatch , (Thucydides); and generally a message , (Pindar) derivation uncertain (ML)

G9127.strongs_def: 1. Lat. taxus, the yew, (Plato Philosophus) 2. the convolvulus , or perhaps bryony , [variant datesTragica Adespota, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G9130.strongs_def: 1. a master of one's craft or art, an adept , of a diviner, (Herdotus Historicus); of poets, (Pindar); of the Creator, (Plato Philosophus); metaphorically, ς. πημάτων an adept in misery, (Euripides) 2. like φρόνιμος, one who is clever in matters of life, a wise man , in which sense the seven Sages are called σοφισταί, (Herdotus Historicus); of Prometheus, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 3. at Athens, a Sophist , i. e. a professor of grammar, rhetoric, politics, mathematics, such as Prodicus, Gorgias, Protagoras, (Thucydides), etc. At first the Sophists were held in honour; but from their loose principles they fell into ill repute, and the word came to mean, 4. a sophist (in bad sense), a quibbler, cheat , (Aristophanes Comicus), etc. (ML)

G9134.strongs_def: 1. of things, to be rare, scarce, scanty , (Pindar) 2. of persons, to lack or be in want of , τινός (Herdotus Historicus), etc.;—;so in Pass., ἐσπανίσμεθ᾽ ἀρωγῶν (Aeschulus Tragicus): absolute to be in want , (Euripides) (ML)

G9135.strongs_def: 1. rare, scarce, scanty , (Herdotus Historicus); σπάνιον ἑαυτὸν παρέχειν, Lat. difficiles aditus habere, (Plato Philosophus); ὕδατι σπανίῳ χρώμενοι having a scanty supply of water, (Thucydides); with infinitive, σπ. ἰδεῖν rare to behold, (Xenophon Historicus): of persons in an adverb sense, σπάνιος ἐπιφοιτᾷ he seldom visits, (Herdotus Historicus):—; σπάνιόν ἐστι, with infinitive, it is seldom that . ., (Xenophon Historicus):—; τὸ σπάνιον = σπάνις, (Aeschines Orator) 2. comparative σπανιώτερος, (Herdotus Historicus): —;Sup. -ώτατος, attic 3. adverb -ίως, seldom , (Xenophon Historicus); so σπανίᾳ, (Plato Philosophus): comparative -ιώτερον, (Thucydides) (ML)

G9136.strongs_def: a swathing band , and in plural swaddling-clothes , (Homeric Hymns); παῖς ἔτ᾽ ὢν ἐν σπαργάνοις (Aeschulus Tragicus); tokens by which a person is identified , Lat. monumenta, crepundia, (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G9140.strongs_def: the space one can span with the thumb and little finger, a span , Lat. dodrans, about 7 1/2 inches , (Herdotus Historicus) derivation uncertain (ML)

G9141.strongs_def: a spark , Lat. scintilla, (Iliad by Homer) (ML)

(Thucydides); σπονδὰς παραδιδόναι (Aristophanes Comicus); δέχεσθαι (Thucydides); τυχεῖν (Xenophon Historicus); σπ. ποιεῖσθαί τινι to make a truce with one, (Herdotus Historicus); πρός τινα (Aristophanes Comicus); σπ. τέμνειν (like ὅρκια τέμνειν); (Euripides); σπ. ἄγειν πρός τινας (Thucydides) 3. αἱ Ὀλυμπικαὶ σπ. the solemn truce or armistice during the Olympic games, (Thucydides) 4. the treaty itself , εἴρηται ἐν ταῖς σπ. (Thucydides) (ML)

G9147.strongs_def: 1. of persons, 2. with accusative rei, to drop, let fall or shed drop by drop , (Iliad by Homer), etc. 3. with dative rei, αἵματι στ. to drip with blood, (Aeschulus Tragicus); στάζων ἱδρῶτι (Sophocles Tragicus);—;rarely with genitive, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 4. intransitive of things, to drop, fall in drops, drip, trickle , (Herdotus Historicus); metaphorically, στάζει ἐν ὕπνωι πόνος (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

G9150.strongs_def: 1. a standing place for animals, Lat. stabulum, a stable, fold, (Iliad by Homer): a stye , (Odyssey by Homer): of men, a dwelling, abode , (Hesiod) 2. quarters, lodgings for travellers or soldiers, Lat. statio, (Xenophon Historicus) 3. in Persia, σταθμοί were stations on the royal road, where the king rested, (Herdotus Historicus): hence a day's journey, day's march , averaging about 5 parasangs or 15 miles, (Herdotus Historicus) 4. like Lat. statio, a station for ships, (Euripides) 5. an upright post, the bearing pillar of the roof, (Odyssey by Homer): a door-post , especially in plural, (Homer), attic 6. the balance , (Aristophanes Comicus); ἱστᾶν σταθμῷ τι πρός τι to weigh one thing against another, (Herdotus Historicus) 7. weight , σταθμὸν ἔχειν τάλαντον to weigh a talent, (Herdotus Historicus); absolute in accusative, ἴσα σταθμόν equal in weight , (Herdotus Historicus); ἡμιπλίνθια σταθμὸν διτάλαντα two talents in or by weight , (Herdotus Historicus):—;in plural weights , (Euripides), etc. (ML)

G9151.strongs_def: flour of spelt mixed and made into dough , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G9155.strongs_def: stiff fat, tallow, suet , Lat. sebum, opp. toπιμελή (Lat. adeps, soft fat), (Odyssey by Homer) (ML)

G9158.strongs_def: 1. waterproof , (Herdotus Historicus); στεγνὰ οἰκήματα, of a cave, (Euripides) 2. as Substantive, στεγνόν, οῦ, a covered dwelling , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

(Sophocles Tragicus):—;Mid., (Aeschulus Tragicus) 3. with accusative to bewail, lament , (Aeschulus Tragicus), etc.; στένειν τινὰ τῆς τύχης to pity him for his ill fortune, (Aeschulus Tragicus): so in Mid., στένεσθαί τινα (Euripides) (ML)

G9166.strongs_def: 1. to deprive, bereave, rob of anything, with accusative pers. et genitive rei, (Odyssey by Homer), attic 2. with accusative rei, to take away , [variant datesAnthology Palantina:—;Pass. to have taken from one , βίον στερείς (Euripides) (ML)

G9167.strongs_def: to deprive of a thing, (Thucydides):—;Pass. to be deprived of a thing, (Herdotus Historicus), attic (ML)

G9168.strongs_def: 1. anything that encircles the head, for defence or ornament: 2. the brim of the helmet, projecting behind as well as before, (Iliad by Homer) 3. part of a woman's head-dress, a diadem, coronal , (Iliad by Homer), etc.:—;metaphorically, of a city, ἀπὸ στεφάναν κέκαρσαι πύργων thou hast been shorn of thy coronal of towers, (Euripides) 4. the brim or edge of anything, the brow of a hill, edge of a cliff , (Iliad by Homer); of a basket, (Moschus Bucolicus) (ML)

G9171.strongs_def: 1. a block of stone used as a prop or buttress to a wall , (Iliad by Homer): a block of rockcrystal, in which the Egyptian mummies were cased, (Herdotus Historicus) 2. a block or slab , bearing an inscription; and so, 3. a gravestone , (Homer), attic 4. a block or slab , inscribed with record of victories, dedications, treaties, decrees, etc., (Herdotus Historicus), attic; γράφειν τινὰ εἰς στήλην, ἀναγράφειν ἐν στήλῃ, whether for honour, or for infamy, (Herdotus Historicus):—;also the record itself, a contract, agreement , κατὰ τὴν στήλην according to agreement , (Aristophanes Comicus); στῆλαι αἱ πρὸς Θηβαίους (Demosthenes Orator) 5. a boundary post, (Xenophon Historicus):—; the turning-post at the end of the racecourse, Lat. meta, (Sophocles Tragicus) 6. for Στῆλαι Ἡρακλήιαι, see. Ἡράκλειος. (ML)

G9173.strongs_def: to set up as a monument , [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

G9175.strongs_def: 1. the warp in the ancient upright loom, (Hesiod) 2. a thread , (Batrachomyomachia) (ML)

G9180.strongs_def: Mid. or Pass. to paint one's eyelids and eyebrows with black paint στίβι); (Strabo Geographus) (ML)

G9181.strongs_def: punctured , [variant datesAnthology Palantina:—;generally, spotted, dappled , (Sophocles Tragicus); στικτὰ ὄμματα, of the hundred eyes of Argus, (Euripides) (ML)

G9184.strongs_def: 1. a row or file of soldiers, (Xenophon Historicus) 2. a line of poetry, a verse , (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G9186.strongs_def: a plant used for stuffing or padding; and metaphorically " padding , " an expletive , (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G9187.strongs_def: 1. to set a row of poles with nets to drive the game into, (Xenophon Historicus) 2. to order or arrange in system , (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

G9188.strongs_def: 1. to put in trim , στολίσας νηὸς πτερά having trimmed the sails, (Hesiod) 2. to equip, dress :—;Pass., ἐστολισμένος δορί armed with spear, (Euripides) 3. metaphorically to deck, adorn , [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

G9191.strongs_def: 1. to aim or shoot at , with genitive, τοῦ σκοποῦ (Plato Philosophus), etc. 2. metaphorically to aim at, endeavour after , (Plato Philosophus); στ. φίλων κριτῶν to aim at having friends as judges, (Xenophon Historicus) 3. to endeavour to make out, to guess at a thing, with genitive, (Isocrates Orator):—; absolute to make guesses, conjecture, (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G9198.strongs_def: 1. to encamp, bivouac, take up a position , (Xenophon Historicus): 2. as Dep. στρατοπεδεύομαι, (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; perfect ἐστρατοπεδεῦσθαι to be in camp , (Xenophon Historicus): of a fleet, to be stationed , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G9199.strongs_def: twisted, crooked , (Aristotle Philosopher); of the brows, knit, wrinkled , [variant datesAnthology Palantina: metaphorically, στρεβλοῖσι παλαίσμασι by cunning dodges in wrestling, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G9202.strongs_def: to twist, twirl or whirl about , (Aristophanes Comicus):—;metaphorically to make dizzy, distract , (Aeschulus Tragicus): —;Pass. to whirl about , (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

G9203.strongs_def: 1. round, spherical , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; λίθοι στρ. pebbles , (Xenophon Historicus) 2. circular , (Plato Philosophus) 3. round, compactly formed , (Xenophon Historicus) 4. of ships, στρ. ναῦς, στρ. πλοῖον, a merchant- ship, from its round shape , as opposite to the long narrow ship-of-war μακρὰ ναῦς); (Herdotus Historicus), etc. 5. metaphorically of phrases, well-rounded, compact, pithy, terse , (Aristophanes Comicus):—;adverb, στρογγυλώτατα as tersely as possible , (Aristotle Philosopher) (ML)

G9207.strongs_def: 1. the sparrow , (Iliad by Homer), etc. 2. ὁ μέγας στρ. the large bird , i. e. the ostrich, Struthio , (Xenophon Historicus): also called στρουθὸς κατάγαιος (i. e. the bird that runs on the ground , does not fly), (Herdotus Historicus); also simply στρουθός, like στρουθοκάμηλος, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G9208.strongs_def: the socket in which the pivot of a door ὁ στρόφιγξ); moved, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G9209.strongs_def: 1. a turning , e.g. of a horse, (Xenophon Historicus); ἐν στροφαῖσιν ὀμμάτων with rolling of the eyes, (Euripides) 2. a twist , such as wrestlers make to elude their adversary, (Plato Philosophus):—;metaphorically a trick, dodge , (Aristophanes Comicus) 3. the turning of the Chorus as they danced from right to left of the ὀρχήστρα: the strain sung during this evolution, the strophe , to which the ἀντιστροφή answers. (ML)

G9210.strongs_def: 1. the pivot, axle or pin on which a body turns , (Euripides) 2. στρόφιγγες were pivots working in sockets , at top and bottom of a door, which served instead of hinges, (Plutarch) 3. metaphorically, στρ. γλώττης, of a well-hung tongue, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G9212.strongs_def: 1. anything spread or laid out for lying or sitting upon, a mattress, bed , Lat. stragulum, vestis stragula, (Theognis Elegiacus):—;in plural the bedclothes, the coverings of a dinner-couch , (Aristophanes Comicus), etc. 2. a horsecloth, horse-trappings , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G9348.strongs_def: 1. a pipe : 2. a musical pipe, a shepherd's pipe, Panspipe , (Iliad by Homer), attic 3. anything like a pipe : 4. a spear-case , = δορατοθήκη, (Iliad by Homer) 5. the hole in the nave of a wheel , [variant datesTragica Adespota 6. a duct or channel in the body, in plural the nostrils , (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G9366.strongs_def: 1. Lat. fall-o (the sigma being lost):—; to make to fall, throw down, overthrow , properly by tripping up, to trip up in wrestling , (Homer), etc.; σφ. ναῦς to throw her on her beam-ends , (Plutarch); ἵππος σφ. τὸν ἀναβάτην throws him, (Xenophon Historicus):—;Pass. to be tripped up , (Aristophanes Comicus); of a drunken man, σφαλλόμενος reeling, staggering , (Aristophanes Comicus) 2. generally, to cause to fall, overthrow, defeat , (Herdotus Historicus):—;Pass. to be overthrown, to fall, fail, be undone, become helpless , (Herdotus Historicus), attic; τόδ᾽ ἐσφάλη this mishap took place , (Sophocles Tragicus); οὔ τι μὴ σφαλῶ γ᾽ ἐν σοί I shall not fail in thy business, (Sophocles Tragicus) 3. to baffle, foil, balk, disappoint , (Herdotus Historicus):—;Pass. to err, go wrong, be mistaken , (Herdotus Historicus) 4. the Pass. is also used with genitive rei, to be balked of or foiled in a thing, ἦ καὶ πατήρ τι σφάλλεται βουλευμάτω; (Aeschulus Tragicus); σφάλλεσθαι γάμου (Euripides); τῆς δόξης (Thucydides) (ML)

G9368.strongs_def: 1. to sling, to use the sling , (Thucydides) 2. to strike by slinging , (Babrius Fabularum Scriptor) 3. to throw as from a sling :—;Pass., (Euripides) 4. to move like a swing, to swing to and fro , (Euripides) from σφενδόνη (ML)

G9369.strongs_def: 1. Lat. funda (the ς being lost), a sling , (Iliad by Homer): metaphorically, σφενδόνας ἀπ᾽ εὐμέτρου with well-measured throw, as from a sling , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 2. the hoop of a ring in which the stone was set as in a sling, especially the broader part round the stone , as in Lat. funda for pala annuli , (Euripides) 3. the stone or bullet of the sling , (Xenophon Historicus); τοιαύταις σφ., of hailstones, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G9373.strongs_def: to bind tight, bind fast , (Aeschulus Tragicus):—;Pass., (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) (ML)

G9374.strongs_def: 1. vehement, violent, excessive , (Thucydides), etc. 2. of men, violent, impetuous , (Plato Philosophus): also strong, robust , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G9376.strongs_def: 1. a hammer , (Odyssey by Homer) 2. a beetle, mallet , for breaking clods of earth, (Hesiod) (ML)

G9379.strongs_def: 1. properly to let loose : hence to slit, open , (Aristophanes Comicus); σχ. φλέβα to open a vein, (Xenophon Historicus), etc.:—;of flowers, σχ. κάλυκας [variant datesAnthology Palantina 2. to let fall, drop , (Xenophon Historicus) 3. to let go , σχάσας τὴν φροντίδα having let the mind go, given it play , (Aristophanes Comicus); σχ. τὰς μηχανάς to let off the engines, (Plutarch) 4. to check, stop, stay , Lat. inhibere, κώπαν σχάσον, i. e. cease rowing, (Pindar); σχάσον ὄμμα lower thine eyes, (Euripides):—;Mid., σχασάμενος τὴν ἱππικήν having dropt one's horsemanship, "given up the turf," (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G9380.strongs_def: 1. a raft, float (such as was made off-hand , compare σχέδιος II), (Odyssey by Homer); generally, a boat, ship , (Euripides) 2. a bridge of boats , of the bridge of Xerxes, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G9382.strongs_def: 1. a piece of wood cleft off, a lath, splinter , Lat. scindula, (Odyssey by Homer): in plural cleft wood, fire-wood , (Homer) 2. an arrow , [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

G9389.strongs_def: 1. to make into a body, to consolidate, organise , (Polybius Historicus) 2. to provide with bodily strength, to recruit , (Polybius Historicus) (ML)

G9394.strongs_def: 1. a band, riband, fillet , especially a head-band , worn in sign of victory, (Xenophon Historicus), etc. 2. a strip or tongue of land , (Plutarch), etc. (ML)

G9395.strongs_def: fit for ordering or arranging , especially in war, τ. ἀνήρ a tactician , (Xenophon Historicus); τακτικὸν ἡγεῖσθαί τι to think it a good piece of tactics , (Xenophon Historicus); οἱ τ. ἀριθμοί the regular battalions, (Xenophon Historicus): τὰ τακτικά the art of drawing up soldiers in array, tactics , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G9397.strongs_def: suffering, wretched , Lat. miser, (Odyssey by Homer); ὦ τάλαιν᾽ ἐγώ (Aeschulus Tragicus); ὦ τάλαν (Sophocles Tragicus);—;with genitive causae, τάλαιν᾽ ἐγὼ τῆς ὕβρεως wretched that I am for this insolence, (Aristophanes Comicus):—;in bad sense, τάλαν wretch! (Odyssey by Homer)—;comparative τᾶλάντερος, η, ον: Sup. τᾶλάντατος, η, ον, (Aristophanes Comicus) τᾶλα_; doric also τᾶλᾶς: vocative τάλᾶν. (ML)

G9398.strongs_def: 1. one who carves and distributes, a dispenser , (Iliad by Homer):—;of Zeus, as the dispenser of all things to men, (Iliad by Homer); so Aeolus is τ. ἀνέμων (Odyssey by Homer):—;of kings or rulers, a controller, director , (Pindar); τ. κώμων master of the revels, (Pindar); τ. Διός the priest of Zeus, (Pindar): τ. Μοισᾶν, i. e. a poet, (Pindar); οἶκος τ. στεφάνων that hath store of crowns, (Pindar); τῆς τε ἐπιθυμίας καὶ τῆς τύχης τ. controller both of his desire and of fortune, (Thucydides); τ. τριαίνης, of Poseidon, (Aristophanes Comicus) 2. in Prose, a controller of payments, treasurer , (Herdotus Historicus); τ. τοῦ ἱροῦ the controller of the sacred treasure in the citadel of Athens, (Herdotus Historicus) 3. at Rome, the quaestor , (Plutarch) (ML)

G9399.strongs_def: 1. to be controller of receipts and expenditure, to be treasurer, paymaster , (Aristophanes Comicus):—;with genitive, τ. τῆς Παράλου to be paymaster of the Paralus, (Demosthenes Orator) 2. at Rome, to be quaestor , (Plutarch) 3. transitive to deal out, dispense , (Plato Philosophus), etc.:—;Pass., τοὺς νόμους τεταμιεύμεθα we have the laws dealt out , (Lysias Orator):—;Mid., ταμιεύεσθαι εἰς ὅσον βουλόμεθα ἄρχειν to control the limits to which we mean to extend our sway, (Thucydides) 4. of keeping house, to regulate, manage , (Aristophanes Comicus):—; Pass., χώρα ταμιευομένα τινί governed or possessed by one, (Pindar) 5. to store up , (Demosthenes Orator); Ζηνὸς ταμιεύεσκε γονάς she was the depository of it, (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G9400.strongs_def: 1. to stretch, strain, stretch out , (Iliad by Homer); τ. βιόν to string a bow, (Odyssey by Homer); and in Mid., τόξον τανυσσάμενος having strung his bow, (Iliad by Homer):—;of putting the strings to a harp, ἐτάνυσσε χορδήν (Odyssey by Homer); τ. κανόνα to push the weaving-bar tight , i. e. to weave, (Iliad by Homer); ὅπως τανύσηι when he reins in [the horses, 8th/7th c.BC]; ἐπὶ Ἀκράγαντι τανύσσας (i.e. ὀϊστούς) having aimed them, (Pindar):—;Pass., γναθμοὶ τάνυσθεν (for ἐτανύσθησαν) the hollow cheeks filled out , (Odyssey by Homer); to run at full stretch , of horses galloping, (Homer) 2. metaphorically to strain, make more intense , μάχην (Iliad by Homer); ἔριδα πολέμοιο πεῖραρ τάνυσσαν strained the tug of war, (Iliad by Homer) 3. to stretch out, lay along, lay , (Homer); τ. τινὰ ἐν κονίηις, ἐπὶ γαίηι to lay one in the dust, stretch him at his length , (Homer):—;Pass. to lie stretched out , (Homer): to extend , (Odyssey by Homer); ἐπὶ χθονὶ κεῖτο τανυσθείς (Iliad by Homer):—;also, τρίβος τετάνυστο the path stretched away , (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) (ML)

G9403.strongs_def: 1. troublous, turbulent , (Herdotus Historicus); ἴχνη τ. uncertain, baffling , (Xenophon Historicus) 2. troubled, disordered , (Aristotle Philosopher) 3. of an army, (Thucydides) 4. adverb, ταραχωδῶς ζῆν to live in a state of confusion , (Isocrates Orator); τ. ἔχειν πρός τινα to be rebelliously disposed, (Demosthenes Orator); Sup. -έστατα (Isocrates Orator) (ML)

G9406.strongs_def: 1. to make quickly , (Sophocles Tragicus); τοῖα σπερχόμενος ταχύνει such are the words which in his eager haste he speaks, (Euripides) 2. intransitive to be quick, to make haste, speed, hurry , (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

G9407.strongs_def: 1. to stretch by main force, to stretch to the uttermost , τόξον ἔτεινεν stretched it to its full , (Iliad by Homer); ἐξ ἄντυγος ἡνία τείνας having tied the reins tight to the chariot-rail, (Iliad by Homer):—;Pass., [ ἱμὰς] τέτατο the strap was made tight , (Iliad by Homer); ἱστία τέτατο the sails were stretched , (Odyssey by Homer):—;absolute, μὴ τείνειν ἄγαν not to strain the cord too tight, (Sophocles Tragicus) 2. metaphorically, ἶσον τείνειν πολέμου τέλος to strain the even tug of war, (Iliad by Homer):—;Pass., ἐπὶ ἶσα μάχη τέτατο (Iliad by Homer); ἵπποισι τάθη δρόμος their pace was strained to the utmost , (Iliad by Homer): also, to exert oneself, be anxious , (Pindar) 3. to stretch out, spread , Ζεὺς λαίλαπα τείνει (Iliad by Homer); νὺξ τέταται βροτοῖσιν night is spread over mankind, (Odyssey by Homer); so, of light, τέτατο φάος (Sophocles Tragicus); of sound, ἀμφὶ νῶτ᾽ ἐτάθη πάταγος (Sophocles Tragicus) 4. to aim at, direct towards a point, properly from the bow, τείνειν βέλη (Sophocles Tragicus): then, metaphorically, τ. φόνον εἴς τινα to aim death to one, design it for him, (Euripides); τ. λόγον εἴς τινα (Plato Philosophus) 5. to stretch out in length , (Herdotus Historicus):—;Pass. to lie out at length, lie stretched , ταθεὶς ἐπὶ γαίηι (Iliad by Homer); ταθεὶς ἐνὶ δεσμῶι lying stretched in chains, (Odyssey by Homer) 6. to stretch or hold out, present , τινὰ ἐπὶ σφαγάν (Euripides):—;Mid., τείνεσθαι χέρε to stretch out one's hands, etc., (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) 7. to extend, lengthen , of Time, (Aeschulus Tragicus); τείνειν λόγον (Aeschulus Tragicus) 8. intransitive, of geographical position, to stretch out or extend , (Herdotus Historicus):—;of Time, τείνοντα χρόνον lengthening time, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 9. to exert oneself, struggle , ἐναντία τινί (Plato Philosophus): to hurry on, hasten , (Euripides) 10. to extend to, reach , Lat. pertinere, ἐπὶ τὴν ψυχήν (Plato Philosophus) 11. to tend, refer, belong to , Lat. spectare ad, τείνει ἐς σέ it refers to, concerns you, (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; ποῖ τείνε; to what tends it? (Plato Philosophus); ἐγγύς τι τείνειν τοῦ θανάτου (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G9408.strongs_def: enclosed by walls, beleaguered, besieged , (Herdotus Historicus), etc. (ML)

G9409.strongs_def: 1. to build a wall , (Aristophanes Comicus), etc.: with accusative cognate, τ. τεῖχος to build it, (Thucydides); so in Mid., τεῖχος ἐτειχίσσαντο they built them a wall, (Iliad by Homer):—;Pass. to be built , (Pindar): 3rd singular pluperfect τετείχιστο, impersonal, buildings had been erected, there were buildings , (Herdotus Historicus) 2. transitive to wall or fortify , τὸ οὖρος (Herdotus Historicus); τὴν πόλιν (Thucydides): in Mid., τειχίζεσθαι τὸ χωρίον (Thucydides):—;Pass. to be walled or fenced with walls , (Thucydides); τὰ τετειχισμένα the fortified parts , (Thucydides) (ML)

G9411.strongs_def: in Act., of the woman, to bear children , in Mid., of the man, to beget them , (Xenophon Historicus): in Mid. of both parents, to breed children , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

Cleon) (Aristophanes Comicus) 4. later, Act. τεκταίνω, in same sense, [variant datesAnthology Palantina, (Lucian); hence participle passive τεκταινόμενος, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G9413.strongs_def: practised or skilled in building , (Plato Philosophus): as Substantive a good carpenter or builder , opposite to a smith, (Xenophon Historicus): —; ἡ -κή (i.e. τέχνη); joiners' work, carpentry , (Plato Philosophus), etc. (ML)

G9414.strongs_def: 1. a broad strap for bearing anything from Root ! τλα, * τλάω, whence also the hero Telamon took his name, compare Ἄτλας 2. a leathern strap or belt , for bearing both shield or sword, (Homer) 3. a broad linen bandage for wounds, (Iliad by Homer); for swathing mummies, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G9416.strongs_def: 1. initiation in the mysteries, (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; ἐς χεῖρας ἄγεσθαι τὴν τελετήν to take in hand the matter of initiation , (Herdotus Historicus):—;in plural mystic rites at initiation , (Euripides), etc. 2. a festival accompanied by such rites , in plural, (Pindar); in singular, (Euripides) (ML)

G9417.strongs_def: 1. last , Lat. ultimus, (Herdotus Historicus); τὰ τ. the endings or terminations , (Herdotus Historicus); τελευταίους στῆσαι to station in the rear ranks , (Xenophon Historicus) 2. of Time, ἡ τελευταία, with or without ἡμέρα, the last day allowed for payment, (Demosthenes Orator); one's last day , (Sophocles Tragicus) 3. last, uttermost , ὕβρις (Sophocles Tragicus) 4. τὸ τελευταῖον, as adverb the last time, last of all , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; or τελευταῖον (Plato Philosophus), etc.; and τὰ τελευταῖα (Thucydides) 5. at last, in the last place , (Aristophanes Comicus), etc.: but, 6. the adjective is often used with Verbs, where we should use the adverb, ὁ τελευταῖος δραμών (Aeschulus Tragicus); παρελθόντες τελευταῖοι (Thucydides) (ML)

G9418.strongs_def: 1. a piece of land cut off, assigned as a domain to kings and chiefs, (Homer) 2. a piece of land dedicated to a god, the sacred precincts , (Homer): in it stood the temple, (Herdotus Historicus):—;metaphorically, the sacred valley of the Nile is the τέμ. Νείλοιο, (Pindar); the Acropolis is the ἱερὸν τ. of Pallas, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G9419.strongs_def: 1. to cut, hew , (Homer), etc.; ὀδόντας οἵους τέμνειν teeth fit for cutting , (Xenophon Historicus) 2. to cut, wound, maim , (Iliad by Homer); πρὸς δέρην τ. to wound her in the neck, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 3. of a surgeon, to cut , (Iliad by Homer): absolute to use the knife , as opposite to cautery ( κάειν), (Aeschulus Tragicus), etc.:—;Pass. to be operated upon , (Plato Philosophus) 4. to cut up, cut to pieces , (Homer), etc.:—; to slaughter, sacrifice , (Iliad by Homer) 5. ὅρκια τάμνειν to sacrifice in attestation of an oath, and so to take solemn oaths , (Homer); θάνατόν νύ τοι ὅρκι᾽ ἔταμνον I made a truce which was death to thee, (Iliad by Homer):—;Mid., of two parties, ὅρκια τάμνεσθαι (Herdotus Historicus):—;cf. Lat. foedus ferire. 6. φάρμακον τέμνειν to cut or chop up a plant for purposes of medicine or witchcraft, (Aeschulus Tragicus), etc.; ἄκος τέμνειν to contrive a means or remedy, (Euripides) 7. to divide , of a river, μέσην τ. Λιβύην to cut it in twain, (Herdotus Historicus); δίχα τ. to cut in two, bisect , (Plato Philosophus) 8. to cut asunder, cut off, sever , κεφαλὴν ἀπὸ δειρῆς (Iliad by Homer), etc.; with double accusative, ἐρινεὸν τάμνε ὄρπηκας cut the branches off the fig-tree, (Iliad by Homer); and in Pass., τρίχας ἐτμήθην had them cut off , (Euripides) 9. to part off, mark off , τέμενος (Iliad by Homer) 10. to cut down, fell trees, (Iliad by Homer), etc.:—;Mid., δοῦρα τάμνεσθαι to fell oneself timber, (Odyssey by Homer) 11. λίθον τ. to hew stone, (Plato Philosophus): Mid., λίθους τάμνεσθαι to have them wrought or hewn , (Herdotus Historicus) 12. to cut down for purposes of destruction, (Euripides), etc.; τ. τὴν γῆν to ravage the country by felling the trees and cutting the corn , (Herdotus Historicus); with partitive genitive, τῆς γῆς τ. to waste part of it, (Thucydides) 13. to cut or hew into shape , δούρατα (Odyssey by Homer), etc. 14. to cut lengthwise, to plough , Solon. 15. τ. ὁδόν to cut or make a road, (Thucydides):—;Pass., τέτμηνται κέλευθοι (Pindar) 16. also to make one's way, advance , τ. ὁδόν (Euripides); τὴν μεσόγαιαν τ. τῆς ὁδοῦ to take the middle road, strike through the interior, (Herdotus Historicus); μέσον τέμνειν to hold a middle course, (Plato Philosophus) 17. of ships, to cut through the waves, plough the sea , (Odyssey by Homer):—;so of birds, to cleave the air, (Aristophanes Comicus) 18. to bring to a decision , Lat. decidere, (Pindar) (ML)

G9422.strongs_def: a borer, gimlet , Lat. terebra, (Odyssey by Homer) (ML)
