G9554.strongs_def: 1. exceeding long , (Aeschulus Tragicus); ἡ βασιλέος χεὶρ ὑπ. the king's arm is very long, reaches very far , (Herdotus Historicus) 2. exceeding high , of mountains, (Herdotus Historicus) 3. ὑπερμάκης βοά a cry exceeding loud , (Pindar) (ML)

G9557.strongs_def: ὑπερ-οράω, see: ὑπερεῖδον. ὑπερ-εῖδον, aor. [in LXX for עָלַם hi., מַעַל, etc. ;] to overlook: with accusative of thing(s), Act.17:30 (AS)

G9559.strongs_def: 1. to set higher, erect , [variant datesAnthology Palantina 2. to set on the other side, carry over , (Plutarch) 3. in Mid. to hold over , so as to protect, [variant datesAnthology Palantina 4. metaphorically, παντὶ θεὸν ὑπερτιθέμεν to set God over all, (Pindar) 5. to communicate a thing to another, ὑπερετίθεα (ionic imperfect for -ετίθην); τὰ ἔμελλον ποιήσειν (Herdotus Historicus):—;so in Mid., especially in order to ask advice, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G9561.strongs_def: 1. to bear or carry over a place, ὑπ. τὸν ἰσθμὸν τὰς ναῦς (Thucydides):—;Pass., [ αἱ ναῦς] αἱ ὑπερενεχθεῖσαι τὸν ἰσθμόν (Thucydides) 2. intransitive to rise above, to surpass, excel, have the advantage over , τινός τινι one in a thing, (Herdotus Historicus); also with accusative pro genitive, ὑπερφέρεις τόλμῃ τόλμαν (Euripides): absolute to excel, have preeminence , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G9565.strongs_def: 1. liable to give account for one's administration of an office, accountable, responsible , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.:—; ὑπεύθυνοι, οἱ, at Athens, magistrates who had to submit their accounts to public auditors λογισταί); (Aristophanes Comicus), etc. 2. with genitive responsible for , ὑπ. ἀρχῆς ἑτέρας quoted in (Demosthenes Orator); of slaves, σῶμα ὑπ. ἀδικημάτων their body is liable for their misdeeds, i. e. they must pay for them with their body, (Demosthenes Orator) 3. with dative responsible to another, dependent on them, Lat. obnoxius, (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

G9566.strongs_def: 1. the body of rowers and sailors, the ship's crew , (Thucydides), etc. 2. service , (Aristophanes Comicus), etc. (ML)

G9567.strongs_def: to put to sleep :—; Pass. to fall asleep, sleep , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G9569.strongs_def: to look up from under the brows at, glance at, to look askance at, eye suspiciously or angrily , Lat. limis oculis suspicere, (Plato Philosophus); also ὑπ. ἐλεεινά to cast piteous glances , [variant datesAnthology Palantina:—;Pass. to be looked at with suspicion , (Euripides) (ML)

G9571.strongs_def: a garment under a coat of mail , (Plutarch) (ML)

G9573.strongs_def: 1. to burn by applying fire below , (Herdotus Historicus): to offer secret sacrifices , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 2. to light under , (Lucian) (ML)

G9576.strongs_def: 1. to lie under or beneath , (Iliad by Homer); with dative, (Plato Philosophus) 2. in various metaphorically senses, 3. to be put under the eyes or mind, i. e. to be submitted or proposed to one , (Pindar); αἱ ὑποκείμεναι ἐλπίδες one's present hopes, (Demosthenes Orator); ὑπόκειταί μοι ὅτι . . I have laid down the rule , that . ., (Herdotus Historicus) 4. to be laid down or assumed as an hypothesis , (Plato Philosophus), etc.; τούτων ὑποκειμένων = Lat. his positis, (Plato Philosophus); impersonal, ὑπόκειται a rule is laid down , (Demosthenes Orator); ὑποκείσθω ὅτι . . let it be granted that . ., (Aristotle Philosopher) 5. to be suggested , (Herdotus Historicus) 6. to be left at bottom, left remaining , (Thucydides) 7. to be subject to, submit to , τινι (Plato Philosophus): absolute to be submissive , (Plato Philosophus) 8. to be left behind in pledge, to be pledged or mortgaged , τινος for a certain sum, (Demosthenes Orator), etc.; ὑποκείμενοι, of persons, bound for payment of a sum of money, (Demosthenes Orator) 9. to underlie , as a substratum, (Plato Philosophus), etc. 10. to be subordinate , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G9577.strongs_def: ὑπό-λειμμα (WH, -λιμμα, see their App., 154), -τος, τό, [in LXX chiefly for שָׁאַר ;] a remnant: Rom.9:27 (Arist., al.; cf. κατάλειμμα).† (AS)

G9578.strongs_def: 1. left behind, staying behind , (Herdotus Historicus); οἱ ὑπ. those who remained alive , (Herdotus Historicus) 2. of things, ὑπ. τὸ βάραθρον γίγνεται the pit still remains , (Aristophanes Comicus); ὅσα ἦν ὑπ. all that remained to be done , (Thucydides) (ML)

G9580.strongs_def: 1. to loosen beneath or below , ὑπέλυσε γυῖα made his limbs give way under him , (Iliad by Homer):—;Pass., γυῖα ὑπέλυντο (Iliad by Homer) 2. to loose from under the yoke, (Homer):—; to loose from bonds , (Odyssey by Homer); in Mid., τὸν ὑπελύσαο δεσμῶν thou didst free him from bonds by stealth , (Iliad by Homer) 3. to untie a person's sandals from under his feet, take off his shoes, (Aeschulus Tragicus):—;Mid. to take off one's sandals or shoes, or to have them taken off , (Aristophanes Comicus) 4. with accusative pers. to unshoe him, take off his shoes , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G9581.strongs_def: 1. a remembrance, memorial , (Thucydides), etc. 2. a note, memorandum , (Demosthenes Orator):—;in plural memoranda, notes, minutes , Lat. commentarii, (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G9584.strongs_def: to prick or sting underneath : generally, to sting , (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) (ML)

G9585.strongs_def: 1. to fall under or down, to sink in , (Plutarch) 2. to fall down before any one, with accusative, (Plato Philosophus): —;hence, to be subject to him, fall under his power, (Isocrates Orator); of a flatterer, to cringe to , τινί (Demosthenes Orator); with accusative ὑποπεσὼν τὸν δεσπότην (Aristophanes Comicus) 3. to fall behind another, (Demosthenes Orator) 4. to get in under or among , (Thucydides) 5. of accidents, to happen, fall out , (Isocrates Orator) 6. of persons, to fall under a punishment, with dative, (Plutarch) 7. of places, to lie under or below , with dative, (Polybius Historicus) (ML)

G9586.strongs_def: 1. to be suspicious , (Xenophon Historicus); also, ὑπ. εἴς τινα to have suspicions of him, (Thucydides) 2. to suspect, guess, suppose , (Xenophon Historicus) 3. transitive to suspect, hold in suspicion , (Sophocles Tragicus); ὑπ. τινὰ εἴς τι of something, (Herdotus Historicus), etc.:—;Pass. to be suspected, mistrusted , (Thucydides); impersonal, ὡς ὑπωπτεύετο as was generally suspected , (Xenophon Historicus) 4. with accusative pers. et infinitive to suspect that , (Herdotus Historicus), etc. 5. with accusative rei, to look suspiciously on , (Thucydides):—;but also, ὑπ. τι to suspect something, (Euripides) from ὑπόπτης (ML)

G9588.strongs_def: 1. to trip up one's heels, upset , Lat. supplantare, (Demosthenes Orator) 2. metaphorically, ὑπ. καὶ ἀνατρέπων (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G9594.strongs_def: rendering service, serviceable, promoting, conducive to a thing, with dative, (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G9595.strongs_def: a light shewing through a small hole: a narrow opening , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G9597.strongs_def: 1. under the hand, in hand , (Odyssey by Homer) 2. of persons, under any one's hand, under command, subject , τινι (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; λαβεῖν τινα ὑποχείριον to get into one's power , (Euripides); ἔχειν τινὰ ὑπ. (Thucydides) (ML)

G9599.strongs_def: 1. indebted, in debt , (Aristophanes Comicus); ὑπ. τινος his debtor , (Plutarch) 2. of property, involved , Lat. obaeratus, (Demosthenes Orator) 3. with genitive, ὑπ. φιλίας bound by ties of friendship, (Plutarch) (ML)

G9601.strongs_def: to bend oneself back, to carry one's head high , (Aeschines Orator):—;Pass., κάρα ὑπτιάζεται his head lies supine , (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)
G9601.outline_usage: to turn up and open hands

G9602.strongs_def: 1. laid back, laid on one's back , πέσεν ὕπτιος he fell backwards , opposite to πρηνής, (Iliad by Homer); of a quadruped, ὀρθοῦ ἑστεῶτος καὶ ὑπτίου rearing upright and falling backwards , (Herdotus Historicus) 2. generally with the under side uppermost , χείρ ὑπτία the hollow of the hand, (Plutarch); ἐξ ὑπτίου κράνους from the upturned helmet, with the hollow uppermost , (Aeschulus Tragicus); so, παράθες ὑπτίαν τὴν ἀσπίδα); (Aristophanes Comicus); ἀψὶς ὑπτία a half-wheel with the concave side uppermost , (Herdotus Historicus); ὑπτίοις σέλμασιν ναυτίλλεται he sails with the bottom uppermost , i. e. suffers shipwreck, (Sophocles Tragicus); ἐξ ὑπτίας νεῖν to swim on the back (in metaphorically sense), (Plato Philosophus) 3. of land, sloping evenly , of Egypt, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G9605.strongs_def: 1. to weave , ἱστὸν ὑφαίνειν to weave a web, (Homer); ἱμάτιον (Plato Philosophus), etc.:—;absolute to weave, ply the loom , (Herdotus Historicus):—;Mid., ἱμάτιον ὑφαίνεσθαι to weave oneself a cloak, (Plato Philosophus) 2. to contrive, plan, invent , Lat. texere, δόλον ὑφαίνειν (Iliad by Homer); μῆτιν ὑφ. (Odyssey by Homer) 3. generally, to create, construct , (Pindar) (ML)

G9606.strongs_def: 1. to seize underneath or inwardly , (Homer) 2. to draw or take away from under a thing, with genitive, (Iliad by Homer):—;also τὴν χεῖρα ὑφῄρει tried to draw it away , (Aristophanes Comicus) 3. to take away underhand, filch away , (Thucydides); ὑφ. τῆς ὑποψίας gradually to take away part of . ., (Thucydides):—;Pass., ὑπαραιρημένος (ionic perfect participle) put secretly away, made away with , (Herdotus Historicus):—;so in Mid. to take away underhand, filch away, purloin , (Herdotus Historicus), etc. 4. in Mid. also with accusative pers., ὑφ. τινά τινος to rob him of a thing, (Aeschines Orator) (ML)

G9609.strongs_def: 1. in these tenses Causal, to place or set under , τί τινι (Herdotus Historicus); τρεῖς σταυροὺς ὑπίστησι plants three piles in the lake to support a house, (Herdotus Historicus):—;metaphorically, γνώμας ὑποστήσας σοφάς having laid them as a foundation , (Sophocles Tragicus) 2. to post secretly or in ambush , (Herdotus Historicus) 3. Causal also in future and aor1 middle to substitute , τί τινι one thing for another, (Xenophon Historicus) 4. Pass., with aorist2 active ὑπ-έστην, perfect ὑφ-έστηκα, ionic participle ὑπ-εστεώς:—; to stand under as a support , with dative, (Herdotus Historicus) 5. to sink to the bottom, settle , τὸ ὑφιστάμενον the milk, opposite to τὸ ἐφιστάμενον (the cream), (Herdotus Historicus) 6. to place oneself under an engagement, engage or promise to do, with infinitive future, ὅσς᾽ Ἀχιλῆι ὑπέστημεν δώσειν (Iliad by Homer), etc.; with infinitive aorist, οὔ τίς με ὑπέστη σαῶσαι (Iliad by Homer); with infinitive present, (Herdotus Historicus):—;absolute, after promise given , (Odyssey by Homer); ὥσπερ ὑπέστη as he promised , (Thucydides):—;when followed by accusative, an infinitive may be supplied, τρίποδας οὕς οἱ ὑπέστη (i.e. δώσειν); (Iliad by Homer); ἐκτελέουσιν ὑπόσχεσιν ἥνπερ ὑπέσταν (Iliad by Homer) 7. to submit to any one, τινι (Iliad by Homer) 8. with accusative rei, to submit to, consent to , ὁ τὸ ἐλάχιστον ὑπιστάμενος who offers to take the least, (Herdotus Historicus); ὑφ. τὸν πλοῦν to undertake it unwillingly , (Thucydides); so, ὑφ. τὸν κίνδυνον (Thucydides): —;rarely with dative, ὑφ. ξυμφοραῖς ταῖς μεγίσταις (Thucydides) 9. to undertake an office, (Xenophon Historicus) 10. to lie concealed or in ambush , (Herdotus Historicus), etc. 11. to support an attack, to resist, withstand , with dative, (Aeschulus Tragicus); with accusative, (Euripides):—;absolute to stand one's ground, face the enemy , Lat. subsistere, (Euripides) (ML)

G9612.strongs_def: 1. to send rain, to rain , Ζεὺς ὗε (Homer), etc.; ὁ θεὸς ὕει (Herdotus Historicus):—;then, the nom. being omitted, ὕει used impersonal, Lat. pluit, it rains, (Hesiod); ὕοντος when it is raining , (Aristophanes Comicus); ὕοντος πολλῷ as it was raining heavily, (Xenophon Historicus) 2. with accusative loci, ἑπτὰ ἐτέων οὐκ ὗε τὴν Θήρην for seven years it did not rain on Thera, (Herdotus Historicus):—;hence in Pass., with future middle to be rained on , (Odyssey by Homer); ὕσθησαν αἱ Θῆβαι Thebes was rained upon , i. e. it rained there, (Herdotus Historicus); ἡ χώρη ὕεται, i. e. it rains in the country, (Herdotus Historicus) 3. with accusative cognate, ὗσε χρυσόν it rained gold, (Pindar); καινὸν ἀεὶ Ζεὺς ὕει ὕδωρ (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G9613.strongs_def: dusky, dun, gray , Lat. fuscus, (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G9614.strongs_def: lentil , and its fruit , (Herdotus Historicus), etc. (ML)

G9615.strongs_def: baldheaded, bald , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; πρόσωπον φαλακρόν (Euripides) (ML)

G9617.strongs_def: a quiver for arrows, Lat. pharetra, (Homer) (ML)

G9618.strongs_def: 1. to administer a drug , (Plato Philosophus) 2. to use enchantments , φαρμακεύειν τι ἐς τὸν ποταμόν to use it as a charm to calm the river, (Herdotus Historicus) 3. with accusative pers. to drug, give him a poisonous or stupefying drug , (Euripides) (ML)

G9619.strongs_def: φάρμακον, -ου, τό, [in LXX for כֶּשֶׁף ;] __(a) a drug; __(b) an in­cantation, enchantment: Rev.9:21, Tr., mg., WH, txt. (RV, sorceries).† (AS)

G9621.strongs_def: the throat, gullet , (Odyssey by Homer), etc. (ML)

G9623.strongs_def: 1. an apparition, phantom , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; φ. ἀνδρός the spectral appearance of a man, (Herdotus Historicus):—; a vision in a dream, (Aeschulus Tragicus), etc. 2. a sign from heaven, portent, omen , (Herdotus Historicus); periphrastic, φάσμα ταύρου a monster of a bull, (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G9626.strongs_def: to hold cheap, to depreciate, disparage , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G9631.strongs_def: that which is brought by the wife (compare ἕδνον); a dowry, portion , Lat. dos, (Herdotus Historicus); also in plural of a dower , as consisting of divers presents, (Euripides); but, φερναὶ πολέμου, of a wife won in battle, (Euripides):—;in plural, also, bridal gifts , (Euripides) (ML)

G9634.strongs_def: 1. the sound of the voice, a voice , (Pindar), etc.: of a person, ὦ φθέγμ᾽ ἀναιδές, for ὦ φθεγξάμενε ἀναιδῆ, (Sophocles Tragicus) 2. language, speech , (Sophocles Tragicus) 3. a saying, word , (Sophocles Tragicus) 4. of other sounds, as of birds, cries , (Sophocles Tragicus); of a bull, roaring , (Euripides); φθ. θυείας the grinding of the mortar, (Aristophanes Comicus); of the nightingale's song, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G9640.strongs_def: fond of a country life , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G9642.strongs_def: 1. to be fond of strife, engage in eager rivalry, be contentious , φιλονεικῶν out of contentiousness or party spirit , (Thucydides); φ. πρός τινα (Lysias Orator):—;with accusative, φ. τὸ ἐμὲ εἶναι τὸν ἀποκρινόμενον to be eager that I should be the answerer, (Plato Philosophus); τὰ χείρω φ. to be so obstinate as to choose the worst, (Thucydides) 2. in good sense, to struggle emulously , φ. περὶ τῶν καλλίστων (Isocrates Orator) (ML)

G9643.strongs_def: 1. a muzzle , Lat. capistrum, (Lucian) 2. the nose-band of a horse's bridle, fitted with pipes through which the horses' breath made a whistling sound, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 3. a kind of cup , used as a dice-box , Lat. fritillus, (Aeschines Orator) (ML)

G9644.strongs_def: to be heated, inflamed, to fester , φλεγμαίνουσα πόλις, opposite to ὑγιής, (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G9645.strongs_def: 1. transitive to burn, burn up , (Iliad by Homer):—;Pass. to take fire, blaze up , (Iliad by Homer) 2. metaphorically to kindle, inflame with passion, (Sophocles Tragicus):—;Pass., like Lat. uri, to burn with passion, be inflamed, (Sophocles Tragicus) 3. to light up , Ζεὺς βέλος φλέγων making it blaze or flash , (Aeschulus Tragicus); metaphorically, ἄταν οὐρανίαν φλέγων letting the flame of mischief blaze up to heaven, (Sophocles Tragicus):—;Pass. to blaze up, be a-light , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 4. metaphorically to make illustrious or famous , Lat. illustrare, (Pindar):—;Pass. to be or become so , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 5. intransitive to burn, flame, blaze , (Aeschulus Tragicus); of armour, to flash , (Euripides) 6. metaphorically to break forth , of passion, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 7. to shine forth, become famous , (Pindar) (ML)

G9646.strongs_def: 1. a vein , (Iliad by Homer), etc.; φλέβα σχάζειν to open a vein , (Xenophon Historicus) 2. a vein of metal, (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G9647.strongs_def: in plural φλιαί, = σταθμοί, the doorposts, jambs , (Odyssey by Homer); in singular, (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) (ML)

G9653.strongs_def: purple-red, purple or crimson , and (generally) red , Lat. puniceus, (Herdotus Historicus):—;attic contracted φοινι-κοῦς, ᾶ, οῦν, (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G9662.strongs_def: 1. a shuddering, shivering , (Plato Philosophus) 2. shuddering , especially from religious awe, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G9664.strongs_def: that causes shuddering, horrible , (Euripides):—;neuter φρικῶδες, as adverb horribly , (Euripides):—; adverb -δῶς, Sup., φρικωδέστατα ἔχειν to be in utter horror , (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

G9665.strongs_def: 1. thought, care, heed, attention bestowed upon a person or thing, with genitive, φροντίδ᾽ ἔχειν τινός (Euripides); ἐν φροντίδι εἶναι περί τινος (Herdotus Historicus) 2. absolute thought, meditation , (Aeschulus Tragicus); ἐν φροντίδι μοι ἐγένετο [ τὸ πρῆγμα] (Herdotus Historicus); ἐμβῆσαί τινα ἐς φροντίδα to set one a thinking , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.:—;in plural thoughts , αἱ δεύτεραί πως φροντίδες σοφώτεραι (Euripides) 3. deep thought, care, concern , (Aeschulus Tragicus); οὐ φροντὶς Ἱπποκλείδῃ no matter to Hippocleides! (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G9666.strongs_def: 1. a looking out, watch, guard , as a duty, (Herdotus Historicus); φρουρὰν ἄζηλον ὀχήσω shall keep unenviable watch , (Aeschulus Tragicus); φρουρὰ ὄμματος my watchful eye, (Sophocles Tragicus); φρουρᾶς ᾄδειν to sing while on guard , (Aristophanes Comicus) 2. a prison , (Plato Philosophus) 3. of persons, a watch, guard, garrison , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; especially of frontier-posts , which were guarded in Attica by the περίπολοι, (Xenophon Historicus) 4. at Sparta, a body of men destined for service , φρουρὰν φαίνειν (see. φαίνω A. 1. 5). (ML)

G9668.strongs_def: 1. a violent snorting, neighing , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 2. metaphorically wanton behaviour, insolence , [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

G9670.strongs_def: 1. to roast or fry , (Aristophanes Comicus); ἐρετμοῖσι φρύξουσι they shall cook with the [wood of] the oars, (Oracle quoted in Herdotus Historicus):—;Pass., πεφρυγμέναι κριθαί roasted barley, (Thucydides) 2. of the sun, to parch , Lat. torrere, (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) (ML)

G9674.strongs_def: to drive from a country, banish , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G9675.strongs_def: 1. one who flees from his country, a runaway, fugitive, a banished man, exile, refugee , Lat. exul, profugus, (Herdotus Historicus), attic; φυγάδα ποιεῖν τινα (Xenophon Historicus); κατάγειν φυγάδας to recall them; etc. 2. of an army, put to flight , (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G9676.strongs_def: 1. growth, stature , especially fine growth, noble stature , (Homer); Νέστορι εἶδός τε μέγεθός τε φυήν τt ἄγχιστα ἐῴκει he was like Nestor both in shape and size and stature (or growth) , (Iliad by Homer) 2. poetry for φύσις, one's natural powers, nature, genius , (Pindar) 3. the flower or prime of age , (Pindar) (ML)

G9679.strongs_def: 1. the chief of a φυ_λή, a phylarch , (Herdotus Historicus):—;used to translated the Rom. tribunus , (Plutarch) 2. at Athens, the commander of the cavalry furnished by each tribe , see. ἵππαρχος. (ML)

G9681.strongs_def: 1. to mix flour or meal so as to make it into dough, to knead , (Herdotus Historicus); γῆν φυράσειν φόνῳ to make earth into a bloody paste , (Aeschulus Tragicus):—;Pass., οἴνῳ καὶ ἐλαίῳ πεφυραμένα ἄλφιτα (Thucydides) 2. metaphorically, μαλακὴν φωνὴν φυράσασθαι to make up a soft voice, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G9683.strongs_def: 1. to mix something dry with something wet , mostly with a sense of mixing so as to soil or defile , δάκρυσιν εἵματ᾽ ἔφυρον they wetted, sullied their garments with tears, (Iliad by Homer); also with genitive, χείλεα φύρσω αἵματος (Odyssey by Homer):—;Pass., δάκρυσι πεφυρμένη (Iliad by Homer); αἵματι οἶκος ἐφύρθη (Aeschulus Tragicus) 2. of dry things, κόνει φύρουσα κάρα (Euripides); γαίαι πεφύρσεσθαι κόμαν to be doomed to have one's hair defiled with earth, (Pindar) 3. metaphorically to mingle together, confuse , ἔφυρον εἰκῆ πάντα they mixed all things up together, did all at random, (Aeschulus Tragicus), etc.:—;Pass. to be mixed up , ἐκ πεφυρμένου καὶ θηριώδους from a confused and savage state, (Euripides) 4. in Pass. also to mix with others, have dealings with him, (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G9684.strongs_def: 1. transitive to puff or blow up, distend , (Aristophanes Comicus); of bag-pipers, (Aristophanes Comicus); φ. τὰς γνάθους to puff them out , (Demosthenes Orator):—;Pass. to be inflated , ἡ γαστὴρ ἐπεφύσητό μοι (Aristophanes Comicus) 2. metaphorically to puff one up, make him vain , and so to cheat , (Demosthenes Orator):—;Pass. to be puffed up , ἐπί τινι at a thing, (Xenophon Historicus) 3. to blow up, kindle a fire: but also 4. to blow out, extinguish , τὴν λαμπάδα (Aristophanes Comicus) 5. to blow out, spurt out , (Sophocles Tragicus) 6. to blow a wind-instrument, (Euripides) (ML)

G9685.strongs_def: an instrument for blowing, blowpipe or tube , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G9687.strongs_def: 1. that which has grown, a plant, tree , (Iliad by Homer), etc. 2. generally a creature , of men, (Euripides) 3. like ἔρνος, of men, a descendant, child , (Euripides) (ML)

G9688.strongs_def: 1. to search after a thief or theft, search a house , (Aristophanes Comicus) 2. in Pass. to be detected , (Demosthenes Orator); with participle, κλέπτης ὢν φωρᾶσθαι (Demosthenes Orator); so, κακὸς [ ὢν] ἐφωράθη φίλοις (Euripides):—;also of things, ἀργύριον ἐφωράθη ἐξαγόμενον money was discovered to be in course of exportation, (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G9693.strongs_def: 1. a small stone, pebble , in plural, (Lucian), etc. 2. as collect. in singular, gravel, rubble , used in building, (Thucydides); so also in plural, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G9694.strongs_def: 1. a smith's shop, forge, smithy , (Herdotus Historicus) 2. = χαλκίον, a copper, caldron , (Herdotus Historicus) 3. a metal reflector in a lamp, (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G9695.strongs_def: of copper or bronze, brasen , (Homer); χαλκήιος δόμος, = χαλκεῖον, a forge , (Odyssey by Homer); χάλκειον γένος, of the Age of brass , (Hesiod) (ML)

G9696.strongs_def: 1. to make of copper or (generally) of metal, to forge , (Iliad by Homer), etc.:—;Mid. to forge for oneself , (Theognis Elegiacus):—;Pass. to be wrought or forged , (Aristophanes Comicus) 2. absolute to be a smith, work as a smith, ply the hammer , (Aristophanes Comicus); τὸ χαλκεύειν the smith's art , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G9697.strongs_def: the chameleon , a kind of lizard known for changing its colour, (Aristotle Philosopher) (ML)

G9698.strongs_def: 1. chaos , the first stateof the universe, (Hesiod), etc. 2. infinite space, the expanse , (Aristophanes Comicus) 3. the nether abyss, infinite darkness , [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

G9699.strongs_def: perhaps a yellowish bird dwelling in clefts the curlew , (Aristophanes Comicus): χαραδριοῦ βίον ζῆν, of a glutton, (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G9701.strongs_def: to fence by a palisade, fortify , (Aeschines Orator) (ML)

G9703.strongs_def: 1. to make sharp or pointed, sharpen, whet , (Hesiod) 2. to furnish with notches or teeth , like a saw, (Aristotle Philosopher):—;Pass., σκύταλον κεχ. ὄζοις a staff jagged or rugged with branches, (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus): metaphorically, [ ὄμμα] ἠλεμάτοις ἀκτῖσι χαράσσεται sparkles with false lights, of the effect produced by painting the eye-lids, [variant datesAnthology Palantina 3. metaphorically in Pass., κεχαραγμένος τινί exasperated at any one, (Herdotus Historicus); κείνῳ τόδε μὴ χαράσσου be not angry at him for this, (Euripides) 4. to cut into furrows, cut, scratch , (Pindar):—;Pass., κέκοπται καὶ χαράσσεται πέδον (Aeschulus Tragicus) 5. to engrave, inscribe , [Refs 3rd c.BC, variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

G9704.strongs_def: 1. a joy , (Euripides); plural joys, delights , (Euripides) 2. = χάρμα II, joy, delight , (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G9710.strongs_def: 1. of or in winter, of or in winter-time , opposite to θερινός, χ. τροπαί (see. τροπή 1), (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; τὴν χ. (i.e. ὥρην); during the winter season , (Herdotus Historicus) 2. wintry , (Thucydides); see. χειμέριος. (ML)

G9712.strongs_def: 1. a voting or electing by show of hands , (Thucydides) 2. a vote , Lat. suffragium, in plural, (Aeschines Orator) (ML)

G9713.strongs_def: 1. to bring into hand, to manage, master, subdue , (Aristophanes Comicus) 2. mostly in Mid., to conquer, overpower, subdue , (Herdotus Historicus); so, τήνδ᾽ ἐχειρούμην ἄγραν became master of this booty, (Sophocles Tragicus) 3. without any sense of violence, to master, subdue , (Xenophon Historicus), etc. 4. χειροῦμαι is also Pass. to be subdued , [variant datesTragica Adespota; future χειρωθήσομαι (Demosthenes Orator); aor1 ἐχειρώθην (Herdotus Historicus); perfect κεχείρωμαι (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

G9714.strongs_def: 1. the swallow , (Odyssey by Homer), etc.:—; the twittering of the swallow was proverbially used of barbarous tongues by the Greeks, (Aeschulus Tragicus); χελιδόνων μουσεῖα (see. μουσεῖον); proverbs also, μία χελιδὼν ἔαρ οὐ ποιεῖ (Aristotle Philosopher) 2. the frog in a horse's foot , so called from its being forked like the swallow's tail , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G9715.strongs_def: 1. a tortoise , (Homeric Hymns); prov. of insensibility, ἰὼ χελῶναι μακάριαι τοῦ δέρματος oh ye tortoises , happy in your thick skins! (Aristophanes Comicus) 2. like Roman testudo, a pent-house formed of shields overlapping each other like the scales on a tortoise's back , used by storming parties in approaching a city's walls: then, generally, a pent-house for protecting besiegers, (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G9718.strongs_def: on or of dry land , ὄρνιθες χ. land- birds, opposite to λιμναῖοι, (Herdotus Historicus); χ. κροκόδειλος a lizard, (Herdotus Historicus):—;also of landsmen , as opposite to seamen, (Euripides); κῦμα χερσαῖον στρατοῦ, an army, opposite to a fleet, (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

G9719.strongs_def: 1. dry land, land , ἐπὶ χέρσου, opposite to ἐν πόντῳ, (Odyssey by Homer); κύματα κυλινδόμενα προτὶ χέρσον (Odyssey by Homer); κῦμα χέρσῳ ῥηγνύμενον (Iliad by Homer); χέρσῳ on or by land , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 2. as adjective, χέρσος, ον, dry, firm , of land, (Herdotus Historicus); ἐν κονίᾳ χέρσῳ, opposite to πόντῳ, (Pindar) 3. dry, hard, barren , (Herdotus Historicus); χ. λιμήν a harbour left dry , [variant datesAnthology Palantina 4. metaphorically barren, without children , of women, (Sophocles Tragicus): with genitive barren of , πυρὰ χέρσος ἀγλαϊσμάτων (Euripides) Prob. from same Root as ξηρός. (ML)

G9721.strongs_def: 1. Radic. sense, to pour : 2. properly of liquids, to pour out, pour , (Homer), etc.; Zeus χέει ὕδωρ, i. e. he makes it rain, (Iliad by Homer); χέει χιόνα βορέας (Euripides); absolute, χέει it snows , (Iliad by Homer):—;Mid. to pour for oneself , especially of drink-offerings, χοὰς χεόμην νεκύεσσι (Odyssey by Homer), etc.:—;Pass., χέονται κρῆναι they gush forth , (Euripides); χυθέντος ποτοῦ ἐς γῆν (Sophocles Tragicus) 3. χ. δάκρυα to shed tears, (Iliad by Homer):—;Pass., of tears, to pour or gush forth , (Homer); so of blood, to be shed , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 4. in Pass. to become liquid, melt, thaw , (Xenophon Historicus) 5. of solids, to shed, scatter , φύλλα (Iliad by Homer); πτερά (Odyssey by Homer); χ. κόνιν κὰκ κεφαλῆς (Homer); χ. καλάμην χθονί, of a mower or reaper (see. καλάμη), (Iliad by Homer) 6. like χώννυμι, to throw out earth, so as to form a mound, σῆμα, τύμβον χ. (Homer) 7. χ. δοῦρα to pour or shower spears, (Iliad by Homer); Mid., βέλεα χέοντο they showered their arrows, (Iliad by Homer) 8. to let fall or drop , ἡνία (Iliad by Homer); so, χέειν κρόκου βαφὰς (see. βαφή II) (Aeschulus Tragicus); but, καρπὸν χ., of trees, to produce fruit abundantly , (Odyssey by Homer) 9. in Pass. to be thrown or heaped up together , (Homer) 10. in Pass. also of living beings, to pour or stream in a dense mass or throng , (Homer) 11. metaphorically of sounds, to pour forth , φωνήν, αὐδήν (Odyssey by Homer); φθόγγον (Aeschulus Tragicus) 12. of things that obscure the sight, κατ᾽ ὀφθαλμῶν χέεν ἀχλύν shed a dark cloud over the eyes, (Iliad by Homer); πολλὴν ἠέρα χεῦε shed a mist abroad, (Odyssey by Homer):—;Pass., ἀμφὶ δέ οἱ θάνατος χύτο was shed around him, (Iliad by Homer); νόσος κέχυται (Sophocles Tragicus); φρὶξ ἐπὶ πόντον ἐχεύατο (Mid. in passive sense), (Iliad by Homer) 13. of persons, ἀμφ᾽ αὐτῶι χυμένη throwing herself around him, (Homer): so in Mid., ἀμφὶ υἱὸν ἐχεύατο πήχεε (Iliad by Homer) 14. perfect passive κέχυμαι, to be wholly engaged in , Δᾶλος, ἐν ἇι κέχυμαι (Pindar) (ML)

G9722.strongs_def: 1. a horse's hoof , (Hesiod):—;also, a cloven hoof , (Euripides) 2. in plural, of the talons of a bird, [variant datesTragica Adespota; of a wolf's claws , (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) 3. a sea-bank, breakwater , formed of stones laid at the base of a sea-wall, to break the force of the waves (so called because it projected like a hoof) , Lat. crepido, (Thucydides) 4. the spur of a mountain or ridge of rocks answering a like purpose, (Thucydides) 5. a cloven implement , such as a netting-needle;—; compare χηλεύω. (ML)

G9725.strongs_def: 1. intransitive to be bereaved of a person or thing, with genitive, (Odyssey by Homer) 2. absolute to be bereaved of a husband, to be widowed, live in widowhood , (Demosthenes Orator), etc.;—;of a man, to be a widower , (Plutarch); so, χηρεύσει λέχος (Euripides) 3. to live in solitude , of an exile, (Sophocles Tragicus) 4. transitive to bereave , (Euripides) (ML)

G9726.strongs_def: of yesterday , τὸ χθιζὸν χρεῖος their yesterday's debt, (Iliad by Homer); ὁ χθ. πόνος yesterday's labour, (Herdotus Historicus); in adverbial sense, with Verbs, χθιζὸς ἔβη he went yesterday , (Iliad by Homer); χθ. ἤλυθες (Odyssey by Homer), etc.:—;neuter χθιζόν as adverb = χθές, (Homer); so plural χθιζά, see. πρώιζος. (ML)

G9727.strongs_def: 1. the earth, ground , (Homer); χθόνα δῦναι to go beneath the earth , i. e. to die, (Iliad by Homer); κατὰ χθονὸς κρύπτειν τινά (Sophocles Tragicus); κούφα σοι χθὼν ἐπάνω πέσοι (Euripides) 2. of the nether world , οἱ ὑπὸ χθονός, i. e. those in the shades below , Lat. inferi, (Aeschulus Tragicus); κατὰ χθονὸς θεαί, i. e. the Erinyes, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 3. earth , i. e. the whole earth, the world , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 4. Earth , as a goddess, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 5. a particular land or country , of Ithaca, (Odyssey by Homer); of Libya, (Pindar); χθὼν Ἀσιᾶτις, Δωρίς, Ἀργεία, Ἑλλάς, Ἰδαία, etc., [variant datesTragica Adespota (ML)

G9728.strongs_def: unripe wheaten groats , as ἄλφιτα are barley-groats, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G9729.strongs_def: 1. the office or post of χιλίαρχος, (Xenophon Historicus) 2. the office of the tribuni militares , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G9732.strongs_def: 1. a she-goat , Lat. capra, (Iliad by Homer), attic 2. Χίμαιρα, ἡ, Chimaera , a firespouting-monster, with lion's head, serpent's tail, and goat's body, killed by Bellerophon, (Iliad by Homer) (ML)

G9733.strongs_def: 1. a he-goat , Lat. caper, = τράγος, (Aristophanes Comicus) 2. also feminine = χίμαιρα, [Refs 3rd c.BC, variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

G9735.strongs_def: Lat. laena, a large square upper-garment, a cloak, mantle, (Homer); it was made of wool, and worn over the χιτών, thrown over the shoulders, fastened with a pin or brooch περόνη). It is also called φᾶρος by (Homer), and in later Greek ἱμάτιον, Latin pallium. derivation uncertain (ML)

G9741.strongs_def: 1. any light porous substance , ἁλὸς χνόος the foam that gathers at the edge of the sea, (Odyssey by Homer); πωλικὸς χν. horse's foam , [variant datesAnthology Palantina 2. the first down on the chin of youths, Lat. lanugo, (Aristophanes Comicus): the bloom on fruit, [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

G9744.strongs_def: 1. like χόλη, gall, bile , (Iliad by Homer) 2. generally metaphorically bile, gall, bitter anger, wrath , (Homer), attic; χόλος ἔδυ τινά (Iliad by Homer); χόλος ἔμπεσε θυμῷ (Iliad by Homer); χόλον πέσσειν, καταπέσσειν (see. entry); χ. σβέσσαι παῦσαι (Iliad by Homer); χόλου παύεσθαι (Hesiod):—;with genitive objecti, anger towards or because of another, (Iliad by Homer); with genitive rei, anger for, because of a thing, (Sophocles Tragicus) 3. an object of anger , [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

G9746.strongs_def: 1. gut-string, the string of a lyre, Lat. chorda, (Odyssey by Homer) 2. tripe , (Batrachomyomachia): also = χόρδευμα, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G9747.strongs_def: 1. to dance a round or choral dance , (Sophocles Tragicus), etc.; especially of the Bacchic chorus, (Euripides):—; to take part in the chorus , regarded as a matter of religion, (Sophocles Tragicus): to be one of a chorus , (Aristophanes Comicus): —;with dative pers. to dance to him, in his honour , (Euripides) 2. generally, to dance , especially from joy, (Sophocles Tragicus) 3. metaphorically to practise a thing, be versed in it, (Plato Philosophus) 4. with accusative cognate, φροίμιον χορεύσομαι I will dance a prelude (to festivities), (Aeschulus Tragicus); χ. γάμους to celebrate them, (Euripides); ὄργια Μουσῶν (Aristophanes Comicus):—;Mid., χορεύεσθαι δίνας to ply the eddying dance , (Euripides):—;Pass., κεχόρευται ἡμῖν (sings the Chorus) our part is played , (Aristophanes Comicus) 5. transitive to celebrate in choral dance , Ἴακχον (Sophocles Tragicus):—;Pass. to be celebrated in choral dance , (Aristophanes Comicus) 6. Causal, to set one a dancing, to rouse, wake to the dance , τινά (Euripides); so, πόδα χορεύειν [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

G9748.strongs_def: 1. the office of a χορηγός at Athens, the defraying of the cost of the public choruses , being the chief of the λειτουργίαι, (Thucydides), etc. 2. means for providing χοροί: abundance of means, fortune , (Aristotle Philosopher) 3. metaphorically supplies for war , (Polybius Historicus) (ML)

G9749.strongs_def: the membrane that encloses the fetus, the afterbirth , Lat. secundae: plural χόρια, ων, τά, a dish made by stuffing it with honey and milk , a kind of haggis , (Aristophanes Comicus): proverbial, χαλεπὸν χορίω (doric genitive) κύνα γεῦσαι "don't let a dog taste blood, " (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) (cf. Horace, canis a corio nunquam absterrebitur uncto). (ML)

G9751.strongs_def: a being fed, feasting , [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

G9753.strongs_def: a coos, a measurement of liquid (Lev.19.36)

G9754.strongs_def: to neigh, whinny , Lat. hinnire, of horses, (Iliad by Homer), etc. Formed from the sound. (ML)

G9756.strongs_def: 1. that which one needs must pay, an obligation, debt , (Odyssey by Homer); a debt for stolen cattle , (Iliad by Homer); χρεῖος ἀποστήσασθαι to pay a debt in full, (Iliad by Homer); ἀρᾶς τίνει χρ. pays the debt demanded by the curse, (Aeschulus Tragicus); χρέος πόλει προσάπτειν to attach a further debt , i.e. guilt to the city, (Sophocles Tragicus); χρέος ἀποδιδόναι to repay a debt , (Herdotus Historicus):—;in plural debts , χρειῶν λύσις (Hesiod); τὴν οὐσίαν ἅπασαν χρέα κατέλιπε left all the property in outstanding debts , (Demosthenes Orator) 2. a needful business, an affair, matter , ἑὸν αὐτοῦ χρεῖος (Odyssey by Homer): a requirement, a purpose , (Sophocles Tragicus): with genitive, like χάριν, for the sake of , σὸν οὐκ ἔλασσον ἢ κείνης χρέος (Euripides) 3. like χρῆμα, a thing , τί χρέο; = τί χρῆμ; wherefore? (Aeschulus Tragicus); ἐφ᾽ ὅ τι χρ. ἐμόλετ; (Euripides) 4. in (Odyssey by Homer), ἦλθον Τειρεσίαο κατὰ χρέος seems to be = Τειρεσίᾳ χρησόμενος, I came to consult him:—;but, κατὰ χρέος according to what is due , as is meet , (Homeric Hymns) 5. a duty, task, charge, office , (Pindar) (ML)

G9757.strongs_def: to utter oracles, divine , (Aristophanes Comicus) from χρησμολόγος (ML)

G9759.strongs_def: 1. the surface of a body, the skin; the body itself, (Iliad by Homer) 2. the superficial appearance of a thing, its colour , (Aeschulus Tragicus), etc.:—;especially the colour of the skin, the complexion , (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

G9762.strongs_def: 1. one who melts gold , of one who gilds the horns of a victim, (Odyssey by Homer) 2. a goldsmith , (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

G9765.strongs_def: 1. poured, shed , αἷμα χυτόν blood shed , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 2. of dry things, shot out, heaped up , χυτὴ γαῖα a mound of earth, a sepulchral mound, (Homer):—;as Substantive, χυτός, οῦ, = χῶμα, a mound, bank, dike , (Herdotus Historicus) 3. melted , ἀρτήματα λίθινα χυτά pendants of melted stone, (Herdotus Historicus) 4. generally, liquid, flowing , [Refs 5th c.BC, variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

G9766.strongs_def: 1. an earthen pot, a pot for boiling, pipkin , Lat. olla, (Aristophanes Comicus) 2. χύτραι, pots of pulse offered to inferior deities, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G9768.strongs_def: a pot with feet , or a portable stove for putting a pot upon, (Hesiod) (ML)

G9770.strongs_def: to be or go lame , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G9771.strongs_def: 1. earth thrown up, a bank, mound , thrown up against the walls of cities to take them, (Herdotus Historicus):—; a dike to hinder a river from overflowing, (Herdotus Historicus):—; a dam , (Herdotus Historicus):—; a mole or pier , carried out into the sea, Lat. moles, (Herdotus Historicus) 2. like Lat. tumulus, a sepulchral mound, [Refs 5th c.BC, variant datesTragica Adespota (ML)

G9779.strongs_def: 1. to cast into a mould ( χόανος), (Aristophanes Comicus) 2. to cast metal: —;Pass., κεχωνευμένος (Plutarch) (ML)

G9782.strongs_def: 1. a pair of scissors , Lat. forfex, [variant datesAnthology Palantina 2. a building with a pointed stone roof, a vault , Lat. fornix, (Sophocles Tragicus) Deriv. unknown. (ML)

G9785.strongs_def: to sing along with stringed instruments
G9785.outline_usage: to sing along with stringed instruments

G9787.strongs_def: like a starling , i. e. speckled, dappled , ψ. ἵππος a dapple-gray horse, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G9789.strongs_def: to falter in speech, speak inarticulately :—;so in Mid., (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G9793.strongs_def: a proposition carried by vote : especially a measure passed in the ἐκκλησία, a decree , (Aristophanes Comicus); τὸ Μεγαρέων ψ. the decree concerning them, (Thucydides); so, περὶ Μεγαρέων ψ. (Thucydides); ψ. γράφειν to bring in a decree , (Aristophanes Comicus); ψ. ἐπιψηφίζειν, of the πρόεδροι, to put it to the vote, (Aeschines Orator); ψ. νικᾶν to carry it , (Aeschines Orator); ψ. καθαιρεῖν to rescind it , Lat. abrogare, (Thucydides) (ML)

G9794.strongs_def: to whisper, say into the ear , (Plato Philosophus):—;metaphorically, ὅταν πλάτανος πτελέᾳ ψιθυρίζῃ when the plane whispers to the elm, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G9795.strongs_def: 1. bare , 2. of land, ψιλὴ ἄροσις a bare corn-field, (Iliad by Homer); πεδίον μέγα τε καὶ ψιλόν (Herdotus Historicus): with genitive, γῆ ψιλὴ δενδρέων land bare of trees, (Herdotus Historicus):—; ψιλὴ γεωργία the tillage of land for corn , opposite to γ. πεφυτευμένη (for vines and olives) , (Aristotle Philosopher) 3. of animals, stript of hair or feathers, bare, smooth , δέρμα (Odyssey by Homer); ἶβις ψιλὴ κεφαλήν bald on the head, (Herdotus Historicus) 4. generally, bare, uncovered , ψιλὸν ὡς ὁρᾷ νέκυν (Sophocles Tragicus):—;with genitive bare of, separated from , ψιλὴ σώματος οὖσα [ ἡ ψυχή] (Plato Philosophus) b. bare, stript of appendages , ψιλὴ τρόπις the bare keel with the planks torn from it, (Odyssey by Homer); ψ. θρίδαξ a lettuce with the side-leaves pulled off , (Herdotus Historicus); ψ. μάχαιραι swords without other arms , (Xenophon Historicus) 5. οἱ ψιλοί (i.e. τῶν ὅπλων); soldiers without heavy armour, light troops , such as archers and slingers, opposite to ὁπλῖται, (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; τὸ ψιλόν, opposite to τὸ ὁπλιτικόν, (Xenophon Historicus); ψ. ἔχων τὴν κεφαλήν bare-headed, without helmet , (Xenophon Historicus) 6. ψιλὸς λόγος bare language, i. e. prose , as opposite to poetry which is clothed in metre, (Plato Philosophus); also, ψ. λόγος is a mere speech, a speech unsupported by evidence , (Demosthenes Orator) 7. ψιλὴ ποίησις mere poetry, without music , i. e. epic poetry, as opposite to lyric , (Plato Philosophus):—;but, ψιλὴ μουσική instrumental music unaccompanied by the voice , (Aristotle Philosopher) 8. Oedipus seems to call Antigone his ψιλὸν ὄμμα, as being the one poor eye left him, (Sophocles Tragicus) 9. adverb ψιλῶς, merely, only , (Plutarch) (ML)

G9796.strongs_def: 1. to strip bare of hair, (Herdotus Historicus):—; Pass. to become bald , (Hesiod): generally, to be laid bare , (Xenophon Historicus) 2. with genitive to strip bare of, to strip of a thing, (Herdotus Historicus) 3. generally, to leave naked, unarmed or defenceless , (Thucydides) 4. Pass. also of things, to be stripped off something, τὰ κρέα ἐψιλωμένα τῶν ὀστέων (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G9798.strongs_def: 1. a blamable fault, a blemish, flaw , (Simonides Lyricus) 2. blame, censure , (Pindar) (ML)

G9799.strongs_def: 1. to make an inarticulate noise, to sound, make a noise , (Euripides); ψοφεῖ λάλον τι sounds chatter-like , as if it were tested like a pot, to see if it were cracked, (Aristophanes Comicus); ὥσπερ κύμβαλον ψοφεῖ (Xenophon Historicus) 2. with accusative, ψοφεῖν τὰς θύρας to knock at the door inside, to shew that some one was coming out, Menand.:—;also of the door (intransitive), εἰ αἱ θύραι νύκτωρ ψοφοῖεν, i. e. if they were heard to open , (Lysias Orator) (ML)

G9800.strongs_def: 1. any inarticulate sound, a sound, noise , (Homer), etc.; of musical instruments, ψ. λωτοῦ, κιθάρας (Euripides) 2. a mere sound, empty sound, noise , (Sophocles Tragicus); ψόφου πλέως, of Aeschylus, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G21228.strongs_def: 1. a tool, implement :—;mostly in plural τεύχεα, 2. implements of war, armour, arms, harness , (Homer);—;so τεύχη in [variant datesTragica Adespota 3. in plural, also, the gear of a ship, tackle , (Odyssey by Homer) 4. in singular a vessel of any kind, a bathing-tub , (Aeschulus Tragicus); a cinerary urn , (Aeschulus Tragicus); a balloting-urn , (Aeschulus Tragicus); a vase for libations , (Aeschulus Tragicus); a vase or ewer for water, (Euripides); a pot or jar , (Xenophon Historicus); ξύλινα τ. chests , (Xenophon Historicus) 5. the human frame, body , (Aristotle Philosopher) 6. a book , [variant datesAnthology Palantina; hence πεντάτευχος, the Pentateuch. (ML)

G21235.strongs_def: 1. to shake or brandish a weapon or shield, (Iliad by Homer), etc. 2. generally, to shake , τ. γαῖαν, of Poseidon, (Iliad by Homer); θρόνον ἐτίναξε upset the seat, (Odyssey by Homer): of wind, to scatter , (Odyssey by Homer):—;Mid., τιναξάσθην πτερά they shook their wings, (Odyssey by Homer):—;Pass., ἐτινάσσετο Ὄλυμπος shook or quaked , (Hesiod) (ML)

G21237.strongs_def: properly, to wind off wool into a clew for spinning: metaphorically to wind off, achieve, accomplish , ἐγὼ δὲ δόλους τολυπεύω, of Penelope's web (where there is a play on the literal sense), (Odyssey by Homer); τ. πόλεμον (Homer) from τολύπη (ML)

G21238.strongs_def: cutting , ἕστηκεν ᾗ τομώτατος is placed as it will cut sharpest , (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G21239.strongs_def: 1. of or for the bow , (Aeschulus Tragicus):—; ἡ τοξική (i.e. τέχνη); archery , (Plato Philosophus) 2. of persons, skilled in the use of the bow , τοξικώτατος (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G21242.strongs_def: to wage war by holding strong positions , (Plutarch) (ML)

G21245.strongs_def: the third wave, a huge wave , for the third was supposed to be the largest (as in Lat. the fluctus decumanus) , (Plato Philosophus):—;metaphorically, τρ. κακῶν (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

G21246.strongs_def: 1. a meeting of three roads , Lat. trivium, (Theognis Elegiacus), etc. 2. Hecate, Lat. Trivia, ἁ θεὸς ἐν τριόδοισι (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus); οἷος ἐκ τριόδου i. e. vulgar, (Lucian) (ML)

G21247.strongs_def: 1. thrice as many, thrice as much, thrice as great as , with genitive, (Aristophanes Comicus), etc.: —;absolute, τριπλασίαν δύναμιν εἶχε (i.e. τῆς προτέρας); (Xenophon Historicus) 2. τριπλάσιον as adverb, τριπλάσιον thrice as much , (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G21252.strongs_def: 1. to tremble, quake, quiver , especially from fear, (Iliad by Homer):—;with infinitive to fear to do, (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) 2. with accusative to tremble before or at a person, to stand in awe of , (Homer) In each sense (Homer) uses both Act. and Mid., but only in present and imperfect; epic and ionic τρομεοίατο for τρομέοιντο, (Iliad by Homer); ionic participle τρομεύμενος (Solon Lyricus) (ML)

G21268.strongs_def: cutting or felling wood , (Iliad by Homer):—; as Substantive ὑλοτόμος, a wood-cutter, woodman , (Iliad by Homer) (ML)

G21275.strongs_def: Dep.:—; to leap over or beyond , with genitive, (Iliad by Homer); also with accusative, (Iliad by Homer); so (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G21284.strongs_def: being above , (Plutarch) From ὑπέ; -ῷος being a term., as πατρῴος, μητρῴος from πατήρ, μήτηρ. (ML)

G21286.strongs_def: 1. that which is placed under, a foundation, hypothesis, supposition , Lat. assumptio, (Plato Philosophus) 2. the subject under discussion, the question , (Xenophon Historicus), etc. 3. that which is laid down as a rule of action, a principle , (Demosthenes Orator): generally, a purpose, plan, design , (Plato Philosophus) 4. a cause, pretext , (Plutarch) (ML)

G21288.strongs_def: 1. a taking up , especially a taking up the word, taking up the matter where another leaves off, (Plato Philosophus):—; a rejoinder, reply , (Isocrates Orator) 2. a taking in a certain sense, an assumption, conception , (Demosthenes Orator) 3. a hasty judgment, suspicion , (Lucian) (ML)

G21305.strongs_def: 1. a sparing , νεκύων (Iliad by Homer) 2. absolute thrift, parsimony , (Odyssey by Homer): thrift in exposing oneself to danger, (Thucydides) (ML)

G21309.strongs_def: love of rule, lust of power , (Theophrastus Philosophus) (ML)

G21312.strongs_def: fond of women , plural φιλογύναικες (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G21315.strongs_def: loving one's life, cowardly, dastardly, faint-hearted , (Euripides) (ML)

G21322.strongs_def: 1. to make wise, instruct, inform, teach , τινά [variant datesTragica Adespota, (Xenophon Historicus); φρενώσω δ᾽ οὐκέτ᾽ ἐξ αἰνιγμάτων, i. e. will teach plainly, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 2. in Pass. to be elated , (Babrius Fabularum Scriptor) (ML)

G21333.strongs_def: 1. glad-eyed, bright-eyed , χαροποὶ λέοντες (Odyssey by Homer); θῆρες (Sophocles Tragicus):—;later, it denoted light-blue or grayish colour , ὄμματά μοι γλαυκᾶς χαροπώτερα πολλὸν Ἀθάνας (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus); also of the Germans, see. χαροπότης. 2. of the eyes of youths, sparkling with joy, joyous, gladsome , [Refs 3rd c.BC, variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

G21335.strongs_def: a plug in a ship's bottom , drawn out when the ship was brought on land, to let out the bilge-water, (Hesiod) (ML)

G21343.strongs_def: 1. to cast into a mould χοάνος); (Aristophanes Comicus) 2. to cast metal:—;Pass., κεχωνευμένος (Plutarch) from χοάνη (ML)

G21347.strongs_def: a place for transacting business, a counting-house , (Plutarch) (ML)

G21348.strongs_def: to be useful or serviceable , τινί to one, (Lucian) (ML)

G21352.strongs_def: juice , especially juice produced by decoction or digestion :—;metaphorically, χυλὸν διδοὺς στωμυλμάτων administering a decoction of small talk, (Aristophanes Comicus); χ. φιλίας (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G21355.strongs_def: 1. sand , so called from its loose, crumbling nature (from ψάω); (Odyssey by Homer), etc.:—;proverbial, ψάμμος ἀριθμὸν περιπέφευγεν (Pindar) 2. ἡ ψ. the sandy desert of Libya, (Herdotus Historicus) Both ψάμμος and ψάμαθος sometimes drop ψ and become ἄμμος, ἄμαθος. (ML)

G21357.strongs_def: 1. to touch lightly, rub ; 2. intransitive to crumble away, vanish, disappear , (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G21361.strongs_def: 1. whispering: slanderous , (Sophocles Tragicus) 2. as Substantive, ψίθυρος, = ψιθυριστής, a whisperer, slanderer , (Pindar) 3. twittering , of birds, [variant datesAnthology Palantina Perh. formed from the sound. (ML)

G21363.strongs_def: a winning of souls, persuasion , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G21364.strongs_def: to be at the last gasp

G21365.strongs_def: 1. the pangs or throes of labour, travail-pains , (Iliad by Homer); ἐν μόναις ὠδῖσιν at a single birth , (Pindar); ἐν ὠδίνων ἀνάγκαις (Euripides); in singular travail-pain, anguish , (Pindar) 2. in singular, also, the fruit of travail or labour, a birth, child , (Aeschulus Tragicus); ἄπτερον ὠδῖνα τέκνων, of young birds, (Euripides) 3. metaphorically any travail, anguish , (Aeschulus Tragicus); also in plural, of love, pangs , (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)
